core_meaning_summary: To utter words, state, command, think, or be spoken of, typically introducing direct speech or expressing an internal thought or directive.

senses.definition: To produce spoken words in communication, whether making a statement, answering, asking, or pronouncing a prophetic message, usually followed directly by the quoted words.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), finite or participial, alone or with אֶל / לְ + addressee, followed by direct speech

senses.definition: To introduce the quoted words of a preceding verb of speaking, telling, calling, or sending a message, functioning as a quotative marker.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), infinitive construct with prefixed לְ (לֵאמֹר) following another verb of communication or sending

senses.definition: To issue an order, give a directive, or state a binding promise or intention regarding an action to be carried out.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), with אֲשֶׁר + imperfect, with לְ + infinitive construct, with an imperative quote, or absolute before resulting action

senses.definition: To hold or express an inner conviction, claim, or resolve within oneself, often equivalent to thinking or supposing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), introducing an assertion or inner resolve (including negated prohibition with אַל)

senses.definition: To be spoken of, designated, or addressed by a descriptive name or characterization.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive stem (Niphal), imperfect + לְ + addressee/referent + predicate designation

collocations_and_notes: Frequently introduces direct discourse with the addressee marked by the prepositions אֶל (ʾel) or לְ (lĕ), or without an explicit addressee. Commonly appears in the prophetic messenger formula כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה (JER 14:15; JER 28:11; JER 38:3; EZK 21:8; AMO 1:11; ZEC 1:17), in the revelation formula וַיְהִי דְבַר־יְהוָה אֵלַי לֵאמֹר (EZK 6:1; EZK 35:1), and in dialogue sequences with wayyiqtol forms (JDG 17:9; 2SA 1:3; 1KI 18:43; 2KI 2:2). The infinitive construct לֵאמֹר is grammaticalized as a speech-introducing particle after verbs such as דִּבֶּר (LEV 10:3; NUM 27:8), שָׁלַח (JOS 10:6; 2SA 13:7), הִגִּיד (2SA 19:9), and קָרָא (ZEC 1:17). Contrastive parallel with חָשַׁב (JOB 35:2) and יִקָּרֵא (ISA 62:4).

core_meaning_summary: The primary negative adverb used to negate verbs, clauses, prohibitions, non-verbal constituents, and negative questions or oaths.

senses.definition: Negates an action, event, state, or capability expressed by a finite verb across past, present, future, or general assertions, as well as in subordinate causal, relative, conditional, or negative-purpose clauses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negative adverb immediately preceding a finite verb (perfect or imperfect)

senses.definition: Expresses a binding, categorical, or lasting prohibition when paired with an imperfect verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negative adverb preceding an imperfect verb in legal, ritual, or instructional discourse

senses.definition: Negates a specific non-verbal phrase, adjective, participle, noun, or prepositional phrase, including the combination בְּלֹא indicating absence ('without').
senses.grammatical_frame: Negative adverb preceding a noun, adjective, participle, or prepositional phrase (or following בְּ)

senses.definition: Functions in rhetorical negative questions expecting an affirmative response, or within אִם ... לֹא constructions to frame a solemn oath, pledge, or judicial denial.
senses.grammatical_frame: Combined with interrogative הֲ (הֲלֹא / הַ... לֹא) or conditional אִם (אִם לֹא)

collocations_and_notes: Commonly precedes finite verbs directly; combines with prepositions (e.g., בְּלֹא 'without'), interrogative הֲ (הֲלֹא expecting an affirmative answer), and conditional אִם (אִם לֹא in conditional clauses or solemn oaths). In legal and prophetic instructions with an imperfect verb, it expresses enduring prohibition.

core_meaning_summary: A male child or descendant, extended to tribal or ancestral members, members of a human group, guild, or locality, young animals, and expressions of age.

senses.definition: A direct male offspring of human parents; used in patronymics to identify a person by their father, and in the plural sometimes encompassing children borne by a mother generally.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural; absolute, with possessive suffixes, or construct before a parent's name

senses.definition: A male or collective descendant traced through earlier generations, or a member of a tribe, clan, or ancestral family named after an ancestor or ancestress.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular in multi-generational chains or construct plural (בְּנֵי) before an eponymous ancestor or clan name

senses.definition: An individual standing in a covenantal or adoptive father-son relationship of loyalty, authority, and protection, used of a king in relation to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular after preposition לְ in parallel with אָב ('father')

senses.definition: A member or representative of a broader category, such as humankind, a professional or religious guild, or the inhabitants of a city or nation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, construct singular or plural before a generic noun (אָדָם), occupational group, or place name

senses.definition: The young offspring of an animal species, specifically young cattle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, construct singular or plural before an animal collective noun (בָּקָר)

senses.definition: A person characterized as having lived a specified number of years, forming the standard idiom for stating age.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, construct singular before a numeral and שָׁנִים ('years')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in construct forms (בֶּן־ / בְּנֵי־) to mark patronymic lineage (e.g., X בֶּן־Y), tribal or clan identity (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, בְּנֵי דָן), human classification (בֶּן־אָדָם / בְּנֵי הָאָדָם), vocational or social guilds (בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים, בְּנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים), animal youth (בְּנֵי בָקָר), and age expressions (בֶּן שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים). Also appears paired with בַּת ('daughter') or אָב ('father') in kinship and inheritance contexts.

core_meaning_summary: A multi-purpose subordinating and coordinating conjunction that introduces causal explanations, clausal complements of perception or speech, temporal or conditional circumstances, and contrastive or exceptive qualifications.

senses.definition: Introduces a clause providing the reason, basis, ground, or motivation for a preceding statement, command, warning, or praise.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction introducing a causal or explanatory finite clause

senses.definition: Introduces a direct or indirect content clause serving as the object or explanation of verbs of seeing, knowing, hearing, or proclaiming.
senses.grammatical_frame: Complementizer following verbs of perception, cognition, or speech (`רָאָה`, `יָדַע`, `שָׁמַע`, `קָרָא`) + finite clause

senses.definition: Introduces a temporal or conditional circumstance under which an action occurs, a point up to which something continues (`עַד כִּי`), or a consequence following a rhetorical question.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction introducing a temporal or conditional protasis (often after `וַיְהִי` / `וְהָיָה` or after `עַד`)

senses.definition: Expresses contrast, restriction, exception, or scalar comparison in combination with preceding particles or negatives, including `לֹא ... כִּי` ("no, rather"), `כִּי אִם` ("unless / except"), `אֶפֶס כִּי` ("however"), and `אַף כִּי` ("how much less / more").
senses.grammatical_frame: Adversative or compound particle following a negation (`לֹא`, `אִם`) or paired with `אִם`, `אֶפֶס`, or `אַף`

collocations_and_notes: Combines in several fixed multi-word expressions observed in the packet: `עַד כִּי` ("until"), `כִּי אִם` ("except / unless" after a negative oath), `לֹא ... כִּי` ("no, rather"), `אֶפֶס כִּי` ("however / yet"), and `אַף כִּי` ("how much less / more"). Frequently introduces object clauses after `רָאָה` ("see"), `יָדַע` ("know"), and `שָׁמַע` ("hear"), or temporal clauses after `וַיְהִי` / `וְהָיָה`.

core_meaning_summary: To exist, be in a state or condition, come into being, become something, or mark the unfolding of an event in narrative or future discourse.

senses.definition: To exist, be present, arise, or take place as an entity, event, or message, frequently negated with `לֹא` or `אַל` to express absence or non-occurrence, or paired with `אֶל` when a divine word comes to a prophet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal); intransitive with subject noun, often with locative phrase or `אֶל` + recipient

senses.definition: To hold a quality, condition, identity, likeness, or measured quantity, linking a subject to a nominal, adjectival, construct, or comparative predicate.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal); copular verb + subject + predicate noun, adjective, numeral, or `כְּ` simile phrase

senses.definition: To transition into a new status, function, or role, or to serve as something for someone, typically marking the resulting status or role with the preposition `לְ`.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), finite or infinitive construct + `לְ` + predicate noun (sometimes also with `לְ` + person)

senses.definition: To stand in a spatial, relational, or possessive connection with someone or a place, including belonging to someone (`לְ`), accompanying or supporting (`עִם`), resting upon (`עַל`), or staying in a location (`שָׁם`).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), finite or infinitive construct + prepositional phrase (`לְ`, `עִם`, `עַל`) or locative adverb + duration

senses.definition: To function as a temporal or discourse-opening marker at the start of a clause, introducing a circumstance, timeframe, or subsequent event in past narrative (`וַיְהִי`) or future announcement (`וְהָיָה`).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) 3rd masculine singular consecutive (`וַיְהִי` / `וְהָיָה`) + temporal phrase, `כְּ` + infinitive, or following clause

collocations_and_notes: Only basic active (Qal) finite, volitive, consecutive, and infinitive forms appear in the sampled verses; no derived stems occur in this packet. Frequently forms fixed relational or discourse patterns: `הָיָה לְ` (possession or becoming/serving as), `הָיָה עִם` (accompaniment/support), `הָיָה עַל` (a spirit coming upon someone), `הָיָה דְבַר יהוה אֶל` (a prophetic word coming to someone), and clause-initial `וַיְהִי` / `וְהָיָה` marking narrative transitions or future events.

core_meaning_summary: A proclitic preposition and conjunction-forming prefix expressing similarity or comparison ('like, as'), conformity to a norm or standard ('according to'), or temporal coincidence ('when, as soon as').

senses.definition: Marks an entity, quality, demonstrative, or verbal event as the standard of resemblance or simile for another entity or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic prefix attached to nouns, demonstratives (כָּזֹאת, כָּאֵלֶּה), or an infinitive construct (ISA 64:1) introducing a comparison

senses.definition: Indicates conformity, correspondence, or measure relative to a command, pattern, precedent, or standard.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic prefix on nouns of rule/pattern (e.g., מִצְוָה, מַעֲשֶׂה, דְּמוּת, כֹּל, פִּי) or forming the conjunction כַּאֲשֶׁר ('just as / according as'), often paired with כֵּן ('so')

senses.definition: Marks the point in time or immediate circumstance at which an action occurs, or compares a situation to an earlier period of time; with מְעַט it denotes brief temporal proximity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic prefix attached to an infinitive construct, to אֲשֶׁר (כַּאֲשֶׁר + finite verb), to time nouns (יוֹם, יָמִים), or to מְעַט (כִּמְעַט)

collocations_and_notes: Attaches directly as a proclitic prefix to nouns, demonstratives (כָּזֹאת, כָּאֵלֶּה), infinitives construct, and the relative word אֲשֶׁר (forming the conjunction כַּאֲשֶׁר). Frequently paired in correlative constructions with כֵּן ('just as ... so', JOS 10:1; JOL 2:4). Specialized collocations include כְּפִי ('according to the command/word of', 1CH 12:24) and כִּמְעַט ('scarcely / just after', SNG 3:4). Notice that כְּ with an infinitive construct expresses either temporal sequence ('when / as soon as', JOS 10:1; 1SA 24:17; 2SA 17:9; NEH 9:28) or vivid comparison ('like when', ISA 64:1).

core_meaning_summary: To make, fashion, perform, carry out, or act toward someone or something across physical fabrication, moral/legal conduct, interpersonal treatment, ritual preparation, and productivity.

senses.definition: Create, construct, or craft physical objects, structures, cultic furnishings, or the heavens and the earth, sometimes specifying both the object and the material or pattern in a double-object construction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) stem; transitive with direct object (frequently marked by אֵת), occasionally taking a second object indicating material or form

senses.definition: Perform, carry out, practice, or commit actions, tasks, commands, statutes, or moral/immoral deeds, or act decisively without an expressed object.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) stem; transitive with task, command, or deed as object, or intransitive/absolute (e.g., 'take action'); frequently preceded by שָׁמַר ('keep/observe') or modified by כְּ / כַּאֲשֶׁר ('according to')

senses.definition: Act toward, treat, or deal with a person or group, whether by showing loyalty and kindness, intervening to protect from harm, or executing justice, judgment, and disaster.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) stem; with recipient marked by לְ ('to/for'), עִם ('with'), בְּ ('against/upon'), or direct object marker אֵת/אוֹת-, often alongside an abstract noun such as חֶסֶד ('loyalty'), מִשְׁפָּט ('justice'), or רָעָה ('harm')

senses.definition: Prepare and offer a sacrificial animal or observe and celebrate an appointed religious festival.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) stem; transitive with sacrificial animal or festival (חַג) as direct object

senses.definition: Produce agricultural yield or acquire and accumulate livestock and property.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) stem; transitive with produce (קֶמַח) or possessions (מִקְנֶה וְקִנְיָן) as direct object, or absolute

senses.definition: Perform miraculous signs before witnesses, or appoint and establish human leaders to carry out a divine deliverance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) stem; transitive with direct object (אֶת + personal name or הָאֹתוֹת)

collocations_and_notes: All 40 sampled occurrences appear in the basic active (Qal) stem; no passive, intensive, or causative stems appear in this evidence packet. Frequent collocations include כַּאֲשֶׁר ... כֵּן ('just as ... so did', EXO 12:50; NUM 8:20; JDG 8:8; JER 50:15), שָׁמַר לַעֲשׂוֹת ('be careful to carry out', DEU 17:10; DEU 32:46), עָשָׂה חֶסֶד עִם ('show loyalty/kindness toward', GEN 20:13; 2SA 3:8; JOB 10:12), הַטּוֹב בְּעֵינֶיךָ ('what is good in your eyes', 2SA 19:39; 2KI 10:5), עָשָׂה מִשְׁפָּט / שְׁפָטִים ('execute justice/judgments', 1KI 8:49; EZK 16:41), and מַעֲשֵׂה ('workmanship of', EXO 26:1; EXO 39:15). Note also the protective idiom עָשָׂה מֵרָעָה ('act to keep from harm', 1CH 4:10).

core_meaning_summary: Deity: predominantly the one supreme God and creator worshipped by Israel, and also used of a deity in personal/national relationship, other/foreign deities, or adjudicating authorities in a legal dispute.

senses.definition: The supreme creator and sovereign deity, often with the definite article or as subject of singular verbs and in direct prayer address.
senses.grammatical_frame: Absolute noun (with or without definite article) governing singular verbs and pronouns, or vocative

senses.definition: The deity worshipped by, allied with, or belonging to a specific people, ancestor, or individual, frequently standing in apposition to the divine name YHWH or in construct chains.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct state or with possessive pronominal suffix, often in apposition to YHWH

senses.definition: Deities other than Israel's God, either as a plural group of foreign/rival deities or as the patron deity of a foreign ruler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Modified by plural adjective/pronoun (e.g., ʾăḥērîm, lāhem) or construct with foreign ruler's suffix

senses.definition: The adjudicating authority before whom disputed property and theft cases are brought for a binding verdict, whether human judicial officials or divine judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: With definite article or bare noun as subject of a plural verb in a legal procedure

collocations_and_notes: Grammatically plural in form, but when referring to the supreme God of Israel it regularly governs singular verbs and pronouns and stands in apposition to the divine name YHWH (e.g., YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl, YHWH ʾĕlōhê ṣəbāʾôt, YHWH ʾĕlōhêkā). Frequently appears in construct phrases such as bêt hāʾĕlōhîm ('house of God'), ʾărôn hāʾĕlōhîm ('ark of God'), and the prophetic title ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm ('man of God'). When modified by plural adjectives or pronouns (ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm, lāhem), it designates plural foreign deities. In EXO 22:8 it takes a plural verb (yaršîʿun) in a legal adjudication context, leaving open whether the text envisions human judges/magistrates acting as legal authorities or a divine tribunal.

core_meaning_summary: In the simple active stem, to move toward and arrive at a place, person, or state, or to enter into a space, relationship, or time; in the causative stem, to cause someone or something to come, i.e., to bring or usher in.

senses.definition: To move through space toward a person or destination and arrive there; used both of reaching a goal and of traveling toward one.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intransitive with directional accusative, ʾel, ʿad, min, or adverbial location

senses.definition: To pass into a bounded physical space, territory, or collective event/commitment such as a house, city, sea, temple courts, battle, or covenant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) with bə-, ʾel, lə-, or direct location noun

senses.definition: To go in to a partner for sexual relations, or to enter a ruler's private quarters for a royal audience/union.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) with ʾel + person (woman or king)

senses.definition: Of the sun, to sink below the horizon at the close of day.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) infinitive construct with subject haššemeš ('the sun')

senses.definition: Of time periods, impending events, or hardships (such as days, disaster, distress, or military attack), to arrive, occur, or come upon someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) with inanimate or abstract subject, often with ʿal ('upon') or participle formula hinnēh yāmîm bāʾîm

senses.definition: To cause a person, animal, or object to come to a place or recipient; to lead, transport, or present something such as offerings, tribute, captives, or provisions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object and optional ʾel or accusative goal

senses.definition: To cause an abstract condition or moral reality (such as enduring righteousness) to arrive or take effect.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with abstract noun object

collocations_and_notes: Commonly takes directional prepositions such as ʾel ('to, into'), bə- ('into'), lə- ('to'), ʿad ('as far as'), min ('from'), and accusative destination nouns (including directional -āh endings like bəʾērāh šābaʿ and taršîšāh). Frequently paired with šûb ('return'), hālak ('walk/go'), qābaṣ ('gather'), and yāraš ('possess'). Notable idiomatic patterns include bôʾ haššemeš ('the going down of the sun', i.e., sunset), yāmîm bāʾîm ('days are coming', prophetic future formula), bôʾ ʾel ('go in to' a woman in sexual/marital union or into a king's presence), and bôʾ babbərît ('enter into the covenant'). In the simple active stem it denotes self-initiated arrival or entry; in the causative stem it denotes bringing or leading someone or something to a goal or causing an abstract condition to arrive.

core_meaning_summary: Masculine noun denoting a sovereign monarch ruling over a city, people, or kingdom, and by extension applied to God as Israel's royal sovereign.

senses.definition: A male sovereign ruler holding supreme political, judicial, and military authority over a city-state, people, nation, or empire.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular (מֶלֶךְ) or plural (מְלָכִים / מַלְכֵי), definite or indefinite, frequently in construct before a territory, city, or people, in apposition to a personal name, or governed by לְ to mark royal office ('as king')

senses.definition: A royal sovereign title or concept applied in poetic parallelism to Israel's God as the king present among the people and greeted with royal acclamation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular indefinite noun (מֶלֶךְ) serving as nomen rectum in construct (תְּרוּעַת מֶלֶךְ) in parallel with יְהוָה אֱלֹהָיו ('YHWH his God')

collocations_and_notes: Appears both with the definite article alone (הַמֶּלֶךְ 'the king') and in apposition before or after a personal name (הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה, 1KI 10:16; פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם, 1KI 3:1). Frequently heads construct chains specifying the ruled realm, city, or people (e.g., מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל, 1KI 22:4; מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל, JER 21:4; מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר, ISA 36:18; מַלְכֵי אָרֶץ, EZK 27:33), and once links via לְ to a city (מֶלֶךְ לָעִיר סְפַרְוָיִם, 2KI 19:13). Polite courtly address uses אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ ('my lord the king', 1SA 26:19; 2SA 14:22; 1KI 1:20; 1CH 21:23). Related institutional phrases include בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ ('the king's house/palace', 2CH 9:11), בֶּן הַמֶּלֶךְ ('the king's son', 2SA 18:20), כִּסֵּא הַמֶּלֶךְ ('the throne of the king', 1KI 1:20), and דְּבַר הַמֶּלֶךְ וְדָתוֹ ('the king's decree and his law', EST 9:1). In NUM 23:21, the poetic parallel between יְהוָה אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ and וּתְרוּעַת מֶלֶךְ בּוֹ associates kingship and royal acclamation with Israel's God.

core_meaning_summary: Feminine noun denoting the physical earth or world as a whole, a specific country or territory, the inhabitants of the earth, or the ground underfoot.

senses.definition: The physical world or terrestrial realm as a whole, often contrasted with the sky or heavens as a part of creation, a recipient of weather, or a cosmic witness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun, usually definite (הָאָרֶץ), paired with הַשָּׁמַיִם ('the heavens') or functioning as subject/object of cosmic or meteorological verbs

senses.definition: By metonymy, the human population living upon the earth or within a domain, summoned to worship or characterized collectively.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun, typically in the phrase כָּל הָאָרֶץ ('all the earth') with plural or collective verbal agreement, or as nomen rectum in construct chains (e.g., עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, רִשְׁעֵי אָרֶץ)

senses.definition: A bounded geographical region, country, or homeland belonging to a nation, tribe, or deity, or marked by a particular physical or social quality; plural denotes multiple foreign nations or territories.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular or plural (אֲרָצוֹת), frequently in construct with a proper name or descriptive noun, modified by an adjective, or taking a possessive suffix (אַרְצְכֶם), often following spatial prepositions (בְּ, מִן, אֶל)

senses.definition: The physical surface of the earth, soil, or ground upon which people walk, animals run, liquids are poured, plants grow, or toward which one bows or looks down.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun, with prepositions (עַל, אֶל), in construct (עֵשֶׂב הָאָרֶץ, אֲפִיקֵי הָאָרֶץ), or with the directional ending -āh (אָרְצָה / אַרְצָה) indicating downward motion

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with הַשָּׁמַיִם ('the heavens') to denote the entirety of the cosmos (GEN 1:1; DEU 4:26; HAB 3:3). In the sense of a specific territory, commonly appears in construct chains with ethnic or geographic names (e.g., אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם 'land of Egypt', EXO 10:15; אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן 'land of Canaan', NUM 33:51; אֶרֶץ יְהוּדָה 'land of Judah', 2CH 17:2) or descriptive attributes (e.g., אֶרֶץ נָכְרִיָּה 'foreign land', EXO 2:22; אֶרֶץ תַּלְאֻבוֹת 'land of drought', HOS 13:5). With the directional ending -āh (אָרְצָה / אַרְצָה), it functions adverbially to indicate downward motion 'to the ground' in prostration (GEN 43:26; JOS 7:6). When preceded by כָּל ('all') and referring to people (כָּל הָאָרֶץ), it can take plural verbal agreement (PSA 66:4). Plural אֲרָצוֹת refers to multiple distinct nations or regions (JER 16:15; EZK 20:6; EZK 39:27).

core_meaning_summary: The period of daylight, a 24-hour calendar day, the present day ('today'), an appointed occasion, or in the plural a span of time, era, or lifetime.

senses.definition: The sunlit period of daylight as opposed to night or darkness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, contrasted with לַיְלָה ('night') or bounded from אוֹר ('dawn/light') to מַחֲצִית הַיּוֹם ('midday')

senses.definition: A full 24-hour calendar day or counted unit of days in sequences, dates, and durations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), modified by cardinal or ordinal numerals, or in construct with an infinitive or date expression

senses.definition: The present day on which an utterance or action takes place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial definite singular הַיּוֹם or prepositional phrase בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה

senses.definition: A particular occasion, decisive moment, or appointed time of action, distress, or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular with demonstrative (בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא, הַיּוֹם הַהוּא) or in construct/comparison with qualitative nouns (e.g., רָעָה, עֶבְרָה, מָר) or infinitives

senses.definition: An extended span of time, historical period, ruler's reign, or the course of a person's life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural (יָמִים / יְמֵי / יָמִין), absolute, with demonstrative (בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם), with possessive suffixes, or in construct with personal names and life stages

collocations_and_notes: Plural is normally יָמִים (construct יְמֵי), with one instance of the ending -în in הַיָּמִין (DAN 12:13). Frequently contrasted with לַיְלָה ('night', GEN 1:5) and paralleled with עֵת ('time', JER 30:7; EZK 7:12). Very common fixed temporal expressions include הַיּוֹם ('today', DEU 4:26; 2SA 19:36), בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא ('on that day', 2SA 2:17; ISA 3:18; ZEP 3:11), בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם ('in those days', 2KI 20:1; EST 2:21), and בִּימֵי + personal name ('in the days/reign of', GEN 14:1; JER 1:2). Lifespan idioms include הֶאֱרִיךְ יָמִים ('prolong days', EXO 20:12; DEU 4:26) and comparing days to a shadow or breath (1CH 29:15; JOB 7:16).

core_meaning_summary: An adult male human being, individual person, or husband; extended to characterized roles, collective fighting bodies, and distributive reference ('each one').

senses.definition: An adult male human being, explicitly contrasted with women or children.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), paired or contrasted with אִשָּׁה ('woman') or טַף ('children')

senses.definition: An individual human being or unspecified person in narrative, legal, or wisdom contexts; with negation, 'no one' or 'anyone'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), definite, indefinite, or negated with לֹא

senses.definition: A married man in relation to his wife; a husband.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, typically with feminine pronominal suffix (אִישָׁהּ) or contrasted with אִשְׁתּוֹ ('his wife')

senses.definition: A person or group of people defined by occupation, character, locality, or allegiance to a leader or community (such as soldiers, prophets, allies, or inhabitants).
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural construct (אִישׁ / אַנְשֵׁי + noun) or plural with pronominal suffix (אֲנָשָׁיו / אַנְשֵׁיהֶם)

senses.definition: A collective body of men, troops, or counted individuals treated as a grammatical singular or unit counter after numerals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective singular in construct with tribal/national names (taking singular verbs) or following cardinal numerals

senses.definition: Each individual within a plural group acting or receiving separately.
senses.grammatical_frame: Distributive singular (אִישׁ / לְאִישׁ) in apposition to or paired with a plural subject or verb

collocations_and_notes: Forms an irregular plural stem אֲנָשִׁים (construct אַנְשֵׁי, suffixed אֲנָשָׁיו / אַנְשֵׁיהֶם) alongside singular אִישׁ (suffixed אִישָׁהּ). Frequently paired with אִשָּׁה ('woman / wife') for gender contrast or marriage (GEN 2:23; JDG 9:49; JER 3:1). Common construct phrases include אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה / אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה ('warriors / fighting men', DEU 2:14; 1SA 18:5; 2SA 17:8), אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים ('man of God', 2KI 4:9), and אַנְשֵׁי בְרִיתֶךָ / אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלֹמֶךָ ('allies / trusted associates', OBA 1:7). With negation לֹא, expresses 'no one / anyone' (GEN 41:44). When singular אִישׁ is in construct with a tribal or national name (e.g., אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִישׁ בִּנְיָמִן), it functions as a collective taking singular verbs (JDG 20:41). Also used distributively as 'each one', sometimes paired with אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחוֹתָהּ (EZK 1:23).

core_meaning_summary: The physical face or countenance, the outward surface or front side of an object or area, and, in prepositional compounds, location before, presence with, priority in time, or cause.

senses.definition: The front part of a human or animal head, facial expression/countenance, or anthropomorphically the face of God; used in idioms for showing favor (lifting the face) or withholding favor/attention (hiding the face).
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun (פָּנִים) with pronominal suffixes or as object/prepositional complement (e.g., עַל פָּנָיו, נֶגֶד פְּנֵיהֶם)

senses.definition: The outer upper surface of water or land, the front/facing side of an object or territory, or figuratively the outward aspect or direction of an affair.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun (פְּנֵי) governed by spatial prepositions (עַל, אֶל, אֶל מוּל) or as direct object

senses.definition: Spatial or relational position in front of, ahead of, or in the presence, sight, or judgment of someone or something (with לִפְנֵי), or departure/avoidance away from someone's presence or threat (with מִפְּנֵי / מִלִּפְנֵי).
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition (לִפְנֵי, מִפְּנֵי, מִלִּפְנֵי) + noun or pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Prior occurrence or order in time (with לִפְנֵי), or cause/reason on account of which an action or emotion happens (with מִפְּנֵי).
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition (לִפְנֵי temporal; מִפְּנֵי causal) + noun, event, or pronominal suffix

collocations_and_notes: Always appears with plural morphology (פָּנִים, construct פְּנֵי) even when referring to a single face or surface. Very frequently compounded with prepositions (לִפְנֵי, מִפְּנֵי, מִלִּפְנֵי, עַל פְּנֵי, אֶל פְּנֵי) to serve spatial, relational, temporal, and causal prepositional functions. Notable idioms include נָשָׂא פָנִים ('lift up someone's face', i.e., show favor or grant a request, 1SA 25:35) and הִסְתִּיר פָּנִים ('hide one's face', i.e., withdraw attention or favor, PSA 51:11, EZK 39:24).

core_meaning_summary: To transfer, grant, or hand over something or someone to a recipient, as well as to place or set in a location, exchange for something else, or render into a state.

senses.definition: To transfer possession of goods, land, money, food, a person (e.g., in marriage or service), or an abstract benefit/deliverance to a recipient; in passive stems, to be granted or assigned to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal) + direct object + recipient (with לְ or אֶל); also passive simple stem (Niphal) and passive participle with לְ

senses.definition: To trade, convert, or offer one thing in return for or in place of another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal) + בְּ (marking medium/price) or תַּחַת (marking substitution)

senses.definition: To surrender, entrust, or place a person, group, or military force under another's authority, custody, or power; in passive forms, to be surrendered or handed over.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), passive imperfect, or passive simple stem (Niphal) + direct object/subject + בְּיַד ('into the hand of') or אֶל

senses.definition: To put, set, fasten, or apply an object, substance, lot, or consequence in or upon a location; figuratively with אֶל לֵב, to apply one's mind to or take to heart.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal) + direct object + locative preposition (בְּ, אֶל, עַל)

senses.definition: To cause a person, land, or structure to become a specified state or condition (such as ruin or an object of scorn).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal) + direct object + predicate complement (with לְ or second accusative)

collocations_and_notes: Almost always occurs in the active basic stem (Qal), with occasional passive forms (passive participle in NUM 3:9, passive simple stem / Niphal in 1SA 18:19 and DAN 11:11, and passive imperfect in 2SA 21:6). Frequent idiomatic collocations include: נָתַן בְּיַד ('deliver/entrust into the hand/control of', JDG 6:1, 1CH 19:11, DAN 11:11); נָתַן אֶל לֵב ('take to heart / consider', ECC 7:2); נָתַן לְאִשָּׁה ('give as a wife', 1SA 18:19); נָתַן גּוֹרָלוֹת ('cast lots', LEV 16:8); and נָתַן + object + לְ or double accusative ('turn/make into', 2CH 7:20, JER 12:10, EZK 35:3). Note also the use of בְּ to mark the medium or price of exchange (DEU 14:25, EZK 27:19).

core_meaning_summary: A collective noun denoting a nation, ethnic or covenant community, the general populace of a land, or a gathered company or troop of people.

senses.definition: A distinct nation, ethnic group, or covenant community viewed as a collective whole, used both of Israel and (especially in the plural) of foreign nations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular collective noun (often with plural עַמִּים); frequently with possessive suffixes or in construct with geographic/ethnic terms

senses.definition: The general populace, citizenry, subjects of a ruler, or local community (including lay inhabitants in contrast to religious officials, or one's kinfolk).
senses.grammatical_frame: Usually definite הָעָם, or construct עַם הָאָרֶץ, or with possessive suffix; takes singular or plural verb agreement

senses.definition: A specific body of people, troop, company, or throng assembled for battle, travel, or a ceremonial procession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular collective noun modified by adjectives, relative clauses (e.g., אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ), or fractions (חֲצִי הָעָם), often taking plural verb/participle agreement

collocations_and_notes: Grammatically masculine singular (e.g., `עַם אֶחָד` in GEN 11:6, `עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף הוּא` in DEU 9:13), yet as a collective noun it frequently governs plural verbs and participles (e.g., `וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲוּוּ` in EXO 12:27, `יֹאמְרוּ` in 1SA 8:7, `הֹלְכִים` in 2SA 13:34, `נִאֲצוּ` in PSA 74:18). Often paired or paralleled with `גּוֹיִם` ("nations") in poetry and prophecy (2SA 22:44, ISA 25:7, EZK 25:7). Common construct phrases include `עַם הָאָרֶץ` ("the people of the land" / general citizenry, 2KI 23:35, JER 52:6) and `כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ` ("all the peoples of the earth", DEU 28:10). Frequently takes 1st-person pronominal suffixes (`עַמִּי`, "my people") to denote Israel in covenant relation with YHWH (EXO 5:1, ISA 5:13) or royal subjects (1CH 28:2).

core_meaning_summary: An unstressed enclitic suffix attached to nouns, adverbs, particles, imperatives, and first-person prefix verbs to indicate spatial direction or location, or to add volitional emphasis and stylistic extension.

senses.definition: Attached to common nouns, proper place names, and compass terms to mark motion toward, spatial orientation, or location at a point or surface.
senses.grammatical_frame: Unstressed suffix (-āh) on common nouns, geographic names, and directional nouns

senses.definition: Attached to spatial adverbs and prepositions to express directional motion, relative position, or upward extension in age or space.
senses.grammatical_frame: Suffix (-āh) on spatial adverbs and prepositions (e.g., מַעְלָה, שָׁמָּה, חוּצָה, נֶגְדָה)

senses.definition: Attached to masculine singular imperatives and first-person singular waw-consecutive prefix verbs to express urgency, solemn appeal, or heightened narrative expression.
senses.grammatical_frame: Suffix (-āh) on masculine singular imperatives and 1st-person singular waw-consecutive prefix verbs

senses.definition: Attached to form the fixed exclamatory expression חָלִילָה ("far be it"), expressing strong rejection or abhorrence of an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Fixed suffix on exclamatory particle חָלִילָה + לְ + pronominal suffix

collocations_and_notes: Frequently attached unstressed to nouns and place names to mark destination or compass orientation, as in the four-direction formula in DEU 3:27 and boundary descriptions in JOS 15:11 and EZK 48:4. On adverbs (`מַעְלָה`, `שָׁמָּה`, `חוּצָה`) and prepositions (`נֶגְדָה`), it forms fixed spatial/directional expressions (`מִלְּמַעְלָה` in GEN 6:16, EZK 1:22; `וָמָעְלָה` "and upward" in age counts EXO 30:14, NUM 1:40). On imperatives and `נֶגְדָה`, it co-occurs with the enclitic particle `נָּא` (GEN 38:16, PSA 116:18). On 1st-person singular `waw`-consecutive prefix verbs (`וָאֶקְרָאֶה`, `וָאֶקְבְּצָה`, `וָאֶתְּנָה`, `וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה`), it appears especially in narrative prayers and first-person memoirs.

core_meaning_summary: Denotes spoken or written language, a message or divine proclamation, a reply, an affair or event, and an appointed daily requirement.

senses.definition: An articulated utterance, statement, saying, or expression; in the plural, spoken discourse, vocabulary, or written text such as laws, songs, or prophetic scrolls.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun functioning as subject, direct object (e.g., of דִּבֶּר, שָׁמַע, כָּתַב, הִגִּיד), or in construct before a speaker or text (e.g., דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה)

senses.definition: An authoritative message, royal or divine decree, prophetic revelation, or spoken promise intended to be heard, obeyed, or fulfilled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun, most often in construct (דְּבַר יְהוָה) or with a pronominal suffix, serving as subject of הָיָה/יָצָא or object of מִלֵּא/שָׁמַע/בִּין

senses.definition: A verbal response, report, or answer returned to an inquirer, characteristically with the Hiphil of שׁוּב ("cause to return").
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun serving as direct object of Hiphil הֵשִׁיב ("bring back word to")

senses.definition: An action, deed, occurrence, situation, legal cause, or matter of concern; in the plural construct דִּבְרֵי, historical deeds or annals of a king or period, and with כָּל in negative clauses, "anything."
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun serving as subject of נִהְיָה/הָיָה, object of עָשָׂה/כִּחֵד, or in construct phrases (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים, דְּבַר הַתֹּעֵבָה)

senses.definition: The fixed quota, task, or appointed obligation assigned to a particular day.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular construct in the adverbial idiom (לִ)דְבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ

collocations_and_notes: Common collocations include דְּבַר יְהוָה ("the word/message of YHWH," often with הָיָה or שִׁמְעוּ), הֵשִׁיב דָּבָר ("to bring back word / reply"), סֵפֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ("book of the affairs/annals of the days"), and דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ ("the daily requirement / each day's allotted portion"). Frequently takes the demonstrative הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה to refer back to a preceding speech, proposal, or event, and with כָּל in negated contexts (לֹא ... לְכָל דָּבָר) expresses total exclusion ("for anything / in any respect").

core_meaning_summary: Marks an endpoint, boundary, or limit in space, time, or degree, and in fixed nominal expressions denotes unending time.

senses.definition: Indicates the spatial limit, destination, or boundary reached by movement, sight, territory, or a written section, often paired with מִן ("from") or used with spatial adverbs such as פֹּה and הֵנָּה.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a place name, spatial noun, or spatial adverb; frequently paired with מִן ... וְעַד

senses.definition: Marks the temporal limit or endpoint up to which a state or action continues, the duration of a period, or in questions with מָתַי the length of time before a change occurs.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a temporal noun, infinitive construct (with or without pronominal suffix), or the interrogative adverb מָתַי

senses.definition: Introduces a subordinate temporal clause marking the point at which an action takes place or, when negated with לֹא, the time prior to an impending state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound conjunction (עַד אֲשֶׁר, עַד שֶׁ, or עַד אֲשֶׁר לֹא) followed by a finite verb clause

senses.definition: Expresses extremity of degree, intensity, or inclusive coverage of every member within a category, including "not even one" in negated clauses with אֶחָד.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun of extremity (מָוֶת), adverb of degree (מְאֹד), numeral (אֶחָד), or the upper end of a paired/inclusive list

senses.definition: Denotes unending or perpetual duration when used nominally after the preposition לְ or in the doubled phrase עֲדֵי עַד.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in prepositional phrases (לָעַד) or construct-like poetic combination (עֲדֵי עַד)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with מִן ("from") to mark both ends of a spatial, temporal, or inclusive range (e.g., מִן הַבֹּקֶר עַד הָעָרֶב in EXO 18:13; לְמִדָּן וְעַד בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע in JDG 20:1; מִקָּטֹן וְעַד גָּדוֹל in 1SA 5:9; מֵהֹדּוּ וְעַד כּוּשׁ in EST 8:9; מִמִּזְרַח שֶׁמֶשׁ עַד מְבֹאוֹ in PSA 50:1). Common fixed combinations include עַד מְאֹד ("exceedingly"), עַד מָתַי ("until when? / how long?"), עַד אֶחָד ("even one" in negative clauses), עַד הֵנָּה ("up to this point"), עַד פֹּה ("this far"), לָעַד and עֲדֵי עַד ("forever / for all time"). Takes the poetic construct-like plural form עֲדֵי in ISA 26:4. Before finite verbs it combines with אֲשֶׁר (or שֶׁ in PSA 123:2), and with אֲשֶׁר לֹא in ECC 12:1 to express "before".

core_meaning_summary: To perceive with the eyes, examine, recognize mentally, or experience; in the passive/reflexive stem to be visible or appear before someone, and in the causative stem to cause someone to see or show.

senses.definition: To perceive physically with the eyes, catch sight of, watch, gaze at, meet face-to-face (`רָאָה פְּנֵי`), or behold a prophetic vision (often introduced with `וְהִנֵּה`).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with direct object, with `מִן`/`בְּ`, or absolute (with `וְהִנֵּה`)

senses.definition: To inspect or examine carefully (such as a skin condition or a land), or to take attentive, compassionate notice of a person's plight or actions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with object or absolute, often with `פְּקַח עֵינֶיךָ` or `וְהִנֵּה`

senses.definition: To perceive mentally, realize, recognize, witness firsthand, or observe and evaluate a fact or outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), taking a `כִּי` or `אֲשֶׁר` complement clause or an event/deed as direct object

senses.definition: To experience, enjoy, or undergo a condition or fate (such as good, affliction, or the pit/death).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with abstract noun object (`טוֹבָה`, `עֳנִי`, `שָׁחַת`)

senses.definition: In the active stem with `בְּ` and `לְ`, to select or provide someone for a role; as a passive participle, to be deemed suitable or fitting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) with `בְּ` + indirect `לְ` + object; or Qal passive participle (`רְאֻיוֹת`)

senses.definition: Substantival participle denoting a prophetic figure who receives divine insight and delivers messages from God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) participle used as a noun with definite article (`הָרֹאֶה`)

senses.definition: In the passive/reflexive stem, to be visible or seen; with `פְּנֵי` or `אֶת פְּנֵי`, to appear or present oneself before the LORD.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), intransitive or with `פְּנֵי` / `אֶת פְּנֵי`

senses.definition: In the causative stem, to cause someone to see something, specifically to show a prophetic vision.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with personal object suffix + `וְהִנֵּה`

collocations_and_notes: The basic active stem (Qal) covers physical sight, careful inspection, mental recognition, experiencing a condition, and selecting/providing. Its passive participle (`רָאוּי`) means 'fitting/suitable' (EST 2:9), and its active participle substantivized (`הָרֹאֶה`) designates a prophetic 'seer' (2CH 16:7). The passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) means 'be seen, be visible' (1KI 8:8) or, specifically with `פְּנֵי` / `אֶת פְּנֵי`, 'appear/present oneself before' the deity (EXO 34:23, ISA 1:12). The causative stem (Hiphil) means 'cause to see, show' (JER 24:1). Common collocations include `רָאָה` + `וְהִנֵּה` introducing a vivid sight or vision, `רָאָה` + `כִּי` introducing a realized fact, and `רָאָה פְנֵי` ('see the face of', i.e., meet or have an audience with).

core_meaning_summary: Masculine singular proximal demonstrative indicating a specific entity, person, time, place, or statement near to the speaker or discourse context, and also serving in spatial, temporal, and emphatic interrogative constructions.

senses.definition: Used attributively after a definite masculine singular noun (or noun phrase) with the definite article, or following `אֲשֶׁר כְּ-`, to single out a specific person, object, matter, place, or day as immediate in context.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive demonstrative with definite article following definite masculine singular noun (`הַ-... הַזֶּה`), or with prefixed preposition after relative particle (`אֲשֶׁר כָּזֶה`)

senses.definition: Used independently as the subject, predicate, or object of a clause to identify an entity, introduce or summarize an account or enumeration, or contrast two items in a correlative pair.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent demonstrative pronoun (subject or predicate of nominal/verbal clause, including correlative `זֶה ... זֶה` and pre-nominal `זֶה עָנִי`)

senses.definition: Used adverbially with prepositions `מִן` or `בְּ` to indicate the immediate place or side, or placed before a time noun to measure elapsed duration up to the present.
glosses: on this side ... on that side
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional spatial adverbial (`מִזֶּה`, `בָּזֶה`) or temporal modifier preceding a noun of time (`זֶה יָמִים רַבִּים`)

senses.definition: Placed immediately after an interrogative particle to add emphasis, surprise, urgency, or focused specification to a question.
senses.grammatical_frame: Enclitic intensifier following an interrogative (`מַה זֶּה`, `לָמָּה זֶּה`, `אֵי זֶה`)

collocations_and_notes: Very frequently occurs attributively with the definite article after a definite noun (`הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה`, 'this day / today'; `עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה`, 'until this day'; `הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה`, 'this matter/word'; `הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה`, 'this place'; `הָעָם הַזֶּה`, 'this people'). Takes prefixed prepositions such as `בָּזֶה` ('here'), `מִזֶּה` ('from here / on this side'), and `כָּזֶה` ('like this / such as this'). Occurs in correlative pairs (`זֶה ... וְזֶה`, `מִזֶּה ... מִזֶּה`) to contrast two entities or opposite sides. When placed immediately after interrogatives (`מַה זֶּה`, `לָמָּה זֶּה`, `אֵי זֶה`), it adds emphasis or urgency. Note that feminine and plural demonstrative forms are separate lemmas; in this sample `זֶה` consistently functions as the masculine singular/unmarked form.

core_meaning_summary: To perceive sound, hear news, listen attentively and obey, or answer a plea, with passive ('be heard') and causative ('proclaim') usages across stems.

senses.definition: To perceive a sound or voice by ear, or to pay auditory attention when summoned to listen.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), with direct object (sound/voice) or absolute in calls to attention

senses.definition: To receive news, a report, or information about an event or person; to learn of something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), with direct object, כִּי ('that') clause, מִן ('from'), אֶל ('about'), or absolute

senses.definition: To listen attentively to instruction, counsel, or command and comply with or obey it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), with בְּקוֹל ('the voice of'), לְ ('to'), אֶל ('to'), direct object ('word'), or absolute

senses.definition: To hear favorably, take note of, and respond to a prayer, plea, or complaint, especially of God toward petitioners.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), with direct object of prayer/supplication/complaint or absolute

senses.definition: To be audible or heard, whether of physical tools, a faint whisper, or spoken blessing and prayer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive (Niphal), with grammatical subject or בְּקוֹל ('in/with voice')

senses.definition: To cause someone to hear something; to proclaim, announce, or declare publicly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative (Hiphil), with direct object or double object (recipient and message)

collocations_and_notes: In the simple active stem (Qal), obedience and compliance are commonly marked with בְּקוֹל / בְקֹל ('the voice of', GEN 27:13, JOS 22:2), אֶל ('to', DEU 18:14, JER 27:17, JER 35:16, DAN 9:6), or לְ ('to', LEV 26:21, PRO 12:15). Frequently parallels verbs of attentive listening such as הֶאֱזִין ('give ear', PSA 54:4, ISA 1:2, ISA 42:23), הִקְשִׁיב ('pay attention', ISA 34:1, ISA 42:23), and הִטָּה אֹזֶן ('incline the ear', JER 11:8). Often paired with עָשָׂה ('to do') to express hearing followed by action (DEU 5:27, DEU 30:12, JER 11:8), and with רָאָה ('to see', LAM 1:18). In the passive stem (Niphal), occurs with בְּקוֹלָם ('their voice was heard', 2CH 30:27).

core_meaning_summary: To speak, utter words, address someone, or declare authoritatively, with simple active, intensive/declarative active, and reciprocal conferring usages across stems.

senses.definition: To utter words, converse, or address someone orally, often introducing direct speech or indicating the content, manner, or language of speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (Piel), absolute or with אֶל ('to'), אֵת ('with'), לְ ('to'), בְּאָזְנֵי ('in the hearing of'), or direct object of speech content

senses.definition: To speak silently within oneself or formulate unspoken thoughts in one's mind.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (Piel) + אֶל לֵב ('to the heart')

senses.definition: To issue an authoritative command, decree, prophetic pronouncement, or binding promise, especially by God, a prophet, or a ruler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (Piel), with אֶל ('to'), עַל ('concerning'), direct object of decrees/words, or absolute in formulaic pronouncements

senses.definition: To speak or express oneself in a specified moral or truthful manner.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal participle) + adverbial/object modifier

senses.definition: To confer together or talk in opposition against someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reciprocal/middle (Niphal) + בְּ ('against')

collocations_and_notes: In the active stem (Piel), frequently introduces direct discourse with the preposition אֶל ('to') marking the addressee followed by לֵאמֹר ('saying') (e.g., GEN 8:15, EXO 6:10, LEV 7:22, NUM 1:48, DEU 20:5). Also constructs with אֵת ('with', EXO 31:18, JER 38:25), עַל ('concerning', 1CH 17:17), בְּאָזְנֵי ('in the ears of', 1SA 25:24), and אֶל לִבִּי ('to my heart', GEN 24:45). Often pairs with the noun דָּבָר ('word/matter') in expressions like הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר (JOS 14:6, 1SA 3:17, 2SA 14:15, JER 29:23), and occurs in the divine confirmation formula כִּי פִי יְהוָה דִּבֵּר ('for the mouth of YHWH has spoken', ISA 1:20, ISA 40:5). Frequently paired with אָמַר ('to say') and עָשָׂה ('to act/carry out', e.g., 1KI 2:38, EZK 24:14).

core_meaning_summary: A permanent, typically fortified settlement or town, and by extension its civic body or inhabitants.

senses.definition: A permanent, built-up settlement—ranging from a regional town to a fortified stronghold or major capital—typically enclosed with walls and gates and distinguished from surrounding open villages or pasturelands.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; used absolutely, with adjectives/demonstratives, in construct with regions, rulers, or functions, and as an unmarked directional accusative

senses.definition: The civic community or population of a city or town, whether referred to collectively by metonymy or through officials and members associated with it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; subject of human actions or states ('was quiet', 'dwell'), or governing noun/genitive in construct with civic offices and residents ('elders of the city', 'men of the city', 'governor of the city')

collocations_and_notes: Feminine noun with irregular plural עָרִים (construct עָרֵי). Frequently appears in construct chains specifying role or possession (e.g., עָרֵי מִקְלָט 'cities of refuge', עָרֵי הָרֶכֶב 'chariot cities', עִיר דָּוִיד 'City of David', שַׂר הָעִיר 'governor of the city', שַׁעַר הָעִיר 'gate of the city'). Often paired or contrasted with surrounding open 'villages' (חֲצֵרִים) or 'pasturelands' (מִגְרָשִׁים), and with 'fortified' (בְּצֻרוֹת) as an epithet. Exhibits distributive repetition (עִיר עִיר 'each city') and singular use with numbers above ten (e.g., שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה עִיר 'thirteen cities').

core_meaning_summary: To sit down or take a seat, remain in place, dwell or settle in a location, and in the causative stem to settle people or repopulate cities.

senses.definition: To take or occupy a seated posture, such as sitting down before someone, sitting in an assembly, or sitting stationed at a gate or landmark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive with prepositional phrases of location ('between', 'before', 'beside', 'in a seat') or participle in construct with a place ('at the gate')

senses.definition: To sit upon a royal throne as ruler, or to occupy a seat of divine dwelling and sovereignty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; participle with 'upon his throne', or infinitive construct denoting a royal or heavenly dwelling seat

senses.definition: To stay, wait, or remain temporarily in a place, with someone, or in a particular state over a period of time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive with locative adverbs ('here'), prepositional phrases ('in one's place', 'with'), or phrases of temporal duration

senses.definition: To live, reside, or settle permanently in a territory, city, or household; the participle frequently functions as a noun meaning 'inhabitant(s)' or 'resident(s)'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive with locative prepositions ('in', 'upon', 'among', 'with'), or participle used substantively (absolute or in construct with a place name)

senses.definition: Of a city or land, to be inhabited, remain populated, or continue to stand as a settled place rather than lying desolate.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive with a city or personified place as subject

senses.definition: To cause people to dwell or settle in a place, or to make desolate cities inhabited again.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem; transitive with direct object (person or city) and optional locative prepositional phrase

collocations_and_notes: Frequently pairs with prepositions indicating location or company: בְּ ('in'), עַל ('upon'), אֵצֶל ('beside'), בֵּין ('between'), לִפְנֵי ('before'), בְּקֶרֶב ('in the midst of'), עִם / אֶת ('with'), and adverbial לָבֶטַח ('securely'). The participle in construct (יֹשְׁבֵי, 'inhabitants of') is a regular designation for the population of a city or land, and יֹשְׁבֵי שָׁעַר ('those who sit at the gate') denotes people gathered at the city gate. Often contrasts with 'going out' (יָצָא) when expressing remaining in place. In the causative stem, it governs both the people settled and the cities repopulated.

core_meaning_summary: To go or come out from a place, condition, or source, and (in the causative stem) to bring, lead, or produce outward.

senses.definition: To exit, depart, or move outward from an enclosed space, city, land, or someone's presence; to come out to meet or pursue someone; in the imperative, to get out or leave.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem), intransitive with מִן, מֵעִם, מִתּוֹךְ, אֶל, לִקְרַאת, אַחֲרֵי, or directional -הָ

senses.definition: To march out on a military campaign, enter battle, or serve as an active soldier or leader before the troops.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem), intransitive with צָבָא, לַמִּלְחָמָה, לִפְנֵי, בְּקֶרֶב, or לְ + destination

senses.definition: To flow or discharge from the body; to sprout or emerge from an object; of a cast lot, to come out or fall to someone; or of abstract qualities such as justice, to proceed from someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem), intransitive with מִן or לְ, with non-human or abstract subject

senses.definition: To cause people or objects to move out of a place; to bring out, lead out, carry away, or deliver someone from confinement or distress into safety.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative stem), transitive with אֶת or object suffix, often with מִן, אֶל, or לְ

senses.definition: Of the ground or earth, to cause vegetation to sprout and grow outward.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative stem), transitive with הָאָרֶץ as subject

senses.definition: To be led out or brought forth from a place (referring to surviving inhabitants).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hophal (passive of causative stem), participle

collocations_and_notes: In the Qal (basic active) stem, the verb is intransitive and takes prepositions indicating source (מִן 'from', מֵעִם 'from the presence of', מִתּוֹךְ 'from the midst of') or goal/direction (אֶל 'to', לְ 'to', לִקְרַאת 'to meet', אַחֲרֵי 'after'). It frequently describes Israel's departure from Egypt (e.g., 1KI 6:1; PSA 114:1) and military mobilization (יֹצֵא צָבָא 'going out to military service', NUM 1:3; תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה 'go out to battle', DEU 20:1). The Hiphil (causative) stem shifts the action to a transitive agent causing exit or emergence, commonly used for God bringing Israel out of Egypt (EXO 16:6; DEU 5:15), removing objects or people (NUM 15:36; EZR 1:7), rescuing from distress (PSA 18:20), or the earth producing plant life (GEN 1:12). The Hophal (passive of the causative stem) appears for people being brought out of a city (EZK 14:22).

core_meaning_summary: To go or come back to a previous place, state, or course of action, and (in the causative stem) to bring back, restore, repay, or reply.

senses.definition: To move or go back to a starting point, former location, person, or original physical state; when paired with a verb of running, to dart back and forth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem), intransitive, often with אֶל, לְ, directional -הָ, or מִן

senses.definition: To turn back or desist from an activity such as pursuit; to turn away from wicked conduct or transgressions; to turn back toward God in devotion; or, of anger, to subside and turn away.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem), intransitive with מִן + infinitive/noun, בְּ, or absolute

senses.definition: Used before another verb to indicate doing something once more or turning one's attention back to an observation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem) coordinated with a following verb

senses.definition: To bring back the captive condition or restore the former well-being and fortunes of a people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active stem), transitive with cognate-like object שְׁבוּת / שְׁבִית

senses.definition: To cause a person or thing to go back; to bring someone back, drive back an armed attack, hold back or restrain anger, or revoke a decreed punishment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative stem), transitive with אֶת or object suffix, often with אֶל or directional adverb

senses.definition: To give back or repay money, property, or territory to its owner; to restore a community's fortunes; or, with 'hand' and עַל, to direct hostile power back against a target.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative stem), transitive with אֶת/object and לְ (recipient) or עַל

senses.definition: To bring back a report or reply in words to someone; with 'to their heart' (אֶל לֵב), to recall to mind and reflect seriously.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative stem), transitive with דָּבָר/מִלִּין or interrogative מָה, or idiomatically with אֶל לֵב

collocations_and_notes: In the Qal (basic active) stem, the verb is predominantly intransitive and frequently pairs with spatial prepositions (אֶל 'to', לְ 'to', מִן 'from') or the directional suffix -הָ, as well as the paired infinitive absolute expression רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב ('running back and forth', EZK 1:14). With מִן followed by an infinitive or noun of action/conduct (such as רְדֹף 'pursuing' or דַּרְכּוֹ הָרָעָה 'his evil way'), it denotes turning back from a pursuit or abandoning wrong behavior. Notably, the idiom 'restore the fortunes/captivity' appears in both the Qal stem (שָׁב שְׁבוּת / שְׁבִית, PSA 53:7; PSA 85:2) and the Hiphil (causative) stem (הֵשִׁיב שְׁבוּת, JER 33:7). The Hiphil stem also forms specialized idioms: הֵשִׁיב דָּבָר ('bring back word / report', JOS 22:32), הֵשִׁיב מִלִּין ('answer with words', JOB 35:4), הֵשִׁיב אֶל לֵב ('bring back to mind / take to heart', 1KI 8:47), הֵשִׁיב אַף ('turn back anger', JOB 9:13), and הֵשִׁיב יָד עַל ('turn one's hand against', EZK 38:12).

core_meaning_summary: Preposition marking accompaniment, association, relational alignment or opposition, shared condition, and (with מִן) separation or source.

senses.definition: Indicating spatial proximity, accompaniment, companionship, or shared participation and fate (including the idiom of lying down or being buried with one's ancestors).
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun phrase or pronominal suffix, often with verbs of motion, sitting, dwelling, or acting together

senses.definition: Marking inclusion alongside other items or persons in a list, social rank, or group estimation and memory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition linking an entity or object to another group or set

senses.definition: Denoting relational alignment, loyal presence or military/divine backing, covenant partnership, standing before God, or possession and knowledge held by someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition in nominal clauses or with verbs of being, covenant-making (כָּרַת בְּרִית), or finding/understanding

senses.definition: Marking the opposing party in conflict, warfare, or hostile conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition with verbs of fighting (נִלְחַם) or hostile conduct (הָלַךְ ... בְּקֶרִי)

senses.definition: Expressing temporal coexistence or duration alongside an enduring phenomenon.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition preceding a celestial noun (שָׁמֶשׁ) in parallel with a temporal phrase

senses.definition: Combined with מִן as מֵעִם to express separation or departure from someone's presence, originating divine agency, or a standard of comparison.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition מֵעִם with verbs of motion/departure, source clauses, or comparative adjectives (רַב מֵעִמּוֹ)

collocations_and_notes: Takes pronominal suffixes with doubled mem (e.g., עִמִּי, עִמְּךָ, עִמּוֹ, עִמָּהּ, עִמָּנוּ, עִמָּכֶם, עִמָּם). Recurring idioms include שָׁכַב עִם אֲבֹתָיו ('lie down with one's fathers', referring to death, 1KI 15:8, 2KI 13:13), כָּרַת בְּרִית עִם ('make a covenant with', DEU 5:2, HOS 2:20), הָלַךְ עִם ('go with / support' in DEU 20:4, DEU 31:6; or 'act in hostility against' with קֶרִי in LEV 26:27), and נִלְחַם עִם ('fight against', DEU 20:4, 2CH 17:10). Often combined with מִן as מֵעִם to express separation, origin, or comparison.

core_meaning_summary: To go, walk, travel, or conduct oneself along a course, and in the causative stem to lead or bring someone along a way.

senses.definition: To move physically from one place to another, depart, travel, crawl (of a serpent), march to battle, or go into exile, often accompanied by directional prepositions or adverbial phrases of accompaniment or route.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); often with prepositions אֶל, מִן, לִפְנֵי, אַחֲרֵי, אִתִּי, locative ה-, or adverbials (יַחְדָּו, בַּגּוֹלָה)

senses.definition: Used immediately before another verb (especially in imperatives or consecutive narrative forms) to introduce or initiate a subsequent action, expressing movement undertaken in order to carry out that action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) imperative or narrative past directly followed by a second imperative or consecutive verb

senses.definition: To conduct oneself, live according to a moral or religious pattern, follow a deity in loyalty or worship, or experience an ongoing emotional state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) with prepositional phrases (בְּדֶרֶךְ, בְּיִרְאַת, אַחֲרֵי, עִם קֶרִי) or a descriptive participle (קֹדֵר)

senses.definition: To advance continuously in degree or status when paired with its own infinitive absolute and a following adjective or participle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) finite verb + Qal infinitive absolute (הָלוֹךְ) + adjective/participle (וְגָדוֹל)

senses.definition: To cause someone to go, lead, guide, escort, or bring a person to a destination.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) taking a direct personal object (אֵת or pronominal suffix) and a goal expression (עַל, אֶל, or locative ה-)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with a second verb to initiate an action (e.g., קוּם לֵךְ 'arise, go' in GEN 28:2, GEN 38:19, SNG 2:13; לֵךְ שֻׁב 'go, return' in EXO 4:19; לְכוּ וְהִכִּיתֶם in JDG 21:10) and with directional expressions using אֶל, מִן, אַחֲרֵי, אִתִּי, לִפְנֵי, or locative ה-. Idiomatic pairings include הָלַךְ הָלוֹךְ וְגָדוֹל (2SA 5:10, progressive growth), הָלַךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ / בְּיִרְאַת (moral/religious conduct, 1KI 16:26, NEH 5:9), הָלַךְ אַחֲרֵי (following/allegiance to a deity, DEU 13:5, JER 7:6), הָלַךְ עִם קֶרִי (acting in hostility, LEV 26:21), and בַּגּוֹלָה יֵלֵךְ (going into exile, JER 49:3). In the simple active stem (Qal), the subject moves or conducts itself; in the causative stem (Hiphil), the subject causes or guides someone else to go (1KI 1:38, 2KI 6:19, JER 31:9, EZK 47:6).

core_meaning_summary: The numeral 'one', functioning to count a single entity, denote uniqueness or solitude, express sameness or unity, distinguish an individual within a set, and mark the first day of a month.

senses.definition: Cardinal number indicating a quantity of one unit, person, item, or occurrence, as well as the unit digit in compound numerals (e.g., eleven, six hundred twenty-one) and tally lists.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective following a singular noun, predicate tally numeral, or component of a compound numeral

senses.definition: Single, solitary, or alone, emphasizing individuality in contrast to a group or total absence in negative statements ('not even one').
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive or predicate modifier, often in negative clauses with לֹא / אֵין or contrasted with a larger group

senses.definition: Identical, uniform, shared, or united, describing a single standard, measure, law, or unified mind/action shared by multiple items or people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive modifier following nouns of measure, law, heart, or collective person (often in כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד 'as one man')

senses.definition: A particular or indefinite individual, one of a set, each individual member of a group, or one in correlation with another ('the one ... the other').
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct or absolute substantive with partitive מִן ('from/of'), definite attributive or correlative (הָאֶחָד ... הָאֶחָד), or indefinite noun modifier

senses.definition: Ordinal designation for the first day in calendrical date formulas.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive with preposition בְּ preceding לַחֹדֶשׁ ('of the month')

collocations_and_notes: Inflects for gender (masculine אֶחָד, feminine אַחַת, construct אַחַד) and agrees with its noun when attributive, typically following the noun (e.g., פַּר אֶחָד, מִדָּה אַחַת). When definite (הָאֶחָד / הָאַחַת), it singles out one individual or paired item ('the one', 'each'). Notable idioms include מִדָּה אַחַת ('same/uniform measurement', EXO 26:2, EXO 36:15, 1KI 6:25), כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד ('as one man / united', JDG 20:11), לֵב אֶחָד ('one heart / single mind', 2CH 30:12), פַּעַם אֶחָת ('once', JOS 6:3), and בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ ('on the first day of the month', EXO 40:2, EZK 31:1). In negative clauses such as לֹא נִשְׁאַר אֶחָד (EXO 8:27) and אֵין גַּם־אֶחָד (PSA 14:3), it emphasizes complete absence ('not even one').

core_meaning_summary: To take hold of, fetch, receive, seize, or acquire an object or person, extending from physical grasping to accepting offerings or bribes, capturing in war, appointing to a role, and taking a spouse.

senses.definition: To lay hold of, pick up, or carry an object or person physically, often in one's hand or arms.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + direct object (often with בְּיָד 'in hand' or עַל־זְרוֹעֹת 'on arms'); also impersonal/passive plural in 2SA 23:6

senses.definition: To fetch, bring, retrieve, or procure someone or something from a source for use, delivery, or action, frequently paired with verbs of going or sending.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + direct object, often with לְ ('for'), אֶל ('to'), or following הָלַךְ ('go') / שָׁלַח ('send')

senses.definition: To receive, collect, or accept something offered, due, or imparted, including sacrifices, tithes, levies, bribes, or moral instruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + direct object, often with מִן / מִיַּד / מֵאֵת ('from' / 'from the hand of')

senses.definition: To capture, seize, arrest, or take possession of people, territory, or spoil by force or official authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + direct object (persons, land, or collective wealth)

senses.definition: To take or remove a person from a prior setting in order to place, conscript, or appoint them to a task or office.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + personal direct object + מִן ('from') or לְ ('for' / infinitive of purpose)

senses.definition: To take someone in marriage or as a sexual partner.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + personal object (woman/women or partners), sometimes with לְ ('for') or עַל ('in addition to')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in serial narrative chains preceding a verb of placement, wearing, sending, or action (e.g., GEN 2:15, GEN 22:6, GEN 27:15, 2KI 16:8). Common prepositional collocations include בְּיָד ('in hand', GEN 22:6, 2KI 9:1, 1KI 17:11), מִן / מִיַּד / מֵאֵת ('from' / 'from the hand of', NUM 5:25, NUM 18:26, JDG 13:23, JOB 35:7), and לְ indicating beneficiary or intended role (EXO 12:21, 1SA 8:13, 2KI 3:15). In 2SA 23:6, the third-person plural form יִקָּחוּ occurs with a negative ('not by hand') either impersonally ('people do not handle them') or as a passive ('they are not taken/handled'); all other forms in the sample are active simple-stem (Qal) usages. Idiomatic expressions include לָקַח שֹׁחַד ('accept a bribe', DEU 16:19, DEU 27:25) and לָקַח אִשָּׁה / נָשִׁים ('take a wife / wives', GEN 31:50, JDG 21:22).

core_meaning_summary: To have mental awareness, factual knowledge, personal acquaintance, practical skill, or experiential familiarity (simple active stem), and to make known, inform, or reveal (causative stem).

senses.definition: To possess cognitive awareness or factual understanding of something, or to discern, ascertain, and find out a fact or state of affairs.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); used with direct object, complement clause (kî / ʾăšer / interrogative), or absolutely

senses.definition: To be personally acquainted with someone or something, or to experience and encounter a condition, relationship, or deity firsthand.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); transitive with direct object of a person, deity, condition, or way of life

senses.definition: To possess practical expertise, competence, or learned ability in a domain or course of action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); construct plural participle with domain noun, or finite verb + lĕ- + infinitive construct

senses.definition: To have sexual intercourse with a partner.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); participle taking the object 'lying with a male' (miškab zākār)

senses.definition: To cause someone to know something; to inform, instruct, declare, or reveal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil); takes personal recipient (direct object or suffix) and/or content object or kî / ʾăšer clause

collocations_and_notes: Observed in two stems: the simple active stem (Qal) for knowing, recognizing, experiencing, or possessing skill, and the causative stem (Hiphil) for informing, revealing, or teaching. Frequent patterns include the recognition formula 'you/they shall know that I am YHWH' (EXO 8:18, EZK 11:12, EZK 20:26, EZK 29:9); infinitive absolute + finite verb for certainty ('surely know', JOS 23:13); 'know good and evil' for moral discernment (GEN 3:5); 'know by name' for personal favor/intimacy (EXO 33:12); and 'know the way of peace' (ISA 59:8). Often paired with 'understand' (bîn) or 'learn' (lāmad) in parallelism (PSA 92:7, ISA 29:24).

core_meaning_summary: The physical organ of sight, extended to attentive regard, emotional or moral disposition, personal judgment or approval ('in the eyes of'), public presence ('before the eyes of'), and the visible appearance or surface of things.

senses.definition: The bodily organ of vision in humans and symbolic beings, or anthropomorphically attributed to God; used for seeing, weeping, waking/sleeping, and directing expectant or watchful attention.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (often dual or construct plural with pronominal suffixes); subject of verbs of seeing, opening, weeping, or failing, or object of 'lift up' (nāśāʾ)

senses.definition: The eye conceived as the seat or expression of an inward moral or emotional attitude toward another, either begrudging stinginess or sparing compassion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun as subject of stative/active verbs ('be evil/grudging' with bĕ-, or 'spare/pity' with ʿal)

senses.definition: A person's or God's perspective, judgment, evaluation, or approval, expressed idiomatically by 'in the eyes of'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase bĕʿênê ('in the eyes of') + noun or pronominal suffix, modifying evaluations ('good', 'evil', 'right', 'contemptible', 'find favor') or comparisons

senses.definition: The direct presence or open view of onlookers, denoting an action carried out visibly or publicly before witnesses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase lĕʿênê ('to/for the eyes of') + noun or pronominal suffix

senses.definition: The outward look, color, or visible surface of a substance or of the land.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun in construct (ʿên hāʾāreṣ) or with suffix/comparison (kĕʿên)

collocations_and_notes: Frequent idiomatic collocations include: 'to lift up one's eyes and see' (GEN 22:13, NUM 24:2); 'to find favor in the eyes of' (EXO 33:17, RUT 2:10, 2SA 15:25); 'to do what is evil/right/good in the eyes of' (JDG 2:11, 2KI 10:30, 1KI 21:2, PRO 12:15); 'open eyes' for attentive care (1KI 8:52, 2CH 6:40); 'your eye be evil against' for begrudging (DEU 15:9); 'my eye spared' for showing pity (EZK 20:17); and 'before the eyes of' for public witness (JER 39:6, EZK 38:23, ZEP 3:20). In comparative or landscape descriptions, it denotes outward look or visible surface (EXO 10:5, NUM 11:7). Dual endings appear for paired eyes (1SA 16:12, SNG 4:1, EZK 10:12).
