core_meaning_summary: To move, go, or come upward, and (causatively) to bring up, lift up, or place onto a surface.

senses.definition: To move physically upward or travel to a higher or central destination (such as a mountain, rooftop, sanctuary, city, or from Egypt/exile to the land).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem; intransitive, with destination marked by direct object, directional ending, אֶל, or לְ, or origin by מִן

senses.definition: Of natural phenomena, plants, objects, or drawn lots: to rise upward, evaporate/lift, sprout, ascend in a balance scale, or come up in lot-casting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem; intransitive with non-human or inanimate subject

senses.definition: To march up to battle or invade a territory (often with עַל 'against' or לַמִּלְחָמָה 'to war'), or with מֵעַל to withdraw/retreat from attacking someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem; intransitive with military goal (עַל / לְ) or separation (מֵעַל)

senses.definition: Figuratively, to intensify (of battle), to excel or surpass others (with עַל), or to come upon and weigh down someone (of transgressions/a yoke upon the neck).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem; intransitive or with עַל introducing the compared standard or affected body part

senses.definition: To be lifted up or taken up off a place (used of the cloud rising from over the tabernacle as the signal for Israel to set out).
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem; infinitive construct with מֵעַל or pronoun subject

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to go up: to bring/lead people up a mountain or out of Egypt/the sea, to carry sacred objects up, to lift someone into a chariot, or to bring an invading army against a people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem; transitive with direct object and optional מִן ('from'), אֶל ('to'), or עַל ('against')

senses.definition: To set up or light lamps, to place or apply ornaments or embroidered figures onto garments/textiles, or to cause flesh to grow over bones.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem; transitive with direct object and optional עַל ('upon')

collocations_and_notes: Stem distinctions in context: the basic active stem expresses self-propelled upward movement, sprouting/rising, military advance/withdrawal, or figurative surpassing; the passive/reflexive stem expresses being lifted or taken up (EXO 40:36, NUM 9:22); the causative stem expresses bringing or leading someone or something up, setting up/lighting lamps, or placing/growing something onto a surface. Frequently pairs with directional ה־ (הָהָרָה, הַשָּׁמַיְמָה), מִן ('from', indicating point of departure such as Egypt or exile), אֶל/לְ ('to'), and עַל ('upon' or 'against' in military, comparative, or surface-contact contexts). Cognate noun מַעֲלֶה ('ascent') and infinitive absolute + finite verb construction ('עָלוּ עָלֹה', 2SA 15:30) also appear in context.

core_meaning_summary: First-person singular independent personal pronoun denoting the speaker ('I').

senses.definition: Identifies the speaker or characterizes the speaker's state, identity, role, or presence as the subject of a verbless (nominal) clause, including divine self-identifications and oath formulas.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun as subject of a nominal (verbless) clause

senses.definition: Supplies the first-person singular grammatical subject for a participial predicate (which lacks person marking), often introduced by הִנֵּה ('behold') or a relative particle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun as subject with a participle

senses.definition: Marks the first-person singular subject alongside a finite verb (whose inflection already marks person) to signal contrast, focus, inclusion ('I also'), exclusivity ('only I'), or coordination with another noun phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun as emphatic, contrastive, or coordinated subject with a finite verb

senses.definition: Frames the speaker's perspective or counsel in an elliptical clause preceding an imperative/infinitive without an explicit verb of speaking.
senses.grammatical_frame: Fronted independent pronoun in an elliptical clause before a command/infinitive

collocations_and_notes: Frequently prefixed with conjunction וַ־ ('and/but I', marking topic shift or contrast), כִּי ('for/that I'), or הִנֵּה ('behold, I'). Frequently appears in covenantal/divine self-identification formulas ('אֲנִי יְהוָה', 'אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם') and oath formulas ('חַי אָנִי', EZK 14:16). Takes pausal form אָנִי (e.g., JOB 33:6, PSA 119:63, EZK 9:8, EZK 14:16). Combines with גַּם ('I also'), רַק ... לְבַדִּי ('only I alone', JOB 1:17), and may be doubled ('אֲנִי אֲנִי', HOS 5:14) for strong emphasis. Alternates with the longer first-person pronoun אָנֹכִי in adjacent clauses (JDG 19:18, NEH 1:6, HOS 5:14).

core_meaning_summary: To die or cease to live (basic intransitive stem), and in causative/intensive stems to put to death or be put to death.

senses.definition: To cease living or undergo physical death, whether of humans or animals, naturally, accidentally, as divine/legal judgment, or by violence. In the infinitive construct it refers to the event of dying ("death", EZK 33:11), and as a predicate participle it can express being dead or imminently about to die (JER 28:16).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic intransitive stem); often reinforced with infinitive absolute (מוֹת תָּמוּת) or with instrument marked by בְּ (e.g., sword, famine, stone)

senses.definition: Used figuratively of an abstract quality or institution coming to an end or disappearing completely along with its possessors.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic intransitive stem) with an abstract noun subject (חָכְמָה, "wisdom")

senses.definition: As a participle functioning adjectivally or as a noun, refers to someone who is dead, a corpse, or collectively the deceased (often contrasted with the living).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal participle used substantively (singular מֵת, plural מֵתִים) or adjectivally/appositionally

senses.definition: To cause a person to die, whether by execution, judicial authority, military action, or murder; expressed in both the causative active stem (Hiphil) and the intensive active stem (Polel, PSA 109:16).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative active stem) + direct object (person); also Polel (intensive active stem) in PSA 109:16

senses.definition: To be caused to die or be executed, commonly in legal statutes prescribing capital punishment (frequently reinforced by an emphatic infinitive absolute as מוֹת יוּמָת) or in warnings of imminent execution.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hophal (causative passive stem), frequently paired with an emphatic infinitive absolute (מוֹת יוּמָת) in legal decrees

collocations_and_notes: Displays clear voice/causativity distinctions across verbal stems: Qal denotes the intransitive event of dying (often reinforced emphatically by an infinitive absolute + finite verb, מוֹת תָּמוּת "you shall surely die", GEN 2:17, GEN 20:7); Hiphil expresses causing someone's death ("to kill, put to death", e.g., 1SA 19:11, 2SA 4:7); Polel similarly expresses slaying/killing (PSA 109:16); and Hophal expresses the passive of causation ("to be put to death, executed", often paired with an emphatic infinitive absolute as מוֹת יוּמָת in legal penalties, EXO 21:12, LEV 20:27). The Qal participle מֵת serves both predicatively ("is dead / about to die", JER 28:16) and substantively ("a dead person, corpse, the dead", NUM 19:11, ISA 8:19). Frequently contrasted with living (חָיָה / חַיִּים, e.g., 2KI 5:7, ISA 8:19, EZK 33:11) and paired with means of death using בְּ ("by sword, famine, plague", JER 42:17).

core_meaning_summary: A spatial adverb pointing to a previously identified or distinct location, expressing position at, motion toward, or separation from that place ("there", "thither", "from there").

senses.definition: Indicates a stationary location or setting at which someone or something exists, remains, or performs an action, at a place distinct from the speaker's immediate vantage point; usually with the bare form שָׁם, and occasionally with the suffixed form שָׁמָּה in locative contexts.
senses.grammatical_frame: Locative adverb (bare שָׁם, or occasionally suffixed שָׁמָּה) modifying verbs of being, dwelling, placing, or action, or serving as predicate in verbless clauses

senses.definition: Indicates direction or motion toward a previously specified or distant place, typically marked with the directional suffix (-āh) as שָׁמָּה following verbs of going, entering, or arriving.
senses.grammatical_frame: Directional adverb with directional ending (שָׁמָּה) complementing verbs of motion or entry

senses.definition: Marks separation, removal, origin, or vantage point from a specified location, formed with the prefixed preposition מִן ("from") as מִשָּׁם.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional-adverbial compound (מִן + שָׁם = מִשָּׁם) with verbs of departing, taking, bringing out, or observing

senses.definition: Functions as a resumptive spatial marker inside a relative clause introduced by אֲשֶׁר (or correlatively with בַּאֲשֶׁר), linking the antecedent place back to the action or state in the clause ("where", "to which", or "from which" depending on whether bare שָׁם, directional שָׁמָּה, or separative מִשָּׁם is used).
senses.grammatical_frame: Resumptive adverb (שָׁם / שָׁמָּה / מִשָּׁם) inside an אֲשֶׁר relative clause or correlative with בַּאֲשֶׁר

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in three distinct morphological configurations: (1) bare שָׁם for static location ("there"); (2) with the directional suffix ה־ as שָׁמָּה for motion toward a place ("to there, thither"), though occasionally also used for static location (e.g., GEN 23:13, 2SA 21:12); and (3) with prefixed preposition מִן as מִשָּׁם for separation or origin ("from there"). Very commonly used as a resumptive spatial adverb inside relative clauses introduced by אֲשֶׁר ("the place which ... there" = "where") or correlatively with בַּאֲשֶׁר ("where ... there", JDG 5:27). Frequently collocates with verbs of dwelling/sitting (יָשַׁב), placing (שִׂים), burying/hiding, eating, and worshipping, as well as existential/presentative particles like הִנֵּה ("behold, there!", GEN 29:2, EZK 8:14).

core_meaning_summary: Negative particle of non-existence and non-possession ('there is not, no, none, without'), negating nominal, existential, possessive, and participial clauses.

senses.definition: Asserts the non-existence or absence of an entity, condition, or class, or asks whether such does not exist.
senses.grammatical_frame: Absolute form (אַיִן) following a noun or as clause predicate, or construct form (אֵין) preceding a noun, pronoun, or adverb (including interrogative הַאֵין)

senses.definition: Negates possession, share, or accompaniment with respect to a person or entity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct אֵין followed by preposition לְ-, עִם, or אֵת marking the possessor or companion

senses.definition: Negates an ongoing action or state expressed by a participle, either for a specified subject or universally ('there is no one who...').
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct אֵין or pronominal-suffixed form (e.g., אֵינְכֶם) governing a participle, with or without an explicit subject

senses.definition: Expresses the disappearance, death, or total absence of a person or thing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle with pronominal suffix (אֵינֶנִּי, אֵינֶנּוּ, אֵינָם) functioning as the complete predicate of a clause

senses.definition: Marks total lack, limitlessness, or privation as an attributive or prepositional qualifier.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct אֵין following prepositions (לְ-, עַד) or coordinated by וְ as an attributive modifier before a noun

collocations_and_notes: Appears in the absolute state (אַיִן) at clause end or after its subject (GEN 2:5; 1SA 10:14), in the construct state (אֵין) before nouns, participles, or prepositional phrases, and with pronominal suffixes (e.g., אֵינֶנִּי, אֵינֶנּוּ, אֵינָם, אֵינְכֶם). Common constructions include the negation of possession אֵין לְ- ('has no', e.g., NUM 27:9; EST 2:7; LAM 1:2), interrogative הַאֵין ('is there not?', 1KI 22:7; הַאַף אֵין in AMO 2:11), exhaustive negation וְאֵין עוֹד ('and there is no other', ISA 45:18), quantitative/limit phrases עַד אֵין מִסְפָּר ('beyond number', PSA 40:13), and formulaic phrases depicting desolation or helplessness such as וְאֵין מַצִּיל ('with none rescuing', JDG 18:28), וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד ('with none causing fear', LEV 26:6), and וְאֵין שָׁלֹם ('and there is no peace', JER 30:5; EZK 13:16).

core_meaning_summary: Demonstrative and correlative adverb indicating manner, likeness, or conformity ('so, thus, in this way'), also forming prepositional discourse connectives meaning 'therefore' and 'afterward', plus one inflected nominal occurrence meaning 'office/position'.

senses.definition: In this manner or way, referring back to a previously stated action, instruction, or condition; likewise or similarly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Standalone adverb modifying a verb or verbless clause

senses.definition: Correspondingly or in the same manner or degree, introducing the second half of a comparison or proportionality clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Correlative adverb paired with a preceding comparative clause or phrase (כַּאֲשֶׁר, כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר, כְּ-)

senses.definition: For this reason or on account of what was just stated, marking logical consequence, inference, or divine judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound prepositional connective (לָכֵן, עַל־כֵּן, or כִּי עַל־כֵּן) introducing a result or proclamation

senses.definition: After that event or under these circumstances, marking temporal sequence or situational transition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound prepositional phrase with temporal or situational prepositions (אַחֲרֵי כֵן, וּבְכֵן)

senses.definition: An official post, station, or position to which someone is restored.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun governed by preposition עַל with first-person singular suffix (עַל כַּנִּי)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with prepositions to form discourse connectives: לָכֵן ('therefore', e.g., NUM 16:11; ISA 5:24; JER 14:15; EZK 5:11, often introducing prophetic declarations with כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה), עַל־כֵּן ('therefore / for this reason', e.g., 1CH 17:25; JOB 22:10; PSA 45:18; AMO 3:2; HAB 1:4; strengthened as כִּי עַל־כֵּן in JDG 6:22), אַחֲרֵי כֵן ('afterward', GEN 23:19; 2CH 24:4), and וּבְכֵן ('and then / in this situation', EST 4:16). Regularly pairs correlatively with כַּאֲשֶׁר, כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר, or כְּ- ('just as ... so', e.g., EXO 1:12; EXO 40:16; DEU 12:22; JER 5:27; EZK 34:12) and appears in the formulaic affirmation וַיְהִי כֵן ('and it became so', GEN 1:7) and execution formula וַיַּעַשׂ כֵּן ('and he did so', JOS 5:15; NUM 5:4). In GEN 41:13, alongside the adverbial כֵּן הָיָה, the inflected nominal form כַּנִּי ('my office/post') is tagged under this lemma ID in the packet.

core_meaning_summary: To utter a call, cry out, summon, name, proclaim, or read aloud, with a passive/middle usage for being called/summoned or chancing to meet.

senses.definition: To raise one's voice in a loud cry, shout, or vocal call, either absolutely or directed toward someone to gain attention or deliver an utterance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb (Qal), used absolutely, with direct speech, or with אֶל ('to') or בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל ('with a loud voice')

senses.definition: To call upon or cry out to God in prayer, worship, or urgent distress, seeking help or an answer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb (Qal) with divine name as direct object, after אֶל ('to'), in בְּשֵׁם ('in the name of'), or used absolutely in prayer contexts

senses.definition: To summon or invite a person or group to appear or participate; in the passive stem or passive participle, to be summoned or invited.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb (Qal) with לְ or אֶל + person summoned (and passive participle הַקְּרוּאִים 'the invited ones'); passive stem (Niphal) in EST 8:9

senses.definition: To assign a name, title, or descriptive designation to a person, place, or thing; in the passive stem, to be named or called by a name.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb (Qal) with לְ + recipient + name, or with שֵׁם ('name') + name; passive stem (Niphal) in ISA 48:1 and EZK 20:29

senses.definition: To proclaim or declare a public observance (such as a fast), or to read a written document or scroll aloud before listeners.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb (Qal) with direct object denoting an observance (צוֹם) or written text (often with בְּאָזְנֵי 'in the hearing of')

senses.definition: To happen to meet or come unexpectedly before someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/middle stem (Niphal) with לִפְנֵי ('before') + persons encountered

collocations_and_notes: Across the observed verses, the simple active stem (Qal) expresses calling aloud, praying, summoning, naming, and reading aloud, whereas the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) expresses being summoned (EST 8:9), being named or called by a title (ISA 48:1, EZK 20:29), and in one instance happening to encounter someone unexpectedly (2SA 18:9). Common collocations include קָרָא בְשֵׁם ('invoke/call upon the name of', GEN 12:8), קָרָא לְ... ('summon' or 'name X as Y', GEN 1:5, 2KI 4:15), קָרָא אֶל ('call out to / pray to', EXO 19:3, JER 33:3), קָרָא בְקוֹל גָּדוֹל ('shout with a loud voice', 2KI 18:28), and קָרָא בְּאָזְנֵי ('read aloud in the hearing of', 2CH 34:30, JER 36:21). In HOS 11:7 (וְאֶל עַל יִקְרָאֻהוּ), the poetic syntax of the prepositional phrase and pronominal object is concise and somewhat obscure, though the verb still denotes calling or appealing upward.

core_meaning_summary: The cardinal number two, denoting a pair of entities, a component in compound numbers, or a twofold quantity.

senses.definition: Expressing the exact quantity of two items, persons, or groups, either modifying a noun (in construct before or in absolute before/after the noun) or with a plural pronominal suffix denoting both members of a pair.
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral in construct before plural noun, in absolute state modifying noun, or in construct with plural pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Standing independently without an explicit counted noun to denote two individuals, two items, or two occasions, or repeated to express distributive grouping ('two each').
senses.grammatical_frame: Absolute numeral standing substantively as subject, object of preposition, or repeated distributively

senses.definition: Combining with ten ('twelve') or higher multiples of ten ('twenty-two', 'forty-two', etc.) to form compound cardinal or ordinal numerals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral in compound numerical phrase with ten or multiples of ten

senses.definition: Expressing a twofold amount, double restitution, or a double share, either independently as an adverbial/substantive quantity or in construct after פִּי ('portion/measure').
senses.grammatical_frame: Absolute numeral as direct object of restitution verb, or in construct phrase פִּי שְׁנַיִם

collocations_and_notes: Exhibits gender agreement with the counted noun: masculine forms שְׁנַיִם / שְׁנֵי (construct) and feminine forms שְׁתַּיִם / שְׁתֵּי (construct). Frequently takes pronominal suffixes in construct (שְׁנֵיהֶם 'both of them', e.g., EXO 22:8, NUM 25:8, DEU 23:19, PRO 20:10, often reinforced by גַּם 'even both'). Combines with עָשָׂר / עֶשְׂרֵה for 'twelve' (NUM 7:78, JOS 18:24) and with tens for compound numbers (e.g., עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם 'twenty-two', 1KI 16:29). Forms distributive pairs by repetition (שְׁנַיִם שְׁנָיִם 'two by two / two each', 1CH 26:17), the adverbial expression פַּעַם וּשְׁתָּיִם 'once or twice' (NEH 13:20), and the idiom פִּי שְׁנַיִם 'a double portion' (2KI 2:9).

core_meaning_summary: A noun denoting a living creature or human person, physical vitality and life, the inner seat of desire and emotion, or a reflexive personal self.

senses.definition: An animate living creature, whether human or animal, viewed as an embodied living being.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular absolute or construct (e.g., נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, נֶפֶשׁ בְּהֵמָה)

senses.definition: An individual human being or person, especially in legal stipulations, enumerations, or characterizations of moral and social conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular or plural, often with כָּל, demonstrative הַהִוא, or descriptive modifier
senses.semantic_domain: Human Beings / Legal and Social Status

senses.definition: Physical life or mortal existence as something that can be preserved, ransomed, endangered, hunted, struck down, or taken away.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, usually with pronominal suffix or in construct, object of verbs of saving, seeking, striking, or ransoming

senses.definition: The inner seat of appetite, craving, longing, distress, devotion, and emotional responsiveness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with pronominal suffix, subject of verbs of emotion/appetite or governed by prepositions (בְּכָל, לְ)

senses.definition: Personal or reflexive reference equivalent to 'myself', 'herself', 'themselves', or 'me' in self-directed speech, vows, or actions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with pronominal suffix functioning as reflexive pronoun, vocative self-address, or emphatic subject/object

collocations_and_notes: Frequently parallels לֵבָב ('heart'), מְאֹד ('strength/might', 2KI 23:25), עַיִן ('eye'), and בֶּטֶן ('belly', PSA 31:10), showing its role as the holistic inner self or vital center. Common idioms include שִׂים נַפְשׁוֹ בְכַפּוֹ ('put one's life in one's hand', i.e., risk one's life: 1SA 28:21; cf. PSA 119:109), בִּקֵּשׁ אֶת נֶפֶשׁ ('seek someone's life', 1SA 20:1, JER 19:9), מִלֵּט אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ ('deliver one's life', 1KI 1:12, JER 51:45), הִכָּה נָפֶשׁ ('strike fatally', DEU 19:6; cf. LEV 24:18), and כֹּפֶר נֶפֶשׁ ('ransom for a life', EXO 30:12, NUM 35:31). Often occurs in the legal formula וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מֵעַמֶּיהָ ('that person shall be cut off from his people', LEV 7:27, LEV 19:8, NUM 15:30). Plural נְפָשׁוֹת appears in EZK 13:18 and JOS 9:24.

core_meaning_summary: An interrogative pronoun and adverbial particle asking about identity, nature, action, cause, or degree, and functioning in prepositional compounds and rhetorical or indefinite expressions.

senses.definition: Interrogative pronoun asking about the identity, character, content, or action of a thing, event, or situation, functioning as subject, predicate, or direct object in direct questions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative pronoun functioning as subject, nominal predicate, or object of finite verb or לְ + infinitive construct

senses.definition: Interrogative or indefinite pronoun introducing an indirect question or an unspecified event/outcome as the complement of verbs of perception or cognition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial complement after verbs of seeing or knowing (רָאָה, יָדַע)

senses.definition: Interrogative adverbial compound with prepositions (לְ or עַל) asking for the reason, cause, purpose, or basis of an action or state, often carrying a note of reproach or protest.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional compound לָמָּה / לָמָה or עַל מָה / עַל מֶה introducing a clause

senses.definition: Rhetorical or exclamatory marker expressing futility, insufficiency, inability, astonishment at brevity/degree, or disavowal of shared obligation or involvement.
glosses: what have I to do with
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative particle in rhetorical clauses, comparisons, or the formula מַה לִּי וָלָךְ

collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with prepositions to form causal or purposeful interrogatives, most notably לָמָּה / לָמָה (with לְ, 'why?') and עַל מָה / עַל מֶה (with עַל, 'for what reason? / on what basis?'). Often reinforced by the demonstrative זֶה (e.g., לָמָּה זֶּה in GEN 25:32, 1SA 26:18, 2SA 3:24, JER 6:20). Forms the fixed idiomatic expression of disengagement or protest מַה לִּי וָלָךְ ('what [is there] to me and to you?', 1KI 17:18). Also used with infinitive constructs (מַה לַעֲשׂוֹת, EST 6:6, ISA 5:4) and in rhetorical questions that imply negation, futility, or inability (JOB 9:2, JOB 21:15, LAM 2:13). Pointing varies between מָה, מַה (often with dagesh in the following consonant), and מֶה (especially before gutturals or in pause/fixed phrases).

core_meaning_summary: The second-person masculine singular independent personal pronoun ('you'), used as the explicit subject of verbal, nominal, and participial clauses or as a fronted topic.

senses.definition: Serves as the explicit masculine singular subject of a finite verb (perfect, imperfect, or imperative), typically marking emphasis, contrast with another participant, shift of focus, or inclusion in a coordinated compound subject.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent personal pronoun (2ms) as subject of a finite verb

senses.definition: Serves as the subject of a verbless (nominal) or participial clause, identifying or characterizing a masculine singular addressee with a noun phrase, adjective, participle, or prepositional phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent personal pronoun (2ms) as subject of a nominal or participial predicate

senses.definition: Stands at the front of a sentence as an extraposed topic addressing a masculine singular person, whose grammatical role in the main clause is resumed by a second-person pronominal suffix.
senses.grammatical_frame: Extraposed topic (casus pendens) resumed by a 2ms pronominal suffix

collocations_and_notes: Commonly preceded by the conjunction וְ (וְאַתָּה, marking contrast, shift of speaker/actor, or circumstantial background, e.g., GEN 21:26, GEN 32:13, NEH 9:28, ISA 33:1), by כִּי ('for/that you', e.g., GEN 3:11, DEU 31:23, PSA 5:13, JON 4:2), by הִנֵּה ('behold, you', 1SA 8:5, 1SA 28:9), by הֲלֹא in rhetorical questions (PSA 60:12), or by אִם in conditional clauses (EXO 10:4, JDG 7:10, JER 38:21). Frequently paired with vocatives such as יְהוָה, אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה, אֱלֹהִים, אֱלֹהֵינוּ, or בֶן־אָדָם (DEU 3:24, 2SA 7:24, EZR 9:13, EZK 21:11, EZK 43:10), and with לְבַדְּךָ ('you alone', 1KI 8:39). Appears in pausal form אָתָּה in GEN 3:11 and ISA 48:4.

core_meaning_summary: A negative particle used primarily before jussive, cohortative, or imperfect verb forms to express prohibitions, warnings, and negative wishes, with one anomalous interrogative occurrence before a perfect verb.

senses.definition: Negates a second-person jussive or imperfect verb to express a direct prohibition, warning, moral instruction, or urgent plea directed at one or more addressees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negative particle + 2nd-person jussive or imperfect verb (often with נָא)

senses.definition: Negates a third-person jussive or first-person plural cohortative/imperfect verb to express a negative wish, prayer, stipulation, or desired prevention of an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negative particle + 3rd-person jussive or 1st-person plural imperfect verb

senses.definition: Functions before a perfect verb to introduce a question concerning the place or target of a military raid, answered with prepositional phrases specifying locations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative particle + 2nd-person plural perfect verb

collocations_and_notes: Frequently combined with the entreaty particle נָא (אַל־נָא, 'please do not / let there not be', GEN 13:8, GEN 47:29) and often joined by the conjunction וְ (וְאַל, 'and do not / and let not', or contrastive 'but do not' in ISA 6:9). Can occur in a series of prohibitions or negative wishes (PRO 3:11; JER 16:5; JON 3:7), with a preceding subject noun such as אִישׁ to negate an entire group ('let no one', HOS 4:4), or with a preceding vocative (אֱלֹהִים, PSA 71:12; בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, 2CH 13:12). In JOS 22:19, the second occurrence is pointed אֶל in the text alongside the first אַל. In 1SA 27:10, אַל stands anomalously before a perfect verb (פְּשַׁטְתֶּם) in a question that is answered by spatial/target prepositional phrases ('against the Negev of...').

core_meaning_summary: Noun denoting a physical road, route, or journey, and by extension spatial direction, human conduct, or divine standards and dealings.

senses.definition: A physical track, road, highway, or passageway along which people or animals travel or pass.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, often as object of verbs of motion/guarding or governed by the preposition בְּ or עַל

senses.definition: An act of traveling, an expedition, or the spatial distance measured by travel over a specified number of days.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun with pronominal suffix, in construct with a time unit (דֶּרֶךְ יוֹם, דֶּרֶךְ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים), or governed by לְ or בְּ with verbs of going/returning

senses.definition: Spatial orientation, direction toward a destination, or route of entry or passage.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun in construct standing adverbially without a preposition before a place-name or architectural noun

senses.definition: A person's habitual conduct, moral behavior, or chosen course of life, and by extension the deeds for which one is held accountable.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, often with possessive suffixes, moral adjectives (יָשָׁר, רָעָה), or verbs of walking, keeping, mending, or turning away

senses.definition: God's characteristic mode of action and dealings, or the standard of conduct he prescribes for people to follow.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun in construct with the divine name or with divine possessive suffixes, frequently as object of לָלֶכֶת בְּ or יָדַע

collocations_and_notes: Displays variable gender agreement in the sample: modified by masculine adjectives (יָשָׁר in PRO 12:15, PRO 16:25; יְשָׁרִים in HOS 14:10) yet takes feminine pronominal reference in 1SA 9:6 (עָלֶיהָ) and PRO 16:25 (וְאַחֲרִיתָהּ). Frequently paired with verbs of motion (הלך בְּ, עבר בְּ, שוב מִן, בּוֹא) and moral verbs (שׁמר, ידע, ישר, היטיב). Used adverbially without a preposition to denote direction or route ('by way of', 'toward') in DEU 1:19, 2CH 6:34, ISA 15:5, and EZK 46:2. Common collocations include דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ ('the king's highway'), עוֹבְרֵי דָרֶךְ ('travelers on the road'), דֶּרֶךְ יוֹם / דֶּרֶךְ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים (distance of travel), דַּרְכֵי יְהוָה ('the ways of YHWH'), and דַּרְכּוֹ הָרָעָה ('his evil way').

core_meaning_summary: Proclitic interrogative particle prefixed to the opening constituent of a clause to mark yes/no, alternative, or rhetorical questions.

senses.definition: Marks a direct yes/no question asking whether an action occurred, will occur, or whether a state holds true, prefixed to the fronted verb, pronoun, existential particle, or prepositional phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Inseparable proclitic particle prefixed to the first word of a direct verbal, nominal, or existential interrogative clause

senses.definition: Introduces the first member of a two-part disjunctive or alternative question, paired with אִם introducing the second alternative.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic particle in the first clause paired with אִם in the second clause

senses.definition: Introduces a rhetorical or deliberative question expressing disbelief, rebuke, astonishment, or an implied negative answer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic particle prefixed to finite verbs, infinitive absolutes, pronouns, or prepositional phrases in rhetorical clauses

senses.definition: Combines with the negative particle לֹא/לוֹא to frame an assertive rhetorical question expecting an affirmative answer, appealing to shared knowledge or obvious fact.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic particle prefixed directly to לֹא or לוֹא at the head of a clause

senses.definition: Marks an elliptical or indirect interrogative phrase following a verb of perceiving or seizing upon a spoken clue, indicating inquiry as to whether something came from the speaker.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proclitic particle prefixed to a prepositional phrase (הֲמִמֶּנּוּ) functioning as an elliptical complement after a finite verb

collocations_and_notes: Exhibits vowel variation before gutturals or certain prefixes in the sample: standard הֲ (e.g., הֲלֹא, הֲתֵלֵךְ) alternates with הַ (e.g., הַאַתָּה in 1KI 13:14, הַאֵין in 2KI 3:11, הַעַל in NEH 2:19 and ISA 64:11, הַֽעוֹד in RUT 1:11, הַאֲקַדְּמֶנּוּ in MIC 6:6). Frequently combines with לֹא/לוֹא as הֲלֹא/הֲלוֹא to form affirmative rhetorical appeals, and with אִם in alternative questions (הֲ... אִם...). Can attach directly to verbs (finite or infinitive absolute as in JER 7:9 and JER 40:14), pronouns, nouns, particles (רַק, גַּם, עוֹד), and prepositional phrases (הֲמִן in GEN 3:11, הַעַל in NEH 2:19, הֲמִמֶּנּוּ in 1KI 20:33).

core_meaning_summary: To lift up, carry, or transport physical objects, raise one's voice, banner, or gesture, endure moral guilt or disgrace, enter specific idiomatic actions (such as taking a census or showing partiality), and (in the passive stem) be exalted.

senses.definition: To pick up, support, carry, or transport a physical load, object, or person from one place to another, or (with מֵעַל / wind) to sweep or strip something away.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem + direct object (physical item or person), often with locative phrases (עַל, בְּ, מִן, מֵעַל)

senses.definition: To raise something upward as a visible sign, posture, gesture, or inner orientation: hoisting a banner, lifting one's face unashamed, raising one's hand in an oath, or directing one's soul toward God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem + direct object (נֵס, פָּנִים, יָד, נֶפֶשׁ), often with directional prepositions לְ or אֶל

senses.definition: To raise one's voice or begin a loud vocal utterance such as calling out, weeping, or chanting a lament.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem + direct object designating voice or vocal genre (קוֹל, בְּכִי, קִינָה)

senses.definition: To bear the burden, liability, or punitive consequence of guilt, sin, shame, or terror.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem + abstract object of burden or culpability (עָוֺן, חֵטְא, כְּלִמָּה, אֵמִים)

senses.definition: To perform conventionalized social or administrative acts expressed by fixed object pairings: taking a head-count/census (+ רֹאשׁ), taking wives in marriage (+ לְ + נָשִׁים), or showing partiality toward someone (+ פְּנֵי).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem in fixed idiomatic collocations with רֹאשׁ, לְ + נָשִׁים, or פְּנֵי + person

senses.definition: To be lifted high or exalted in status and prominence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal passive/reflexive stem, intransitive, paired with verbs of height and elevation

collocations_and_notes: Exhibits well-defined idiomatic object pairings in the Qal stem: with קוֹל ("voice") or lament terms (בְּכִי, קִינָה) it means to raise a cry or dirge; with נֵס it means to hoist a signal banner; with עָוֺן, חֵטְא, or כְּלִמָּה it means to bear guilt, punishment, or disgrace; with יָד + לְ it expresses raising the hand to swear an oath (EZK 20:15); with רֹאשׁ it means to take a count/census (NUM 31:49); with לְ + נָשִׁים it means to take wives (2CH 13:21); and with פְּנֵי (another's face) it means to show partiality (JOB 34:19), whereas with one's own face (JOB 11:15) it expresses looking up unashamed. In the Niphal stem (ISA 52:13) it expresses being lifted up or exalted alongside verbs of height.

core_meaning_summary: To rise up physically from a lower or resting posture, initiate an action or hostile confrontation, endure or hold valid, and (in causative/intensive stems) erect, rouse, uphold, or ratify.

senses.definition: To change posture by rising from a lying, sitting, sleeping, or fallen position, often contrasted with sitting or lying down or followed by an infinitive expressing purpose.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem, intransitive; often contrasted with verbs of sitting/lying or followed by לְ + infinitive

senses.definition: To bestir oneself to begin a journey, undertaking, or decisive intervention, commonly linked directly with a second verb of motion or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem, intransitive; frequently imperative or narrative sequential form paired with a verb of motion or action

senses.definition: To move aggressively or come forward in opposition against someone, whether in physical assault or legal accusation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem + preposition אֶל, עַל, or בְּ introducing the target; also used as a substantivized participle

senses.definition: To step into a role or position of power in succession to predecessors, or for a state of tumult to break out among a population.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem + תַּחַת (in place of) or עַל (over), or with an event noun as subject

senses.definition: To remain firm, endure, succeed, or hold valid, said of a legal case, kingship, plans, or an agreement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal basic active stem, intransitive with abstract or institutional subjects

senses.definition: To cause a structure to stand upright by assembling or erecting it, or to rouse a resting creature to its feet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil causative stem + direct object (physical structure or animate suffix)

senses.definition: To bring an opponent into active hostility against someone, or to uphold and carry out an authoritative command.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil causative stem + direct object (person in opposition or command)

senses.definition: To confirm, establish, or make an official written directive binding.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel intensive/factitive stem + direct object (official letter/decree)

senses.definition: To set oneself up in active resistance or hostility against someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpolel reflexive/reciprocal stem participle + preposition לְ

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in narrative and commands with verbs of motion such as הָלַךְ ("go"), בָּרַח ("flee"), or שׁוּב ("return") to mark the start of an action or journey. Often contrasted with שָׁכַב ("lie down") or יָשַׁב ("sit"). With אֶל or עַל (and as a substantive participle הַקָּמִים עָלַי) it expresses hostile opposition or attack. In legal and treaty contexts (DEU 19:15; ISA 28:18) it denotes validity or standing firm, while in the causative Hiphil and intensive Piel stems it shifts from intransitive rising to setting up objects, raising adversaries, carrying out commands, or ratifying documents.

core_meaning_summary: A noun denoting the anatomical head of a person and, by extension, the top or upper part of things, a leader or chief, a military unit, a counted sum or principal, the temporal beginning, the choicest quality, or (when paired with wormwood) a bitter toxic plant.

senses.definition: The physical head of a human being, appearing in contexts of blessing, anointing, mourning gestures, execution, protection in battle, and physical discomfort or shelter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun, often in construct or with pronominal suffixes and prepositions (עַל, לְ, בְּ)

senses.definition: The person as the locus of moral accountability, used in judicial and retributive expressions where bloodguilt, conduct, or a wicked scheme returns or is placed upon the perpetrator.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun with pronominal suffix following prepositions עַל or בְּ with verbs of returning or giving (שׁוּב, נָתַן)

senses.definition: The uppermost part, summit, or capital of a physical structure or geographical feature, as well as a branch or stream dividing from a main river.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, often in construct (רֹאשׁ הָהָר) or with suffix referring to architectural elements

senses.definition: A person holding supreme or representative authority over a family, ancestral house, clan, people, military force, or kingdom, as well as a capital city exercising dominance over a territory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, frequently in construct (רָאשֵׁי אָבוֹת, רָאשֵׁי הָעָם, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁלִישִׁים) or as predicate with verbs of appointing (שִׂים, נָתַן)

senses.definition: An organized military detachment, company, or raiding column operating as a distinct unit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun with article and numeral (הָרֹאשׁ אֶחָד) as subject of verb of movement (פָּנָה)

senses.definition: The total head-count or census sum of a population group, or the original principal sum of property owed before an added penalty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun in the census idiom נָשָׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ, or with preposition בְּ in restitution law (שִׁלַּם בְּרֹאשׁוֹ)

senses.definition: The starting point or earliest time in a sequence or in history, contrasted with the end or later generations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun governed by preposition מִן (מֵרֹאשׁ), paired or contrasted with סוֹף ("end") or אַחֲרֹנִים ("last ones")

senses.definition: The highest grade or finest portion of a valuable commodity or trade good.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun in construct before כָּל + commodity noun (בְּרֹאשׁ כָּל בֹּשֶׂם)

senses.definition: A bitter or poisonous plant or substance, paired with wormwood to evoke severe affliction or destructive religious unfaithfulness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun coordinated with לַעֲנָה ("wormwood") as object of bearing (פֹּרֶה) or remembrance

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in construct phrases for clan and civic leadership (רָאשֵׁי אָבוֹת / רָאשֵׁי הָאָבוֹת, "heads of ancestral houses"; רָאשֵׁי הָעָם, "heads of the people"). Idiomatic verbal expressions include נָשָׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ ("take a count/census", NUM 4:22, NUM 31:49), הֵרִים רֹאשׁ ("lift up [someone's] head", restoring honor/confidence, PSA 3:4), הֵנִיד בְּרֹאשׁ ("shake/wag the head" in shock or derision, JER 18:16), and returning/placing blood, conduct, or plots עַל רֹאשׁ / בְּרֹאשׁ ("upon the head" of the responsible person, 1KI 2:32, 1KI 8:32, EST 9:25, EZK 11:21). In DEU 29:17 and LAM 3:19, רֹאשׁ is paired with לַעֲנָה ("wormwood") to denote a bitter or toxic plant/substance; although identically pointed in the text, this usage is semantically distinct from the "head/top/chief" cluster.

core_meaning_summary: Feminine singular proximal demonstrative pronoun and adjective referring to a nearby or contextually salient feminine entity, object, statement, event, or situation ("this", "this one").

senses.definition: Demonstrative adjective modifying a definite feminine singular noun (and any accompanying attributive adjective), identifying a specific nearby or contextually highlighted entity, place, or object.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive feminine singular demonstrative with definite article following a definite feminine singular noun (הַ + noun + הַזֹּאת)

senses.definition: Independent pronoun pointing to a specific feminine person, geographical boundary, or body of instruction/law, often serving as the subject of a verbless identification clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent feminine singular pronoun as subject, predicate, or prepositional object referring to a feminine noun or person

senses.definition: Independent pronoun referring abstractly to an action, deed, situation, proclamation, or regulation—either previously stated or immediately following in the discourse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun functioning as verbal subject or direct object without a feminine noun antecedent

senses.definition: Independent pronoun governed by a preposition to express means, reason, circumstance, or subsequent time in relation to a preceding or following event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase (בְּזֹאת, לָזֹאת, עַל זֹאת, אַחֲרֵי זֹאת, בְּכָל זֹאת)

collocations_and_notes: Commonly follows a definite feminine singular noun (with הַ prefixed to both noun and demonstrative: הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת, הָעִיר הַזֹּאת, הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת) or stands alone as a feminine/neuter-like pronoun. Frequent verbal collocations include עָשָׂה זֹאת ("to do this", e.g., GEN 20:6, GEN 44:17, LEV 26:16, 2CH 25:16, ISA 9:6) and interrogative מַה זֹּאת עֲשִׂיתֶם ("what is this you have done?", JDG 2:2). Frequently introduces legal/instructional summaries (זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה, זֹאת חֻקַּת הַתּוֹרָה, וְזֹאת הַמִּצְוָה) and forms prepositional connectors such as בְּזֹאת ("by this"), עַל זֹאת ("concerning/because of this"), בְּכָל זֹאת ("in all this"), and אַחֲרֵי זֹאת ("after this").

core_meaning_summary: The cardinal numeral three (with its plural form thirty), used to quantify items, form higher compound numbers, mark ordinal years, and designate specific numbered military groups.

senses.definition: The basic cardinal quantity three, used both independently and as an element in compound numbers (such as thirteen, twenty-three, three hundred, and three thousand).
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral preceding or following a noun in apposition (שָׁלֹשׁ, שְׁלֹשָׁה), in construct before plural nouns or larger unit words (שְׁלֹשׁ, שְׁלֹשֶׁת), or with pronominal suffixes (שְׁלָשְׁתְּכֶם, שְׁלֹשְׁתָּם)

senses.definition: Cardinal form functioning ordinally in chronological and regnal date formulas to specify the third or thirteenth year.
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral in construct chain following שְׁנַת or governed by מִן in date expressions (שְׁנַת שָׁלוֹשׁ; מִן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה)

senses.definition: The plural-form cardinal numeral thirty, occurring alone, in compound numbers, and in regnal or chronological date formulas.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form numeral (שְׁלֹשִׁים) standing before singular or plural nouns, combined with units or hundreds/thousands, or in construct date phrases (שְׁנַת שְׁלֹשִׁים וּשְׁמֹנֶה)

senses.definition: Substantivized definite numeral designating a recognized rank or corps of elite warriors ("the Three" or "the Thirty").
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral with definite article or in apposition to הַגִּבֹּרִים, governed by prepositions בְּ or עַל

collocations_and_notes: Displays reverse gender agreement in the base cardinal: masculine-marked שְׁלֹשָׁה / שְׁלוֹשָׁה (construct שְׁלֹשֶׁת) pairs with masculine nouns (e.g., שְׁלֹשָׁה בָנִים, שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים, שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים), whereas unmarked שָׁלֹשׁ / שָׁלוֹשׁ (construct שְׁלֹשׁ) pairs with feminine nouns (e.g., שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת). Suffixed forms take the base שְׁלָשְׁתּ־ / שְׁלֹשְׁתּ־ (שְׁלָשְׁתְּכֶם, שְׁלֹשְׁתָּם). Frequently forms compound numerals with ten (שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, thirteen), hundreds (שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת, three hundred), thousands (שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים, three thousand), and multiples via the plural form שְׁלֹשִׁים (thirty). Appears in the graded numerical sequence עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה ... וְעַל אַרְבָּעָה in AMO 1:6.

core_meaning_summary: Water as a physical liquid substance, encompassing natural bodies and sources, water used for drinking and washing, and figurative expressions of peril, vitality, or instability.

senses.definition: Water forming natural terrestrial, subterranean, or atmospheric bodies, including seas, rivers, floodwaters, springs, pools, cisterns, and rain-clouds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun (absolute מַיִם, construct מֵי, suffixed מֵימ־); subject of verbs of motion/state, object of prepositions (בְּ, עַל, אֶל, לְ), or in construct chains with topographical terms

senses.definition: Potable water drawn, stored, given, or consumed for drinking and physical survival, often paired with bread as a basic necessity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun as object of verbs of drinking, drawing, giving, or lacking (שָׁתָה, הִשְׁקָה, שָׁאַב, נָתַן, אֵין), or in construct with containers and provisions (צַפַּחַת, מִשְׁעַן)

senses.definition: Water used for physical washing, bathing, ritual purification, judicial ordeal, or cultic pouring.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun governed by instrumental/locative בְּ with verbs of washing, dipping, or cleansing (רָחַץ, כִּבֵּס, טָבַל), or as subject/object in ritual actions

senses.definition: Water used figuratively to depict overwhelming peril, swift transience, deep/abundant speech, or physical collapse from terror.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun in metaphorical predicates, prepositional phrases (עַל פְּנֵי מַיִם), or adverbial/result expressions (תֵּלַכְנָה מָּיִם)

collocations_and_notes: Always appears with plural morphology and takes plural verb and pronominal agreement (e.g., הָיוּ, חָרְבוּ, יָשֻׁבוּ, יָצְאוּ, לִשְׁתּוֹתָם, אֹתָם). Occurs in construct as מֵי (e.g., מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, מֵי הַיַּרְדֵּן, מֵי מְרִיבָה) and with pronominal suffixes on the reduplicated stem מֵימ־ (מֵימֶיהָ, מֵימֵינוּ, מֵימֵיהֶם). Common collocations include פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם (surface of the water), מַעְיְנֵי/מַבּוּעֵי/נַחֲלֵי מַיִם (springs/streams of water), לֶחֶם וּמַיִם (bread and water), and רָחַץ בַּמַּיִם (wash/bathe in water).

core_meaning_summary: Humankind collectively or an individual human being, including the construct idiom for a mortal human and the personal name of the first man.

senses.definition: Human beings considered collectively as a species or population, especially in contrast to animals or to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular used collectively with or without the definite article; takes plural or singular verb agreement according to context, and appears in construct as a modifier (e.g., human hands, human foot).

senses.definition: An individual human being or any person in general, including a specific single human figure when determined by context or the definite article.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular functioning as an indefinite or definite singular subject, object, or genitive modifier (e.g., a person's bone), often paired with singular verbs and pronouns.

senses.definition: A mortal human being, occurring in the construct expression 'son of humankind / children of humankind', used both generally for mortals and as a direct form of address to a prophet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular as the second element in the construct phrase בֶּן אָדָם (singular) or בְּנֵי אָדָם (plural), used as a noun phrase or standalone vocative.

senses.definition: Adam, the proper name of the first human ancestor in genealogical and historical reference.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun masculine without article, functioning as the named ancestor in a genealogical heading (or in comparison with a named figure).

collocations_and_notes: Invariably singular in form (never takes a plural suffix); functions both as a collective noun for humankind and as an indefinite singular for a person. Frequently paired or contrasted with בְּהֵמָה (livestock/beasts: GEN 7:21; EXO 9:9; NUM 8:17; NUM 31:11; JER 32:43; EZK 32:13) and with אֵל (God/deity: ISA 31:3; EZK 28:2) to underscore human mortality and non-divine status. In the construct phrase בֶּן אָדָם / בְּנֵי אָדָם, it designates mortal humans generally or serves as a direct vocative to Ezekiel. In HOS 6:7 (כְּאָדָם), context allows either comparison to humankind generally or to the individual Adam.

core_meaning_summary: A prominent elevated landform such as a mountain, hill, or highland region, often serving as a geographical landmark, regional territory, or sacred site.

senses.definition: A distinct elevated natural landform rising steeply above the surrounding terrain, whether a single peak, named mountain, or hill.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine, singular or plural, absolute or construct with a proper name (e.g., Mount Sinai, Mount Hor) or modified by adjectives such as high; often governed by spatial prepositions (on, to, from, in).

senses.definition: An extended mountainous area, mountain range, or upland territory inhabited or named as a geographical district, often contrasted with valleys, lowlands, or plains.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular or plural, frequently in construct before a territorial or tribal name (e.g., Gilead, Ephraim, Seir, Samaria, Israel) or listed alongside regional terrain zones.

senses.definition: A mountain designated as a sacred place of divine presence, worship, or pilgrimage (especially Zion/Jerusalem), and by poetic extension an emblem of God-given stability.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular, typically in construct with divine, cultic, or Zion-related nouns (e.g., mountain of God, mountain of the house of the LORD, holy mountain) or with first-person pronominal suffix.

collocations_and_notes: Occurs in singular (הַר), plural (הָרִים), construct plural (הָרֵי), and suffixed poetic stem form הַרְרִי (PSA 30:8). Common construct expressions include הַר סִינַי (Mount Sinai: EXO 19:23; EXO 31:18; LEV 7:38; NEH 9:13), הַר שֵׂעִיר (Mount/hill country of Seir: DEU 2:1; EZK 35:15), הַר אֶפְרַיִם (hill country of Ephraim: JDG 2:9; JDG 19:16; 2KI 5:22), רֹאשׁ הָהָר / רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים (summit/tops of the mountain[s]: JOS 15:8; JDG 9:25; ISA 2:2; ISA 30:17; EZK 6:13; MIC 4:1), הַר בֵּית יְהוָה (mountain of the house of the LORD: ISA 2:2; MIC 4:1), and הַר קָדְשִׁי / הַר הַקֹּדֶשׁ (holy mountain: ISA 66:20; JER 31:23; ZEP 3:11). Often paired or contrasted with other terrain terms such as גִּבְעָה (hill), בִּקְעָה (valley), שְׁפֵלָה (lowland), עֲרָבָה (plain), and נֶגֶב (southern steppe). In PSA 30:8, הַרְרִי is used metaphorically for secure standing or stability granted by God.

core_meaning_summary: To cross over a barrier or waterway, travel through or pass by, overflow, elapse or perish, violate or overlook a norm, or (in causative and reflexive stems) bring across, proclaim, or erupt in anger.

senses.definition: To move from one side of a river, wadi, sea, boundary, or ritual division to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active); transitive with direct object of the waterway/barrier, or intransitive with `אֶל` (into/to), `בְּ` (across), or `בֵּין` (between)

senses.definition: To travel through a territory or city, pass by or ahead of someone, outrun another runner, or (of a territorial boundary) run along and extend from one point to another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active); intransitive with `בְּ` / `בְּתוֹךְ` / `בְּקֶרֶב` (through), `עַל` / `עַל־פְּנֵי` (by/before), or `מֵאֵת` (from); transitive when overtaking a person

senses.definition: To surge over or sweep irresistibly through, used of floodwaters or a metaphorical overwhelming calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with `עַל` (over)

senses.definition: To go by or come to an end (of a time of day or agricultural season), or to pass away and perish (of mortal life).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with `בְּ` indicating the instrument of death

senses.definition: To step beyond and violate a binding covenant, or conversely to pass over and disregard an offense without retaliation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active); transitive with `בְּרִית` (covenant) for violating, or intransitive with `עַל` (over) + `פֶּשַׁע` (offense) for forgiving/overlooking

senses.definition: To cause something or someone to pass across or through: to make wind blow over the earth, escort or guide someone across water or through provinces, carry a horn blast throughout a country, or hand over children as a ritual offering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), transitive with direct object (`אֵת` or suffix); with prepositions `עַל` (over), `בְּ` (through/across), or `לְ` (to)

senses.definition: To overflow with anger or become enraged (parallel to fire kindling and wrath rising).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael (reflexive/intensive), intransitive; absolute

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with `לִפְנֵי` (before/ahead of), `בְּתוֹךְ` / `בְּקֶרֶב` (through the midst of), `עַל` (over/by), and direct objects of waterways or barriers (`הַיַּרְדֵּן`, `נַחַל`). Stem distinctions: Qal expresses active crossing, passing, overflowing, elapsing, or transgressing; Hiphil expresses causing to pass/blow, escorting across, proclaiming by horn throughout a land, or ritually handing over children; Hithpael (attested in PSA 78:21) expresses overflowing with anger/becoming enraged.

core_meaning_summary: Large in physical size or number, intense in degree or severity, or exalted in rank, authority, and majesty.

senses.definition: Large in physical dimensions, spaciousness, weight, or numerical size, applied to objects, structures, cities, animals, or large groups of people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective (including construct with body part, e.g., גְּדוֹל כְּנָפַיִם)

senses.definition: High in degree, intensity, abundance, or gravity, describing sounds, rain, emotions, calamities, battles, loyal kindness, or grave offenses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective modifying event or abstract nouns, often intensifying cognate nouns

senses.definition: Exalted in status, wealth, power, or authority, used of God, monarchs, prominent individuals, and the chief priest.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective (sometimes comparative with מִן, or in the fixed title הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל)

senses.definition: Used as a noun for older or higher-ranking persons (in paired contrast with 'small'), or in the feminine for major matters and mighty deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adjective (masculine singular for persons in merisms with קָטֹן; feminine singular or plural for deeds or matters)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with קָטֹן / קְטַנָּה ('small, young, junior', e.g., GEN 1:16, GEN 19:11, NUM 22:18, DEU 25:13, 2CH 31:15, EST 1:5, AMO 6:11), where merisms like מִקָּטֹן וְעַד גָּדוֹל express totality across age or social rank. Often combined with רַב ('many, great', DEU 2:21) or גִּבּוֹר / נוֹרָא ('mighty, awesome', NEH 1:5, JER 32:18). Forms the official title הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל ('the high priest', 2KI 22:4) and cognate intensity phrases with nouns of emotion or outcry (תְּרוּעָה גְדוֹלָה, JOS 6:5; שִׂמְחָה גְדוֹלָה, NEH 8:17, JON 4:6; קִנְאָה גְדוֹלָה, ZEC 1:14). Appears in construct with a body part to express size (גְּדוֹל כְּנָפַיִם, 'large-winged', EZK 17:7).

core_meaning_summary: To take or maintain an upright or stationary position, stop moving, serve in attendance, withstand opposition, or (in the causative stem) station and appoint others.

senses.definition: To take or maintain an upright posture or stationary spatial position (used of people, feet, waters, or upright structures), often accompanied by a prepositional phrase specifying location.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with prepositions (`עַל` upon/beside, `בְּ` in/at, `אֵצֶל` beside, `לְנֶגֶד` opposite)

senses.definition: To cease moving, come to a halt, stay behind, or remain abiding in a place or course of conduct (including non-physical persistence such as lingering in a way of life, persisting in practices, or a spirit remaining among a community).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with `תַּחַת` (in one's place), `מֵרָחוֹק` (at a distance), `אֵת` (with), or `בְּ` (in)

senses.definition: To stand in attendance before a ruler, superior, or deity in service, cultic ministry, or intercession, or to step into an office in someone's place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; typically with `לִפְנֵי` (before), `עַל` (in attendance upon / at one's post), or `תַּחַת` (in place of)

senses.definition: To take a hostile stand against someone in battle, or to hold one's ground and withstand an attacker's assault.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; with `עַל` (against) or `לִפְנֵי` (before), often negated with `לֹא` or `אֵין כֹּחַ` (no strength to)

senses.definition: To cause someone or a group to stand in a designated place, present a person before an authority or deity, station military guards or choirs, or appoint officials to a role.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), transitive with direct object (`אֵת` or pronominal suffix); often with `לִפְנֵי` (before) or `לְ` (for/as)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with prepositions indicating spatial orientation or social hierarchy: `לִפְנֵי` (before, in service, appearance, or opposition), `עַל` (beside, upon, or against), `תַּחַת` (in one's place, including succession), and `אֵצֶל` / `לְנֶגֶד` (beside / opposite). The idiomatic phrase `עָמַד עַל עָמְדָם` (2CH 30:16) denotes taking one's appointed station. Contrasts between stems: Qal is intransitive/stative (standing, halting, attending, resisting), while Hiphil is causative (making someone stand, stationing personnel, or appointing officials).

core_meaning_summary: Good, pleasant, or desirable in quality, character, or benefit, used across physical, aesthetic, ethical, and advantageous contexts.

senses.definition: Possessing high quality, fertility, beauty, or pleasantness, applied to created things, land, produce, fragrance, or personal appearance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective (including construct before nouns of appearance such as תֹּאַר and מַרְאֶה)

senses.definition: Morally upright, faithful, or benevolently gracious, characterizing divine disposition and action or human conduct acceptable to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective, often with prepositional phrases (לְ, לִפְנֵי, עַל)

senses.definition: Beneficial, fitting, acceptable, or preferable in someone's estimation or experience, including comparative superiority over something else.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative adjective with לְ ('for'), בְּעֵינֵי ('in the eyes of'), or מִן ('than' in comparisons)

senses.definition: Used as a noun for what is morally right, advantageous, prosperous, or glad tidings (singular), or for upright and virtuous people (plural).
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adjective (singular abstract or masculine plural for persons), often object of verbs of doing, speaking, or seeking

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with רַע / רָעָה ('evil, bad, harmful', e.g., GEN 3:5, GEN 26:29, NUM 13:19, JOS 23:15, JOB 30:26, PSA 34:15, JER 24:2) and in parallel with נָעִים ('pleasant', GEN 49:15), צַדִּיקִים ('righteous', PRO 2:20), and שָׁלוֹם / יְשׁוּעָה ('peace, deliverance', ISA 52:7). Common idioms include טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי ('pleasing/right in the eyes of', 1SA 29:9, 2SA 15:26, 1CH 21:23, EST 8:8), טוֹב לְפָנָיו ('acceptable before him [God]', ECC 2:26, ECC 7:26), דִּבֶּר בְּ... טוֹב ('speak favorably about', 1SA 19:4), and comparative טוֹב ... מִן ('better than', PSA 63:4, PSA 119:72, PRO 16:8, JON 4:3). Appears in construct with aspect nouns for physical appearance (טוֹב תֹּאַר, 1KI 1:6; טוֹבוֹת מַרְאֶה, EST 2:2).

core_meaning_summary: A spatial and relational preposition indicating a position beneath or below something, subordination under authority, or substitution and exchange in place of something else.

senses.definition: At or into a lower spatial position relative to a person, object, sky, or structure; includes compound forms indicating location below or motion beneath, as well as the idiom 'under the sun' for the earthly realm and suffixed forms meaning 'in one's spot / without moving'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing nouns or pronominal suffixes; also in compound expressions מִתַּחַת (לְ) and אֶל תַּחַת (לְ)

senses.definition: Under the authority, control, domination, or immediate disposal of someone, regularly paired with יָד ('hand') or verbs of subjugation and deliverance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition with יָד ('hand') or pronominal suffix, following verbs of subduing, delivering, or possessing

senses.definition: In place of, as a successor to, or in exchange, compensation, or recompense for another person, object, injury, or condition; used especially in royal succession formulas, legal restitution, and reversals of state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun or pronominal suffix, often with verbs of reigning, repaying, giving, or becoming

senses.definition: Used with a following relative marker to introduce a causal or retributive clause explaining the ground for a restriction or action.
glosses: in return for the fact that
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound conjunction תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר + finite clause

collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with preceding prepositions such as מִן (מִתַּחַת, מִתַּחַת לְ 'from under, beneath, below') and אֶל (אֶל תַּחַת, אֶל תַּחַת לְ 'to underneath'). Recurring idiomatic expressions include תַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ ('under the sun', denoting the earthly mortal sphere in Ecclesiastes), תַּחַת יַד ('under the hand/control/power of', or 'on hand / in one's possession'), יָשַׁב תַּחְתָּו ('stay in one's place'), and מָלַךְ תַּחַת ('reign in place of / succeed as king').

core_meaning_summary: To move from one place to another on foot or by flow, and figuratively to conduct one's life, follow a way or allegiance, or progress continuously.

senses.definition: To move physically from place to place, travel along a route, depart, come toward someone, accompany, or traverse an area; used in the simple active stem for general movement, in the intensive/iterative stem for going about persistently or as a roving traveler, and in the reflexive/iterative stem for traversing territory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intensive/iterative stem (Piel), and reflexive/iterative stem (Hithpael); intransitive or with prepositions (אֶל, עַל, אֵת, מִפְּנֵי, לְ, בְּ) or direct object of path/way

senses.definition: Of water, wine, news, or inner attention/beings: to flow along a course, spread abroad, pass smoothly, attend in thought, or pass onward to a final destination such as death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), with inanimate or abstract subjects (river, water, wine, fame, heart, all beings)

senses.definition: To conduct one's life, behave habitually, or maintain religious and moral allegiance; commonly framed as walking before God or people, walking in someone's ways or statutes, going after other gods, or going about as a slanderer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) and reflexive/iterative stem (Hithpael); with prepositions לִפְנֵי ('before'), בְּ ('in'), אַחֲרֵי ('after'), or nominal complement רָכִיל ('slander')

senses.definition: Used as a progressive auxiliary paired with a following adjective or participle to express steady, continuous increase or intensification in a condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem participle (הוֹלֵךְ) followed by וְ + adjective or participle

collocations_and_notes: Across the sampled verses, three verbal stems appear: (1) the simple active stem (Qal), used for basic locomotion, spatial flow, figurative conduct, and the progressive auxiliary construction הֹלֵךְ וְ־ + adjective/participle indicating steady increase (2SA 3:1; EST 9:4); (2) the intensive/iterative stem (Piel), used for going about persistently in a condition such as mourning (JOB 30:28) or as an agent noun for a traveler/rover (PRO 6:11); and (3) the reflexive/iterative stem (Hithpael), used for walking about or surveying an area (JOS 18:4) and especially for habitual conduct or living faithfully before God or the community (GEN 17:1; 1SA 2:35; 1SA 12:2; PSA 35:14; PSA 82:5; ISA 38:3). Common collocations include הָלַךְ לְדַרְכּוֹ ('go on one's way'), הָלַךְ אַחֲרֵי ('follow after' another deity), הָלַךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ / בְּחֻקּוֹת ('live according to a way/statutes'), הָלַךְ לִפְנֵי ('live/serve before' God or people), הָלַךְ רָכִיל ('go about slandering'), and הֹלֵךְ הָלוֹךְ וְ־ ('continue going and...' for ongoing action, JER 41:6).

core_meaning_summary: An audible voice, sound, noise, cry, thunderclap, or public report/proclamation, also used idiomatically with 'hear' to express obedience or compliance.

senses.definition: The audible speaking voice or vocal utterance of a human being or deity, including cries of distress, weeping, joyful shouting, or prayer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often in construct (קוֹל + speaker or emotion), with prepositional בְּ/לְ, or as object of נָשָׂא / נָתַן / שָׁמַע

senses.definition: In combination with the verb שָׁמַע ('listen') and בְּ or לְ, the spoken command, counsel, or plea to which one responds with obedience, compliance, or favorable consent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun governed by שָׁמַע בְּ־ / שָׁמַע לְ־ + speaker

senses.definition: Any non-speech audible sound or noise, such as footsteps, bells, horns, millstones, crowds, wings, rushing water, crashing structures, or animal calls.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, typically in construct (קוֹל + sound source) or as object of שָׁמַע / נָשָׂא

senses.definition: Thunder or a booming atmospheric rumble, especially in the plural (קֹלוֹת) alongside rain or in descriptions of divine manifestation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (קֹלוֹת) or singular construct referring to divine meteorological roaring

senses.definition: Spoken news or rumor circulating in a household, or an official oral proclamation issued throughout a kingdom.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun as subject of passive נִשְׁמַע (be heard) or object of causative הֶעֱבִיר (circulate)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs with the verb שָׁמַע ('hear, listen'): with direct object (שָׁמַע אֶת קוֹל) it normally denotes perceiving a sound or hearing a plea, whereas with the prepositions בְּ or לְ (שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל / לְקוֹל) it consistently denotes heeding, obeying, or granting someone's request. Other recurring idioms include נָשָׂא קוֹל ('raise one's voice', JOB 2:12; PSA 93:3), נָתַן קוֹל ('utter a cry/voice', JER 48:34), בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל ('in a loud voice', PRO 27:14), and הֶעֱבִיר קוֹל ('circulate a proclamation', 2CH 36:22).

core_meaning_summary: To strike, beat, hit, or fatally smite a person, animal, object, or military force, spanning physical blows, lethal violence, battlefield defeat, and divine or natural affliction.

senses.definition: To deliver physical blows to or beat a person, whether in assault, corporal punishment of a servant, or judicial flogging, without inherently causing immediate death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (person) or partitive מִן, optionally with instrumental בְּ (with)

senses.definition: To strike or hit an inanimate object (such as rock, water, or an architectural structure) with an implement or hand; with כַּף ('palm/hand') as object, to clap or strike one's hand in an expressive gesture of anger.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (inanimate object or body part), optionally with instrumental בְּ or directional אֶל

senses.definition: To strike a fatal blow to, slay, assassinate, or execute an individual human or wild animal; in the simple passive/middle (Niphal) and causative passive (Hophal) stems, to be fatally wounded or struck down.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (person or animal); passive in simple passive/middle stem (Niphal) or causative passive stem (Hophal)

senses.definition: To defeat, attack, capture, or slaughter opposing armies, rulers, cities, or territories in warfare, often paired with לְפִי חֶרֶב ('at the edge of the sword') or with a cognate noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (army, king, people, city, or land), or with בְּ / partitive מִן

senses.definition: To devastate, discipline, blight, or kill people, livestock, or vegetation through severe weather or divine judgment; in the causative passive stem (Hophal), to be blighted or withered.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) with natural force or deity as subject; causative passive stem (Hophal) in figurative comparison

senses.definition: In an idiom with לֵב ('heart') as subject, to strike someone internally with remorse or pangs of conscience.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) with לֵב (heart) as subject + direct object (person)

collocations_and_notes: In the sampled corpus, active forms occur exclusively in the causative active stem (Hiphil), while passive counterparts occur in the simple passive/middle stem (Niphal, 2SA 11:15) and the causative passive stem (Hophal, NUM 25:18; PSA 102:5). Frequent collocations include instrumental בְּ (e.g., בַּשֵּׁבֶט 'with a rod', EXO 21:20; בְּמַטֵּהוּ 'with his staff', NUM 20:11), לְפִי חֶרֶב ('by the edge of the sword', JOS 10:32; 2KI 10:25), cognate accusative מַכָּה גְדוֹלָה ('a great blow/defeat', 1SA 19:8; 1KI 20:21), and partitive מִן indicating casualties out of a larger group (JOS 7:5; JDG 20:45; NEH 13:25). In 2SA 24:10, לֵב ('heart') serves as the subject of the verb in an idiom for feeling guilt. In EZK 22:13, הִכֵּיתִי כַפִּי ('I struck my palm') expresses indignation.

core_meaning_summary: An adverb indicating continuation ('still, yet'), repetition or addition ('again, further'), or, when paired with negation or rhetorical questions, cessation ('no longer, no more').

senses.definition: Indicates the repetition of an action, a renewed future occurrence, or something additional beyond what already exists.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs or interrogative clauses

senses.definition: Indicates the ongoing persistence of a state, existence, or simultaneous action at the time of reference.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb in nominal/participial clauses or with pronominal suffix (עוֹדֶנּוּ)

senses.definition: With negative particles (לֹא, אֵין, oath אִם) or in rhetorical questions, marks the end, absence, or non-recurrence of a state or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb following negation (לֹא / אֵין / אִם) or in rhetorical questions

senses.definition: In the phrase כָּל עוֹד, expresses the entire duration during which a condition continues to hold.
senses.grammatical_frame: Conjunctional phrase (כָּל עוֹד) introducing a temporal/conditional clause

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in negative constructions with לֹא, אֵין, or the oath particle אִם, often paired with the auxiliary verb יָסַף ('do again/continue', e.g., 2SA 2:28; 2KI 6:23; PSA 77:8; ISA 10:20; ISA 52:1; HOS 1:6) to express 'no longer / never again'. Takes pronominal suffixes when indicating ongoing state in nominal or participial clauses (עוֹדֶנּוּ, GEN 18:22; NUM 11:33). Also combines with כָּל in כָּל עוֹד to mean 'as long as' (JOB 27:3).

core_meaning_summary: Encompasses both a Qal verb meaning to tend, pasture, or graze livestock (and figuratively to shepherd or govern people) and a feminine noun denoting moral wickedness, harm, distress, or disaster.

senses.definition: To tend, pasture, or feed a flock or herd; also used reflexively/critically of leaders feeding themselves rather than the flock.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb (transitive with direct object)

senses.definition: Of animals (flocks, cattle, donkeys, gazelles), to graze or browse in pasture or among vegetation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb (intransitive)

senses.definition: Figuratively, to shepherd, guide, care for, or rule over a people (applied to kings or God); also extended to agricultural produce nourishing people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb (transitive, metaphorical)

senses.definition: One who tends flocks; frequently used metaphorically for a ruler, political leader, or God as protector and guide of Israel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active participle (used substantively, singular and plural)

senses.definition: Moral wrong, wickedness, or an evil deed committed by individuals, leaders, or a nation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular, construct, and plural)

senses.definition: Harm, danger, distress, misfortune, or calamity experienced by people or brought upon a community as judgment or hostility.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (often with prepositions לְ / בְּ or as object of verbs like הֵבִיא)

collocations_and_notes: The evidence packet groups two distinct but homographic lexical usages under this lemma: (1) a Qal verb meaning to tend/graze/shepherd (with its participle functioning substantively as 'shepherd' or figuratively 'leader/ruler', e.g., EZK 34:2, 10, 23; MIC 5:4; PSA 80:2), and (2) a feminine noun denoting moral evil/wickedness or harm/calamity. Common nominal expressions include בְּיוֹם רָעָה / לְיוֹם רָעָה ('in/for the day of disaster', PSA 41:2; PRO 16:4), הֵבִיא רָעָה עַל ('bring disaster upon', 1KI 21:29; JER 19:3; JER 23:12; JER 49:37), לְרָעָה ('for harm/calamity', JDG 2:15; 2SA 18:32; JER 28:8), and contrast with שָׁלוֹם ('peace/welfare', JER 38:4). In the plural (רָעוֹת), it denotes either wicked deeds (JER 3:5; JER 44:9; EZK 6:9) or experienced calamities (1SA 10:19, paired with צָרוֹת 'distresses').

core_meaning_summary: Many, numerous, great, or abundant in number, extent, or degree; also used substantively for a multitude, predicatively for "enough," and in construct as a title meaning "chief" (as well as in the city name Rabbah).

senses.definition: Large in number; consisting of many individuals, items, occurrences, or units of time, modifying plural nouns or collective singular nouns.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, attributive or predicative, plural or singular with collective nouns

senses.definition: Large in extent, volume, intensity, or degree, modifying mass nouns, abstract qualities, wealth, crowds, or waters.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective (attributive, predicative, or construct before a noun), singular or plural with מַיִם

senses.definition: A large number of people, a crowd, or the majority/multitude.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive plural adjective, with or without the definite article

senses.definition: Sufficient or enough, used as an exclamation or predicate indicating that no more is needed or that an action should cease.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative/exclamatory singular adjective at clause start

senses.definition: High-ranking leader, commander, or chief officer over a group of subordinates.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct singular noun preceding a plural noun (רַב טַבָּחִים)

senses.definition: Proper geographic name (Rabbah), designating the capital city of the Ammonites when in construct with בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular construct form (רַבַּת) in a place name

collocations_and_notes: Frequently modifies countable plural nouns such as יָמִים ("days"), עַמִּים ("peoples"), גּוֹיִם ("nations"), and מַיִם ("waters," conveying abundance or mighty volume), as well as collective singular nouns like עַם ("people"), גּוֹי ("nation"), and עֵץ ("trees"). In construct with a plural noun of functionaries (רַב טַבָּחִים), it denotes an official title ("chief of the guard"). In DEU 3:11 and 2SA 17:27, the feminine singular construct form רַבַּת appears as the place name Rabbah (רַבַּת בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן, "Rabbah of the Ammonites"), which is grouped under this lemma in the corpus. Note also the elliptical feminine plural רָאוֹת רַבּוֹת ("seeing many things," ISA 42:20).
