core_meaning_summary: Sacredness or consecrated status belonging to God, also designating holy places, consecrated objects or offerings, and in superlative constructions the innermost sanctuary or most sacred things.

senses.definition: The state or status of being sacred, consecrated, and set apart to God, predicated of persons (priests, Levites), days (Sabbath), consecrated animals, sacrificial portions, vessels, land, or dedicated wealth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun as predicate or subject with הָיָה / verbless clause (often with לַיהוָה)

senses.definition: Used as the second element in a construct chain to qualify a preceding noun as belonging to the divine or cultic realm—such as ground, garments, temple vessels, standard weights, dwelling, mountain, throne, spirit, name, words, or covenant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun (absolute or with pronominal suffix) as nomen rectum in construct chain

senses.definition: With the definite article, the consecrated precinct or sanctuary where cultic service and libations take place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Definite singular noun (הַקֹּדֶשׁ) as object of construct or following locative preposition בְּ

senses.definition: In the plural, consecrated things, sacred offerings, or dedicated temple gifts and treasures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (קֳדָשִׁים / קָדָשַׁי) in construct chains or with pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Superlative construction (singular or construct plural governing the definite or indefinite plural) denoting either the innermost sacred chamber of the tabernacle or temple (behind the veil / inside the דְּבִיר) or objects and sacrificial offerings of the highest degree of sanctity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct superlative phrase: קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים / קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים / קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים

collocations_and_notes: Frequently functions as the nomen rectum in construct chains to characterize nouns as sacred or belonging to the divine sphere (e.g., אַדְמַת קֹדֶשׁ 'holy ground', שֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ 'sanctuary shekel', בִּגְדֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ 'holy garments', שֵׁם קָדְשִׁי 'my holy name', רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ 'his holy spirit', הֵיכַל קָדְשֶׁךָ 'your holy temple', בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ 'holy covenant'). Forms the superlative construction קֹדֶשׁ (הַ)קָּדָשִׁים / קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים ('holy of holies' / 'most holy') for both the innermost chamber of the tabernacle/temple and the most restricted sacrificial offerings. Appears in explicit contrast with זָר ('outsider/layperson', EXO 29:33) and in parallel/opposition to profaning (חִלֵּל, LEV 21:6, EZK 36:20).

core_meaning_summary: To guard, watch over, observe, or keep (physically protecting, monitoring, fulfilling obligations, or, in the Niphal, taking care and being on guard).

senses.definition: To watch over, protect, tend, or keep under guard, whether caring for a place or property, protecting lives, maintaining custody over people or objects, or standing sentry at a post; as a participle, a watchman or custodian.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), transitive with direct object, with עַל, or substantival participle

senses.definition: To observe closely, monitor, or pay close attention to conditions, paths, or one's own conduct and speech, including watching out for and steering clear of harmful ways.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), transitive with direct object or with לְ + noun

senses.definition: To observe, obey, carry out, or fulfill faithfully, applied to divine commandments, statutes, covenants, sacred days, vows, promises, justice, and priestly or sanctuary duties.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), transitive with direct object or followed by infinitive construct לַעֲשׂוֹת

senses.definition: To watch oneself, be careful, or be on guard against doing something wrong or dangerous, appearing in warnings and prohibitions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reflexive/passive stem (Niphal), imperative with ethical dative לְךָ/לָכֶם or בְּנַפְשׁוֹתֵיכֶם, often followed by פֶּן or אַל

senses.definition: To pay regard to, cling to, or devote oneself to something (specifically worthless idols or vanities, contrasted with forsaking loyalty).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive stem (Piel), participle governing a direct object

collocations_and_notes: Commonly pairs with legal/covenantal objects such as מִצְוָה (commandment), חֻקָּה (statute), תּוֹרָה (law), בְּרִית (covenant), מִשְׁפָּט (justice), and שַׁבָּת (Sabbath), often alongside עָשָׂה (do) or שָׁמַע (listen). In cultic contexts, frequently governs מִשְׁמֶרֶת or מִשְׁמָר (charge, watch, guard duty). In Niphal warning formulas, appears in the imperative followed by לְךָ/לָכֶם and פֶּן (lest) or a negative prohibition. Idiomatic expressions include שָׁמַר לְפִי מַחְסוֹם ("keep a muzzle on my mouth," PSA 39:2) and שָׁמַר אָרְחוֹת פָּרִיץ ("avoid/keep clear of the paths of a violent person," PSA 17:4). The participle serves substantively as a title for a guard, watchman, or custodian (e.g., שֹׁמְרֵי הַסִּפִּים "threshold-keepers," שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּגָדִים "keeper of the garments"). Note stem distinctions: Qal expresses outward guarding, observing, or fulfilling; Niphal expresses reflexive caution ("be careful, watch oneself"); Piel (JON 2:9) expresses devoted attachment or regard toward objects of worship.

core_meaning_summary: Cardinal number four, used independently, in compound numerals, and in the plural form to denote forty.

senses.definition: The basic cardinal quantity four, quantifying nouns (preceding or following the noun, or in construct state), taking pronominal suffixes to refer to a group of four, or functioning substantivally (such as for four limbs in walking or in graded poetic sequence).
senses.grammatical_frame: Cardinal numeral (absolute, construct before noun/thousand, post-nominal, with pronominal suffix, or substantivized after preposition)

senses.definition: Component of compound cardinal and calendar numerals, combining with ten (fourteen), multiples of ten (twenty-four, thirty-four, sixty-four), or hundred (four hundred) to count years, days, objects, livestock, or people, including ordinal-like designation of the twenty-fourth day of a month.
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral in compound expressions with עָשָׂר/עֶשְׂרֵה, tens, or מֵאוֹת

senses.definition: Plural form denoting the multiple forty, used alone or in combination with smaller or larger numerals to specify durations of days and years, troop or population counts, and reign lengths.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural numeral אַרְבָּעִים preceding counted nouns (usually singular for יוֹם, שָׁנָה, לַיְלָה, אֶלֶף) or coordinated with units

collocations_and_notes: Exhibits gender-polarized agreement patterns common to Hebrew numerals (masculine-form אַרְבָּעָה with masculine nouns such as רָאשִׁים, אֲנָשִׁים, שֻׁלְחָנוֹת, אוֹפַנֵּי; feminine-form אַרְבַּע with feminine nouns such as טַבְּעֹת, רוּחוֹת, עָרִים, קַרְנֹתָיו). Appears in construct (אַרְבַּעַת) before definite/counted plural nouns such as יָמִים (JDG 11:40) and אֲלָפִים (1CH 23:5, EZK 48:30), and takes pronominal suffixes (לְאַרְבַּעְתָּם/לְאַרְבַּעְתָּן, EZK 1:10). Idiomatic expressions include הֹלֵךְ עַל אַרְבַּע ('walking on all fours', LEV 11:21), אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת / אַרְבַּע קְצוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם ('four winds / four ends of the heavens', JER 49:36), graded numerical parallelism שְׁלֹשָׁה... וְעַל אַרְבָּעָה ('three... and for four', AMO 1:3), and the recurring duration formula אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לַיְלָה ('forty days and forty nights', EXO 34:28, DEU 9:9).

core_meaning_summary: To locate, encounter, reach, or attain something or someone (active), or to be discovered, detected, or present (passive).

senses.definition: To locate, come upon, or meet a physical object, person, place, or material resource, either through deliberate search or by chance encounter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with a direct object or relative clause

senses.definition: To reach, overtake, or strike an unintended or hostile target (such as spreading fire catching thorns, a flying axe-head hitting a person, or archers overtaking a fleeing warrior).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with a nonhuman or hostile subject and direct object

senses.definition: To discover, attain, or experience an abstract quality, inner state, explanation, fault, or person of a specific character; also to muster the resolve to act (with an infinitive complement).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with abstract nouns, character descriptions, or an infinitive complement

senses.definition: To be discovered, detected, caught, recorded, or present on hand, shifting the grammatical focus from the finder to the person, item, or record that turns up.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive stem (Niphal), intransitive with the located item, person, or written statement as grammatical subject

collocations_and_notes: Appears in the active simple stem (Qal) to describe locating, encountering, attaining, or striking an object or goal, and in the passive stem (Niphal) to describe being discovered, caught, detected, or present on hand. Frequently pairs with `בִּקֵּשׁ` ("to seek", e.g., 1KI 1:3, PSA 37:36, ECC 12:10). Common idioms include `מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי` ("to find favor in the eyes of", GEN 33:15), `לֹא מָצָא בְּיָד` ("to find nothing [wrong] in someone's hand", 1SA 12:5), and `נִמְצָא בְיָד` / `אִתּוֹ` ("to be found in one's possession", GEN 44:9, 1SA 9:8). In 1CH 17:25, `מָצָא` takes an infinitive complement (`לְהִתְפַּלֵּל`) to express finding the resolve or boldness to pray.

core_meaning_summary: An indefinite or unbounded span of time, denoting either perpetual future duration, enduring permanence, or remote antiquity.

senses.definition: Perpetual future duration without a foreseen end, whether spanning a person's ongoing existence, successive generations, or unlimited time; with negation it indicates "never."
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in prepositional phrases (with lamed or ad) or adverbial accusative of time

senses.definition: Lasting permanence or unending character as an attribute of institutions, covenants, conditions, or divine titles; in the plural, all successive ages.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural) as the second member of a construct chain modifying another noun or adjective

senses.definition: Remote past time or distant antiquity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun after the preposition min ("from") or as the second member of a construct chain denoting ancient peoples or sites

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in prepositional phrases marking unending duration (`לְעוֹלָם`, `עַד־עוֹלָם`, `עַד־הָעוֹלָם`, `מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם`) or distant past (`מֵעוֹלָם`). Often stands in poetic parallelism with `דֹּר וָדֹר` ("generation and generation", e.g., PSA 89:2, PSA 100:5, PSA 106:31, PSA 145:13) or `עַד` ("perpetuity", PSA 21:5, ISA 26:4). In construct chains it regularly qualifies legal ordinances (`חֻקַּת עוֹלָם`, `חָק־עוֹלָם`), covenants (`בְּרִית עוֹלָם`), emotional states (`שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם`, `כְּלִמַּת עוֹלָם`), and divine titles (`אֵל עוֹלָם`, `צוּר עוֹלָמִים`). In PSA 73:12, `שַׁלְוֵי עוֹלָם` describes the wicked as perpetually carefree or always at ease.

core_meaning_summary: A verb meaning to move downward or collapse in its simple active stem (Qal)—including prostrating, perishing in battle, or defecting—and to cause to drop, strike down, or cast lots in its causative active stem (Hiphil).

senses.definition: To drop from a higher place, lose footing and collapse, or crumble down (of people, animals, hairs, walls, or mountains).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), intransitive, often with locative adverbials (בְּ, אָרְצָה)

senses.definition: To throw oneself downward intentionally, whether prostrating face down in reverence or awe, embracing someone's neck, or casting oneself onto a sword.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) + עַל or אֶל + body part or weapon (פָּנִים, צַוָּארִים, חֶרֶב)

senses.definition: To die violently or be slain in combat or slaughter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), often with instrumental or locative phrases (בַּחֶרֶב, לְפִי חֶרֶב, בְּיַד) or with חָלָל ("slain"); participle frequently used substantivally for battle casualties

senses.definition: To suffer political or military ruin and overthrow, said metaphorically of a city or nation (contrasted with rising again).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), intransitive with city or personified nation as subject

senses.definition: To desert one's own side and go over or surrender to an opposing ruler or army.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) + עַל or אֶל + opposing ruler or people

senses.definition: To descend or come suddenly upon someone, whether of a raiding destroyer or an overwhelming sensation such as terror.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) + עַל + object affected

senses.definition: To cause something or someone to drop, bring down trees, knock out a tooth, bring about someone's death by the sword, or cause a deep sleep to come upon a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) + direct object (often with אֶת or object suffix), sometimes + עַל, בַּחֶרֶב, or בְּיַד

senses.definition: To throw or cast lots in order to reach a decision or join a shared undertaking, or to apportion territory by measuring line as an inheritance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) + direct object גּוֹרָל / פּוּר ("lot"), or object suffix + בְּחֶבֶל נַחֲלָה ("by a measuring line of inheritance")

collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear grammatical contrast between the simple active stem (Qal), where the subject moves downward, collapses, prostrates, defects, or perishes, and the causative active stem (Hiphil), where an agent causes something or someone to drop, be cut down, be slain, or casts lots/apportions territory. Common idiomatic frames include נָפַל עַל/אֶל פָּנָיו ("fall on one's face" in awe or supplication), נָפַל עַל צַוָּארָיו ("fall upon one's neck" in greeting), נָפַל בַּחֶרֶב / לְפִי חֶרֶב ("fall by the sword"), נָפַל אֶל / עַל + ruler/nation ("defect to"), and הִפִּיל גּוֹרָל / פּוּר ("cast lots"). Paired with כָּשַׁל ("stumble") in PSA 27:2 and contrasted with קוּם ("rise") in AMO 5:2.

core_meaning_summary: A temporal adverb meaning "now" or "at this time" that also functions widely as a discourse particle marking a logical transition to a command, request, or conclusion.

senses.definition: Refers to the present moment, current circumstances, or an imminent turning point in time, sometimes explicitly contrasted with past time (אָז) or preceding events.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying a clause or verb; occasionally paired with pronouns or temporal contrasts

senses.definition: With the preposition מִן, marks the present moment as the starting point of an ongoing or unbounded duration.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition מִן + עַתָּה (מֵעַתָּה), paired with וְעַד עוֹלָם

senses.definition: Signals a logical or rhetorical shift in speech from prior statements or conditions to a resulting command, plea, warning, conditional clause, or declaration.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial discourse marker, typically prefixed with וְ (וְעַתָּה) or וְגַם (וְגַם עַתָּה), preceding imperatives, jussives, prohibitions, or questions

collocations_and_notes: Very frequently prefixed with conjunction וְ as וְעַתָּה (and occasionally וְגַם עַתָּה in JOL 2:12) at the opening of a clause to pivot from an observation or narrative condition to an imperative, jussive, prohibition (אַל), plea (with נָא), or rhetorical question. In temporal usage, it contrasts directly with אָז ("then") in JOS 14:11 and combines with the preposition מִן as מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם ("from now and forever") in PSA 131:3. Appears in pausal form עָתָּה in JOS 14:11. Sometimes introduces a presentative הִנֵּה (1SA 12:2; 2CH 18:22) or causal/conclusive לָכֵן (JER 32:36).

core_meaning_summary: Personal interrogative pronoun asking "who?" or "whose?" in direct and indirect questions, rhetorical challenges implying "no one," and wish formulas meaning "would that!".

senses.definition: Interrogative pronoun inquiring after the identity, possessor, or agent of a person or group in direct or embedded questions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable interrogative pronoun (subject or predicate of verbal or nominal clauses, direct object with אֶת־, second member of a construct chain, prepositional complement, or introducing an indirect question after verbs of knowing or seeing)

senses.definition: Rhetorical interrogative used in challenges, boasts, laments, expressions of humility, or claims of incomparability to imply that no one exists or is able to act (or, when paired with negation, that everyone must do so); occasionally stands before a noun in the sense "what/which?" (DEU 4:7, MIC 7:18).
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable interrogative pronoun in rhetorical clauses (clause-initial, sometimes preceded by כִּי/וְכִי, with imperfect, perfect, participial, or nominal predicates, or immediately preceding an indefinite noun)

senses.definition: Particle introducing an ardent wish or longing, especially in the fixed phrase מִי יִתֵּן ("who will give?" = "if only! / would that!").
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative pronoun in optative constructions (fixed phrase מִי יִתֵּן + noun/clause, or מִי + imperfect verb with suffix)

collocations_and_notes: Indeclinable and uninflected for gender or number, though used with masculine, feminine (RUT 3:16, ISA 51:12), and plural (2KI 10:13) referents. Frequently joins with prepositions (לְמִי, עַל מִי, מִיַּד מִי) or direct object marker (אֶת־מִי), and follows a construct noun to ask "whose?" (שׁוֹר מִי, חֲמוֹר מִי in 1SA 12:3). Can be reinforced by demonstrative זֶה ("who is this?": ISA 63:1) or pronoun הוּא ("who is he/there?": JOB 17:3). The fixed sequence מִי יִתֵּן functions idiomatically to introduce an ardent wish ("O that! / would that!": DEU 28:67, PSA 53:7).

core_meaning_summary: The upper expanse or sky above the earth, extending to the transcendent abode of God and occasionally personified as cosmic witnesses or worshippers.

senses.definition: The visible sky, upper atmosphere, or physical cosmos above the earth—where birds fly, clouds form and release rain, and celestial bodies are set—frequently paired with the earth to encompass all creation or to denote extreme height and universal scope.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (with or without definite article הַ־, in construct phrases as second member, after spatial prepositions בְּ־/מִן/אֶל/תַּחַת/עַד, or with directional ה־ ending הַשָּׁמַיְמָה)

senses.definition: The transcendent heavenly realm conceived as God's dwelling place and seat of rule, from which God and his messenger look down, speak, hear prayer, and send sustenance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (typically definite with spatial prepositions בְּ־ or מִן, in nominal clauses locating God's throne, or as adverbial accusative of place with a verb of hearing)

senses.definition: The heavens personified or associated with celestial beings, summoned as witnesses or depicted as praising, rejoicing, or falling short of purity before God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (vocative or subject of plural verbs of speech, praise, or evaluation, or direct object of verbs summoning witnesses alongside the earth)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with אֶרֶץ ("earth/land") as a cosmic merism for the whole created order (GEN 1:1, GEN 2:1, DEU 31:28, 1CH 29:11, PSA 146:6). Common construct phrases include עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם ("birds of the sky": GEN 7:23, 1KI 21:24, PSA 104:12, JER 34:20, EZK 32:4, HOS 4:3, ZEP 1:3) and צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם ("host of the sky," referring to sun, moon, and stars: DEU 4:19, 2KI 17:16). Spatial expressions include תַּחַת (כָּל) הַשָּׁמַיִם ("under [all] the sky," i.e., anywhere on earth: DEU 4:19, DEU 9:14), the directional ending in הַשָּׁמַיְמָה ("skyward": EXO 9:8, DEU 4:19), and adverbial accusative הַשָּׁמַיִם ("in/from heaven" with verbs of hearing: 1KI 8:34, alternating with מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם in 2CH 6:21, 2CH 7:14). Always plural in morphology and takes plural verb agreement (e.g., נָטָפוּ JDG 5:4, יִרְגָּזוּ 2SA 22:8, לֹא זַכּוּ JOB 15:15, וְיוֹדוּ PSA 89:6, יִתְּנוּ JER 14:22).

core_meaning_summary: In the basic active (Qal) stem, to answer, respond, speak up, or testify; in the intensive/factitive (Piel), passive (Pual), and reflexive (Hithpael) stems, to afflict, oppress, humble, or be afflicted.

senses.definition: To answer, reply, or respond verbally to a person, question, argument, or summons.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); transitive with direct object (אֶת or suffix) or intransitive, frequently followed by וַיֹּאמֶר/וַיְדַבֵּר

senses.definition: To speak up, address, declare, or respond in turn, including liturgical acclamation and responsive singing or chanting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); intransitive or with direct quotation / suffix, often paired with אָמַר

senses.definition: Of God (or a deity), to answer a call, prayer, or appeal by acting, delivering, or granting a favorable outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); transitive with person or outcome (אֶת / suffix), often with instrumental בְּ־ (e.g., בָאֵשׁ, בֶּאֱמֶת)

senses.definition: To testify or give formal witness in a dispute or legal proceeding, either on behalf of or against someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); verb + בְּ־ (indicating the person testified for or against) + optional object (e.g., סָרָה)

senses.definition: To afflict, oppress, or mistreat a people or community through harsh treatment or subjugation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (factitive/intensive active); transitive with direct object (אֶת or noun phrase)

senses.definition: To humble or afflict oneself through prescribed self-denial and fasting on a sacred day.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (factitive/intensive active); transitive with אֶת נֶפֶשׁ (reflexive object "one's soul/self")

senses.definition: To violate sexually, abuse, or humiliate a woman.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (factitive/intensive active); transitive with אֶת + female person as object

senses.definition: To be afflicted, humbled, or endure hardship alongside another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael (reflexive/mediopassive, with בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר) and Pual (passive infinitive construct with pronominal suffix)

collocations_and_notes: In this dataset, the verb עָנָה exhibits a sharp stem-based semantic division: the Qal stem expresses communication, answering, testifying, or responding (senses 1a–1d), whereas the Piel, Pual, and Hithpael stems express affliction, oppression, self-denial, or violation (senses 2a–2d). In Qal narrative dialogue, וַיַּעַן ... וַיֹּאמֶר ("he answered and said") is a standard formula both for replies and for initiating a formal speech or response to a situation (e.g., 1SA 26:6; JOB 8:1; ISA 21:9; ZEC 4:4). When divine action is in view, Qal עָנָה frequently pairs with קָרָא ("to call," JOB 12:4; PSA 20:10; ISA 50:2; ISA 65:12; JER 33:3) and takes בְּ־ to indicate the means of response (e.g., בָאֵשׁ "with fire," 1KI 18:24; 1CH 21:26; בְקוֹל "with a voice," EXO 19:19). In Piel, the idiom עִנָּה אֶת נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם ("afflict your souls/selves") is fixed for ritual fasting and self-denial on the Day of Atonement (LEV 23:27; NUM 29:7).

core_meaning_summary: As a noun, denotes the nose, nostrils, face, or anger/wrath; as an adverbial or conjunctive particle, marks addition or intensification ("also," "even," "indeed").

senses.definition: The nose or nostrils as the physical organ of breathing and smelling (used both literally of breath entering the body and figuratively of wind/blast or receiving the scent of incense).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular or dual (often with pronominal suffix and preposition בְּ־)

senses.definition: The face or countenance, especially in expressions of prostration to the ground or haughtiness ("loftiness of face/nose").
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, dual or singular (with preposition עַל in prostration idioms, or in construct גֹּבַהּ אַפּוֹ)

senses.definition: Fierce displeasure, anger, or wrath (human or divine), frequently depicted as burning, kindling, or being turned back, and contrasted with patience ("long of anger").
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular (or dual in אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם), subject of חָרָה/שׁוּב, object of הֵשִׁיב/שָׁלַח/הֶחֱזִיק, or with בְּ־ / חֲרוֹן / חֳרִי

senses.definition: Additive particle introducing an additional participant, item, or parallel action alongside what has already been stated.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle (often וְאַף), preceding a pronoun, noun phrase, prepositional phrase, or clause

senses.definition: Emphatic or corroborative particle heightening a statement, introducing a climactic, confirming, or contrasting assertion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial or phrase-initial particle modifying a clause, verb, or predicate adjective

collocations_and_notes: This entry encompasses two distinct grammatical categories sharing the same spelling: a noun and a conjunctive/adverbial particle. As a noun, אַף frequently appears in the dual (אַפַּיִם) for nostrils or face (GEN 2:7; 1KI 1:23), and in the idiom אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם ("slow to anger," literally "long of nostrils/anger," PRO 15:18). For anger, it commonly collocates with verbs of burning (חָרָה, e.g., GEN 30:2; NUM 11:33; JDG 6:39; 2SA 12:5) and turning back (שׁוּב/הֵשִׁיב, JOB 9:13; ISA 9:20), as well as the construct phrases חֳרִי אָף ("burning anger," 1SA 20:34; 2CH 25:10) and חֲרוֹן אַף ("heat of anger," JOB 20:23; PSA 85:4; HOS 11:9), and is paired with חֵמָה ("wrath") and קֶצֶף ("fury") (JER 32:37; EZK 5:15; EZK 22:20). As a particle, it frequently combines with the conjunction וְ־ (וְאַף) or personal pronouns (אַף אָנִי, אַף הֵמָּה, אַף הִיא) to add a parallel or intensified statement.

core_meaning_summary: A preposition expressing an intermediate position, interval, mutual relationship, or distinction separating or connecting two or more entities, groups, categories, or points in time.

senses.definition: Spatial preposition marking a location, gap, boundary, or movement situated in the interval separating two or more places, objects, or body parts; includes the compound מִבֵּין (and מִבֵּינוֹת לְ) denoting origin or emergence from an intervening space.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + X + וּבֵין / וְלְ + Y; preposition + plural/dual noun; or compound מִבֵּין / מִבֵּינוֹת לְ

senses.definition: Preposition with a single plural noun or plural pronominal suffix denoting presence, comparison, sharing, or standing within a larger group.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + plural noun or plural pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Preposition denoting a reciprocal bond, legal status, covenant, peace, conflict, or judicial arbitration involving two or more persons, families, or peoples.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + X + וּבֵין / לְ + Y (personal nouns or pronominal suffixes)
senses.semantic_domain: Social Relations / Covenant, Conflict, and Law

senses.definition: Preposition marking a conceptual boundary or differentiation between distinct categories or states, or pairing contrasting extremes exhaustively ("whether ... or").
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + X + וּבֵין / לְ + Y (abstract or categorical nouns)

senses.definition: Temporal preposition in the fixed expression בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם ("between the two evenings"), designating the transitional period at the close of day.
senses.grammatical_frame: fixed temporal phrase בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם

collocations_and_notes: Regularly constructs with pronominal suffixes in either singular-like base forms (e.g., בֵּינִי, בֵּינְךָ, בֵּינוֹ) or plural-like base forms (e.g., בֵּינֵיכֶם, בֵּינֵיהֶם), and once in the compound feminine-plural form מִבֵּינוֹת לְ (EZK 10:6). Two main correlative patterns appear: בֵּין X וּבֵין Y (most frequent) and בֵּין X לְ Y (NUM 30:17, 2CH 14:10, EZK 22:26) or בֵּין X וְלְ Y (JOL 2:17). Compounds with מִן as מִבֵּין ("from between"; DEU 28:57, EZK 47:18, ZEC 6:1). Frequently governed by verbs of separating or distinguishing (הִבְדִּיל in GEN 1:4, LEV 10:10, EZK 22:26; הִפְלָה in EXO 11:7), covenant-making (כָּרַת בְּרִית in 2KI 11:17, 2CH 23:16; נָתַן בְּרִית in GEN 17:2), and judging (שָׁפַט in DEU 1:16).

core_meaning_summary: An enclitic particle of entreaty, urgency, or present focus attached chiefly to imperatives, cohortatives, jussives, and interjections.

senses.definition: Particle attached to an imperative (or a consecutive perfect expressing a request, as in GEN 40:14) to soften a command into a polite request or to add earnest urgency to a directive, plea, or summons.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following an imperative (or volitional consecutive perfect)

senses.definition: Particle attached to cohortative (first-person) or jussive (third-person) verb forms to mark a polite proposal, earnest wish, prayer, or (in ISA 47:13) an ironic challenge.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following a cohortative or jussive verb

senses.definition: Particle following the presentative interjection הִנֵּה or an interrogative word (אַיֵּה), drawing immediate attention to a current circumstance or sharpening an inquiry.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following הִנֵּה or an interrogative adverb

collocations_and_notes: Frequently induces gemination (conjunctive dagesh) in the initial nun (נָּא) after certain verbal or pronominal suffixes (e.g., GEN 19:8, GEN 27:21, GEN 40:14, GEN 50:5, 2SA 14:17, 2SA 18:22, 2KI 7:12, 1CH 21:13, NEH 1:11, PSA 122:8). Commonly follows וְעַתָּה ("and now"; GEN 50:5, EXO 10:17, JOS 2:12, JDG 7:3, 1SA 28:22, JER 18:11) or הִנֵּה ("behold"; GEN 12:11, GEN 19:8, JDG 19:9, 1SA 9:6, JOB 33:2), and co-occurs with plea formulas such as בִּי אֲדוֹנָי (JDG 13:8) and אָנָּא (NEH 1:11). Used across social registers: by petitioners to superiors or to God (GEN 40:14, 1KI 20:32, NEH 1:11, JOB 10:9), between equals (GEN 12:11, JDG 19:9), and by superiors or God in urgent directives (JDG 7:3, 2SA 13:17, ISA 7:3).

core_meaning_summary: A sea, ocean, or large inland body of water, and by extension the western cardinal direction.

senses.definition: A large body of water, whether an ocean, sea, or large inland lake, conceived as a domain of waves, marine life, navigation, and coastal boundaries, and named in specific geographical designations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine, singular יָם, plural יַמִּים); frequently definite (הַיָּם), in construct chains (יַם סוּף, יָם הַמֶּלַח, חוֹל הַיָּם, יוֹדְעֵי יָם), or with locative/directional prepositions (בַּיָּם, עַל הַיָּם, מִיָּם עַד יָם, יָמָּה in 1KI 5:23)

senses.definition: The western cardinal direction or western side/border, paired with east, north, and south (and in PSA 107:3 paired with north after east and west).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine) with directional ending -āh (יָמָּה), in prepositional phrases (מִיָּם, מִגְּבוּל יָם), or in construct with פְּאַת ('west side/quarter', פְּאַת יָם / פְּאַת יָמָּה)

collocations_and_notes: Plural יַמִּים occurs for bodies of water in general or turbulent seas (GEN 1:10, PSA 8:9, EZK 27:34). With directional suffix -āh (יָמָּה), it denotes either literal movement 'to the sea' (1KI 5:23) or the cardinal direction 'westward / on the west' (GEN 28:14, EXO 36:32, EZK 48:8). Frequent constructs designate specific waters or features: הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל ('the Great Sea', i.e. the Mediterranean), יַם סוּף ('Sea of Reeds'), יָם הַמֶּלַח / יָם הָעֲרָבָה ('Salt Sea / Sea of the Arabah'), הַיָּם הַקַּדְמֹנִי ('eastern sea'), הַיָּם הָאַחֲרוֹן ('western/hinder sea'), לְשׁוֹן הַיָּם ('bay/tongue of the sea'), חוֹל הַיָּם ('sand of the sea'), דְּגֵי הַיָּם ('fish of the sea'), חֶבֶל הַיָּם ('coastal region'), מְצֻלוֹת יָם ('depths of the sea'), and יוֹדְעֵי יָם ('those knowledgeable of the sea', i.e. seafarers). In PSA 107:3, מִיָּם pairs with מִצָּפוֹן after מִמִּזְרָח וּמִמַּעֲרָב, where it either refers to a southern sea or functions poetically as the fourth compass point.

core_meaning_summary: To feel fear or dread toward danger or enemies, to revere and stand in awe of God, or (in the passive/stative stem) to be fearsome and awe-inspiring.

senses.definition: To experience fear, alarm, or dread because of enemies, threats, calamity, or exposure, or to shrink back hesitantly from an action or speaking out of deference or apprehension.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stative/active stem (Qal) and adjectival/participial forms (יָרֵא / יְרֵאִים), absolute or with אֶת, מִן, מִפְּנֵי, or לְ + infinitive

senses.definition: To stand in reverent awe of God (or his name and presence), expressed through worship, covenant loyalty, keeping commandments, and turning from evil; as a verbal adjective or substantive, one who reveres and is devoted to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stative/active stem (Qal) with direct object (אֶת or pronominal suffix) or מִן, and construct/suffixed adjectival-substantive forms (יְרֵא, יְרֵאָיו, יְרֵאֶיךָ)

senses.definition: To be fearsome, terrible, or awe-inspiring (describing God or a sacred place); in the feminine plural as a noun, awesome or mighty deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/stative participle (Niphal: נוֹרָא, fem. pl. נֹרָאוֹת / נוֹרָאוֹת), used attributively, predicatively, or substantively

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in negated reassurance formulas (אַל־תִּירָא / אַל־תִּירְאוּ "do not be afraid"), often paired with "be strong and courageous" (חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ) or "do not be dismayed" (אַל־תֵּחָת / אַל־תִּשְׁתָּע). Objects of fear or reverence are introduced either by the direct-object marker אֶת (or suffix) or by the prepositions מִן / מִפְּנֵי. Across stems, the basic stative/active stem (Qal) and related adjectival forms express experiencing fear or holding God in reverence, whereas the passive/stative stem (Niphal participle נוֹרָא / נֹרָאוֹת) describes a place, deity, or deeds that inspire awe and dread.

core_meaning_summary: Moving air or wind, life-sustaining breath, an inner human disposition or attitude, the active spirit of God, or a divinely dispatched spiritual agent or impulse.

senses.definition: Moving air or atmospheric wind, ranging from a gentle breeze or directional air current to a destructive storm blast; also used figuratively for emptiness or futility, and metonymically for cardinal directions ('every wind', 'four winds').
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (typically feminine); subject of motion verbs (e.g., בָּאָה, בֹּאִי, שְׁבָרֵךְ), object of שֹׁמֵר, or in directional prepositional phrases (לְכָל רוּחַ, מֵאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת) and construct expressions (רְעוּת רוּחַ, כַּנְפֵי רוּחַ, רוּחַ הַקָּדִים)

senses.definition: The animating breath or vital life-force within living beings, sustained or withdrawn by God, upon whose departure a creature dies.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine) with pronominal suffixes or in construct (רוּחַ הַחַיָּה); object of verbs of keeping, gathering, or taking away (שָׁמְרָה, יֶאֱסֹף, תֹּסֵף), and paired with נִשְׁמָתוֹ

senses.definition: A person's inner disposition, seat of emotion, courage, resolve, patience, integrity, or mental inclination.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine) with personal suffixes or in construct (רוּחַ חָכְמָה, עֲצֻבַת רוּחַ, רוּחַ נְגִידִים), frequently with בְּ ('in') or as subject of stative/affective verbs (קָמָה, תִקְצַר, כָּלְתָה) and paired with לֵב ('heart')

senses.definition: The active spirit or power of God, hovering over primordial waters, resting upon or rushing into individuals to impart wisdom, prophecy, strength, or visionary transport.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine) in construct with אֱלֹהִים, יְהוָה, or קָדְשׁוֹ, or absolute with definite article (אִישׁ הָרוּחַ); subject of verbs of motion/empowerment (מְרַחֶפֶת, תִּצְלַח עַל, תִּשָּׂאֵנִי) and object of נָתַן ('give/put') or עִצְּבוּ ('grieve')

senses.definition: An unseen spiritual agent or divinely dispatched impulse that acts in the heavenly council or enters human beings to produce terror, deception, stupor, or sudden compliance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine in 1SA 16:15; masculine in 1KI 22:21) with article (הָרוּחַ), modifying adjective (רָעָה), or in construct denoting effect (רוּחַ שֶׁקֶר, רוּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָה); object of נָתַן ('put') or נָסַךְ ('pour out')

collocations_and_notes: Usually takes feminine verbal and adjectival agreement (e.g., מְרַחֶפֶת GEN 1:2, קָמָה JOS 2:11, גְּדוֹלָה JOB 1:19, רָעָה 1SA 16:15, וַתִּשָּׂאֵנִי EZK 43:5), though masculine agreement occurs when denoting a heavenly agent (וַיֵּצֵא הָרוּחַ 1KI 22:21). Frequent construct and prepositional collocations include רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים / רוּחַ יְהוָה ('spirit of God/YHWH'), רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ ('his holy spirit'), אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת ('four winds/directions'), כַּנְפֵי רוּחַ ('wings of wind'), רְעוּת רוּחַ / רַעְיוֹן רוּחַ ('pursuit/striving after wind', paired with הֶבֶל 'vapor/futility'), and construct phrases characterizing a disposition or effect (רוּחַ חָכְמָה, רוּחַ שֶׁקֶר, רוּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָה, רוּחַ מַשְׁחִית, עֲצֻבַת רוּחַ, רוּחַ נְכֵאָה). Often paired with לֵב ('heart') for inner life and with נְשָׁמָה ('breath') for mortal vitality.

core_meaning_summary: To move, flow, or extend downward from a higher position to a lower one, or (in the causative stem) to bring, lead, or cast someone or something down.

senses.definition: To move physically from a higher place to a lower one, dismount, withdraw from an area or shelter, travel to another region (especially Egypt), or march down toward someone in encounter or battle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), intransitive, often with directional -āh, direct place name, or prepositions (אֶל, עַל, בְּ, מִן, מֵעַל)

senses.definition: Of God or heavenly fire, to descend from heaven to earth, a mountain, or a meeting place to reveal presence, speak, inspect, or consume.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) with divine subject or fire (אֵשׁ), with עַל, בְּ, or מִן

senses.definition: Of liquids, tears, shadows, or geographical boundaries, to flow downward, shed streams, move down steps, or slope/extend downward toward a landmark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) with non-personal subjects (water, eyes, shadow, border), often with עַל, אֶל, מִתַּחַת, or directional -āh

senses.definition: To go down, be brought down, or cause someone to go down to the realm of the dead (Sheol/the pit), or of violence/retribution, to come down upon an offender's head.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), causative active stem (Hiphil), and causative passive stem (Hophal) with אֶל־שְׁאוֹל, שְׁאֹלָה, or עַל קָדְקֳדוֹ

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to move downward, take or lower an object from an elevated support, guide or bring people down to a lower place, or bring down enemies, peoples, or strongholds in defeat and judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) taking a direct object (with אֶת or pronominal suffix), often with אָרְצָה, אֶל, מֵעַל, or מִשָּׁם

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast or sequence with ascending ("go up", עָלָה), as in 1SA 6:21, 2CH 20:16, and PRO 21:22. Common directional constructions include the directional ending -āh (e.g., מִצְרָיְמָה "to Egypt", אָרְצָה "to the ground", שְׁאוֹלָה "to Sheol", הַיַּרְדֵּנָה "to the Jordan"), prepositions אֶל, עַל, בְּ, and מִן / מֵעַל. In poetic lament, eyes "run down" with streams of water (פַּלְגֵי־מַיִם, PSA 119:136, LAM 3:48). Across stems, the basic active stem (Qal) expresses intransitive downward motion of people, water, fire, borders, or shadows, whereas the causative active stem (Hiphil) expresses bringing/taking/leading someone or something down or bringing enemies/strongholds low, and the causative passive stem (Hophal, ISA 14:15) expresses being brought down to Sheol.

core_meaning_summary: To make known, report, or declare facts, secrets, divine messages, or events (in the Hiphil), and to be reported or revealed (in the Hophal).

senses.definition: To communicate news, facts, answers, or confidential information to someone, including reporting events or divulging a matter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil stem (active transitive); recipient normally marked by לְ, with content expressed by a direct object, כִּי clause, לֵאמֹר + direct speech, or עַל + topic; participle used substantivally as 'informer/messenger'

senses.definition: To disclose, explain, or reveal something hidden, puzzling, or previously unknown, such as a riddle, a secret, a name, divine counsel, or future events.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil stem (active transitive); takes a direct object (e.g., riddle, name, word, course) and optionally a recipient marked by לְ

senses.definition: To proclaim publicly, testify, instruct, declare praise, or denounce wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil stem (active, transitive or absolute); with direct object (e.g., faithfulness, uprightness, transgression) and optional recipient marked by לְ

senses.definition: To be reported, made known, or revealed to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hophal stem (passive); impersonal or with a grammatical subject naming the message/vision and the recipient marked by לְ

collocations_and_notes: Only Hiphil (active) and Hophal (passive: JDG 9:47; ISA 21:2) stems appear in the attested sample; no Qal forms occur. The recipient is routinely marked by לְ ('to'), while the message may be a direct object, a כִּי clause (GEN 3:11; JDG 9:47), direct speech introduced by לֵאמֹר (1SA 14:33; 19:2; 1KI 1:23; 2KI 5:4), or a topic introduced by עַל (1CH 19:5). The Hiphil infinitive absolute paired with the finite verb expresses certainty (הַגֵּד יַגִּיד, 1SA 22:22). Participial forms function substantivally for a messenger or reporter (2SA 1:5; 18:11; JER 51:31). Frequently paired with verbs of hearing, asking, or knowing (שָׁאַל in 1SA 25:8; שָׁמַע in ISA 41:26; 45:21; יָדַע in NEH 2:16; ISA 41:26; JER 33:3; רָץ in JER 51:31).

core_meaning_summary: Bodily blood of humans and animals, sacrificial blood used in ritual, and by extension lifeblood, violent bloodshed, or legal accountability for killing.

senses.definition: The red fluid sustaining life within human or animal bodies, whether flowing from wounds, drained at slaughter, or appearing as a substance replacing water.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular, or plural with suffix in bodily reference); used as subject, direct object, or object of prepositions (בְּ, מִן, לְ, עַל)

senses.definition: The blood of a slaughtered sacrificial animal manipulated in cultic rituals, such as sprinkling, pouring, throwing against the altar, or applying to consecrated persons and objects.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun (often definite or in construct with an offering or animal); direct object of verbs of taking, applying, sprinkling, or pouring, or governed by מִן / בְּ

senses.definition: The vital life-essence or life itself identified with or symbolized by blood, grounding the prohibition against eating blood and figuratively representing risk to human life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with possessive suffix or in construct; subject, predicate nominal, or direct object

senses.definition: Lethal violence, murder, or the violent loss of human life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular or plural noun (frequently plural absolute דָּמִים or plural construct דְּמֵי); object of verbs such as שָׁפַךְ ('shed') or אַרַב לְ ('lie in wait for'), or in construct chains denoting violent people

senses.definition: Moral or legal culpability for a person's death, or the claim for requital and vengeance arising from a killing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular or plural noun; in construct with גֹּאֵל ('avenger of'), or in predicative and prepositional clauses with לְ, בְּ, or מִיַּד ('from the hand of')

collocations_and_notes: Plural forms (דָּמִים, construct דְּמֵי) commonly denote violent bloodshed or guilt for killing, as in דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם ('their bloodguilt is upon them', LEV 20:27), בֵּית הַדָּמִים ('house of bloodshed', 2SA 21:1), אַנְשֵׁי דָמִים ('men of bloodshed', PSA 26:9), and דָּמִים בְּדָמִים נָגָעוּ ('bloodshed touches bloodshed', HOS 4:2). Key idioms include גֹּאֵל הַדָּם ('avenger of blood', NUM 35:27; DEU 19:12), אֵין לוֹ דָם ('he has no bloodguilt', NUM 35:27) contrasted with דָּמִים לוֹ ('bloodguilt belongs to him', EXO 22:2), שָׁפַךְ דָּם ('pour out/shed blood', used both for altar blood in DEU 12:27 and murder in JER 22:17; EZK 22:3; 23:45), דַּם הַנָּקִי ('innocent blood', JER 22:17), and דָּמִים מָלֵאוּ / דָּם בִּידֵיהֶן ('hands full of blood / blood on their hands', ISA 1:15; EZK 23:45). In EZK 5:17, דָּם ('bloodshed') pairs with דֶּבֶר ('pestilence').

core_meaning_summary: First-person singular independent personal pronoun, 'I', serving as subject in nominal and participial clauses or for emphasis and contrast with finite verbs.

senses.definition: First-person singular pronoun functioning as the grammatical subject of a verbless (nominal) or participial clause where person is not otherwise marked.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun serving as subject of a nominal or participial clause (often introduced by הִנֵּה, כִּי, or relative אֲשֶׁר)

senses.definition: First-person singular pronoun used explicitly alongside a finite first-person singular verb to mark emphasis, speaker focus, inclusion ('I too'), or contrast with another participant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun placed as explicit subject before or after a finite 1st-person singular verb (perfect, imperfect, or cohortative), frequently with contrastive וְ or גַּם

collocations_and_notes: Frequently introduced by הִנֵּה ('behold, I...', e.g., GEN 25:32, GEN 50:5, EXO 19:9, 1SA 3:11, 1CH 17:1, ISA 54:16, HOS 2:16) to announce present or imminent action. Common in the Deuteronomic formula אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה/מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם ('which I am commanding you today', DEU 7:11, 11:27, 15:11, 27:10, 30:16). Doubled for heightened emphasis in ISA 43:11 (אָנֹכִי אָנֹכִי יְהוָה). Appears alongside the shorter 1st-person singular pronoun אֲנִי within the same verse in 2SA 3:13 and JON 1:9, and often stands in direct contrast to 2nd-person pronouns אַתָּה/אַתְּ/אַתֶּם (DEU 4:22, JDG 11:35, 1SA 17:8, 1SA 23:17).

core_meaning_summary: Bad, inferior, morally wicked, or harmful; as a substantive, moral wrongdoing or adversity and calamity.

senses.definition: Defective, spoiled, inferior in physical quality, or unattractive in appearance, applied to animals, produce, offerings, or outward look.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective (including construct phrase רָעוֹת מַרְאֶה 'poor of appearance'); also substantive contrasting with טוֹב ('good')

senses.definition: Morally wrong, wicked, malicious, or unacceptable in character, disposition, speech, conduct, or reputation; as a plural substantive, wicked or hostile people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective modifying persons, deeds, ways, heart, or reputation (sometimes with בְּעֵינֵי 'in the eyes of'); or plural substantive (רָעִים)

senses.definition: That which is morally wrong, sinful, or contrary to divine standard; moral evil or wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular substantive, frequently definite (הָרַע) as direct object of עָשָׂה ('do') with בְּעֵינֵי ('in the eyes of'), or indefinite paired with טוֹב ('good')

senses.definition: Harmful, distressing, or adverse; as a substantive, misfortune, injury, trouble, or calamity affecting a person or community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular substantive (after prepositions מִן, בְּ, לְ, in construct יְמֵי רָע, or object of הֵבִיא 'bring') and attributive adjective modifying events, spirits, or occurrences (רוּחַ, פֶּגַע, מוֹקֵשׁ, מַעֲשֶׂה)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired as an antonym with טוֹב ('good', e.g., GEN 2:9, LEV 27:33, DEU 1:39, 2CH 18:17, PRO 15:3, AMO 5:15). Common recurring idioms include עָשָׂה הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה ('do what is evil/displeasing in YHWH's eyes', DEU 31:29, JDG 10:6, 1KI 16:30, 2KI 8:18, 2KI 17:2, 2KI 21:16, 2CH 36:5, ISA 66:4), הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע ('spread a bad/slanderous reputation', DEU 22:19), and יְמֵי רָע ('days of trouble/adversity', PSA 94:13). In PSA 140:12 (אִישׁ חָמָס רָע יְצוּדֶנּוּ), the syntax admits either an adjectival reading ('wicked man of violence') or a substantive subject ('evil/calamity will hunt him'). Note that the feminine singular form רָעָה also appears in the packet (e.g., 1SA 19:9, JER 35:15) as an adjective agreeing with feminine nouns, whereas substantive instances of 'calamity/evil' in DEU 31:29 and JER 4:6 reflect the feminine noun lemma rather than this entry.

core_meaning_summary: A manufactured object, container, utensil, furnishing, weapon, or piece of personal equipment used for a particular function.

senses.definition: A pot, jar, bowl, or receptacle (made of clay or metal) designed to hold liquids or other contents.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), often in construct with material (clay) or modifier (drinking, empty)

senses.definition: Utensils, implements, furnishings, or sacred articles belonging to the tabernacle or temple and used in sanctuary service.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (chiefly plural), in construct with sanctuary terms (service, holiness, house of God) or with pronominal suffixes referring to sacred furniture

senses.definition: Finely crafted objects, ornaments, or precious articles of silver or gold used as gifts, tribute, or royal treasure.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), in construct with precious metals (silver, gold, refined gold) or quality (prized)

senses.definition: Weapons, armor, or military equipment carried into battle; also used poetically for instruments of violence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (plural, or singular in figurative construct), frequently governed by 'carry/bear' (weapon-bearer) or 'strip off', or in construct with 'war' or 'violence'

senses.definition: Personal equipment, baggage, apparel, or an item of domestic furniture (such as a seat); in ritual purity discourse, possibly referring either to personal gear or to the body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), with pronominal suffix or in construct (a man's gear, exile's baggage), or absolute for a seat/article

collocations_and_notes: A broad general term whose specific referent is narrowed by construct phrases, materials, or context: e.g., kəlî ḥereś (earthenware vessel), kəlê kesep/zāhāb (silver/gold articles or vessels), kəlê haššārēt / haqqōdeš / hāʿăbōdâ (sanctuary service utensils/furnishings), kəlê hammilḥāmâ (weapons/war gear), and the frequent military title nōśēʾ kēlîm (weapon-bearer / armor-bearer). In 1SA 21:6, kəlê hannəʿārîm appears in a discussion of sexual abstinence and ritual purity, referring either to the young men's gear/packs or, by euphemism, to their bodies.

core_meaning_summary: To draw near or approach in space or time, and causatively to bring near, present, or offer a sacrifice.

senses.definition: To move physically closer to a person, place, or sacred space; to step forward or approach for service, inquiry, or ritual action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple stem (Qal), intransitive with directional preposition (to) or absolute; also causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively (EXO 14:10), and verbal adjective/participle (NUM 3:38)

senses.definition: To become imminent or at hand (of a time, event, or condition), to be on the point of doing something, or to reach and affect someone adversely (of harm or terror).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple stem (Qal) with an event, time, or affliction as subject; causative stem (Hiphil) with an infinitive construct (GEN 12:11, ISA 26:17)

senses.definition: To approach or present oneself directly before another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive stem (Piel) with a direct pronominal object suffix

senses.definition: To cause a person, group, or non-sacrificial item to come forward; to bring into someone's presence or present tribute to a ruler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with direct object (person, group, or gift) and optional directional preposition (to, before)

senses.definition: To bring and present an animal, grain, salt, wine, or dedicatory gift to God as a ritual sacrifice or offering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with sacrificial item as direct object, frequently with indirect object ('to YHWH' or 'before YHWH')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently distinguishes between the simple stem (Qal), used intransitively for moving closer to a place, person, or altar (often with the prepositions 'el 'to' or bə- 'against/in') or for events/times drawing near, and the causative stem (Hiphil), used transitively for bringing someone or something forward or presenting sacrificial offerings (often paired with qorbān 'offering', 'iššeh 'fire-offering', or ḥaṭṭā't 'sin-offering', and directed lə-YHWH 'to YHWH' or lipnê YHWH 'before YHWH'). The causative stem also appears intransitively for approaching (EXO 14:10) and with an infinitive construct for being on the point of doing something (GEN 12:11, ISA 26:17). The intensive stem (Piel) appears once in the sample with a direct pronominal suffix for approaching a person (JOB 31:37).

core_meaning_summary: A collective noun denoting small livestock (sheep and goats) kept in flocks, also used metaphorically for a community led by God or rulers and in the name of a Jerusalem gate.

senses.definition: Domesticated small livestock—sheep and goats collectively, or sheep specifically when contrasted with goats—tended in flocks for wool, milk, offspring, wealth, and sacrifice.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective noun (taking singular or plural, often feminine plural, verbal/adjectival agreement); frequently paired with בָּקָר, governed by רָעָה/רֹעֶה, or partitive after מִן

senses.definition: Figurative designation for a human group—especially Israel or a community under divine or human leadership, or numerous/vulnerable individuals—depicted as a flock needing care, protection, or guidance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective noun in simile (כַּצֹּאן) or construct chains (צֹאן מַרְעִית, צֹאן הַהֲרֵגָה, צְעִירֵי הַצֹּאן), parallel to עַם or עֵדֶר

senses.definition: Component of the proper architectural/topographical name שַׁעַר הַצֹּאן, designating a specific gate in the wall of Jerusalem.
senses.grammatical_frame: Definite collective noun as the second element in the construct proper name שַׁעַר הַצֹּאן

collocations_and_notes: Collective noun that exhibits both singular (e.g., יֻצָּג in EXO 10:24) and feminine plural or masculine plural agreement (e.g., תָּבֹאןָ and וַיֵּחַמְנָה in GEN 30:38; הַמְּקֻשָּׁרוֹת in GEN 30:41; לָהֶם in NUM 27:17; וַתִּהְיֶינָה in EZK 34:8; וּבִקַּרְתִּים in EZK 34:11). Frequently paired with בָּקָר 'cattle/herd' to denote total livestock wealth or sacrificial offerings (EXO 10:24, EXO 34:3, DEU 14:23, 2SA 12:2, 2CH 7:5, ECC 2:7). Common collocations include רֹעֵה צֹאן 'shepherd/herder' (GEN 4:2, GEN 46:34), הִשְׁקָה צֹאן 'to water the flock' (GEN 29:7, EXO 2:16), גִּדְרֹת צֹאן 'sheepfolds' (NUM 32:16), מִן הַצֹּאן 'from the flock' for sacrificial rams (LEV 5:25, EZK 43:25), and צֹאן מַרְעִית 'flock of pasture' in metaphors for God's people (PSA 74:1, PSA 100:3, JER 23:1, EZK 34:31). While encompassing both sheep and goats (GEN 31:10), in 1SA 25:2 צֹאן is listed alongside עִזִּים 'goats' and associated with shearing (גָּזַז), showing it can specifically highlight wool-bearing sheep.

core_meaning_summary: The inner self of a person, functioning as the seat of thought, intention, emotion, courage, and moral or religious character.

senses.definition: The cognitive faculty or inner mind where thoughts arise, understanding takes place, realities are recalled, and silent self-speech occurs.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; object of verbs of cognition/motion (e.g., יָדַע עִם, הֵשִׁיב אֶל, עָלָה עַל) or locative prepositional phrase with verbs of thinking/speaking (אָמַר בְּ/לְ, חָשַׁב)

senses.definition: The seat of will, desire, purpose, and concealed intention, whether directed toward constructive plans, seeking God, obstinate resistance, or hidden malice.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; in prepositional phrases (בְּ, עִם) indicating what one intends, or direct object of verbs of directing/hardening (הֵכִין, אִמֵּץ)

senses.definition: The center of emotional states and morale, encompassing gladness, sorrow, dread, grudgingness, and courage or faintheartedness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; subject of stative/process verbs (יָטַב, רָעַע, מָסַס), head of construct chains of emotion (פַּחַד, שִׂמְחַת), or modified in construct/attribute phrases (רַךְ הַלֵּבָב)

senses.definition: The moral and spiritual core of a person scrutinized by God, representing sincerity, ethical integrity, or wholehearted religious loyalty versus stubbornness or wickedness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; modified by ethical/devotional adjectives (שָׁלֵם, עָרֵל), governed by כֹּל in בְּכָל לֵבָב, or construct with moral nouns (תֹּם, יֹשֶׁר, רֹעַ)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in construct with moral/character nouns (תֹּם לֵבָב 'integrity of heart', יֹשֶׁר לֵבָב 'uprightness of heart', רֹעַ לֵבָב 'evil of heart') or in the emphatic devotion phrase בְּכָל לֵבָב 'with all the heart' (often paired with בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ in DEU 30:6). Common verbal idioms include הֵשִׁיב אֶל לֵבָב 'to recall to mind / reflect upon' (DEU 4:39), יָדַע עִם לֵבָב 'to recognize internally' (DEU 8:5), אָמַר בְּ/לְ לֵבָב 'to say to oneself / think' (JER 13:22, HOS 7:2, ZEP 2:15), הָיָה עִם לֵבָב 'to be one's intention' (2CH 6:8), מָסַס לֵבָב 'for courage to fail / melt' (DEU 20:8, JOS 5:1), יָטַב לֵבָב 'to be glad/content' (JDG 19:9), רַךְ לֵבָב 'timid/fainthearted' (DEU 20:8, 2CH 13:7), לֵבָב שָׁלֵם 'undivided/loyal heart' (1KI 11:4, 1KI 15:3, 2CH 19:9), and אִמֵּץ לֵבָב 'to harden one's resolve/will' (2CH 36:13). Parallel with נֶפֶשׁ 'soul/inner self' (PSA 13:3) and contrasted with outward speech or hands (כַּפַּיִם, GEN 20:5, PSA 28:3, PSA 73:13, PSA 78:72, LAM 3:41). In all 40 sampled verses, the noun refers to psychological, cognitive, volitional, or moral-spiritual faculties rather than the physical organ.

core_meaning_summary: The God of Israel or a deity/idol in general, alongside two occurrences in the corpus of the homographic plural demonstrative "these" (הָאֵל).

senses.definition: The supreme God, YHWH, the God of Israel, referred to in narrative, prayer, wisdom discourse, and liturgical titles as creator, judge, and deliverer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used absolutely, with definite article (הָאֵל), with 1cs suffix (אֵלִי), in construct or apposition with attributes/titles, and as vocative

senses.definition: A deity or god in a generic sense, including a fabricated idol or false object of worship, and in plural for other deities/gods.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun (including negated בְלֹא אֵל, object of יָצַר "fashion", and with כָּל־) and masculine plural (אֵלִים in DAN 11:36)

senses.definition: Near plural demonstrative determiner pointing out specific persons or nations already in view ("these"); homographic form grouped under this lemma in the corpus.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural demonstrative with prefixed definite article (הָאֵל) following and agreeing with a definite plural noun (הָאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵל, הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵל)

collocations_and_notes: Predominantly refers to the God of Israel and frequently stands in poetic parallelism with יְהוָה, אֱלֹהִים, אֱלוֹהַּ, and שַׁדַּי (e.g., JOB 5:8, JOB 12:6, JOB 15:25, PSA 7:12, PSA 18:31, PSA 68:36). Forms numerous construct and appositional divine titles: אֵל עֶלְיוֹן (GEN 14:18), אֵל שַׁדַּי (GEN 35:11), אֵל רַחוּם / חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם (DEU 4:31, JON 4:2), אֵל דֵּעוֹת (1SA 2:3), אֵל־נְקָמוֹת (PSA 94:1), אֵל־הַכָּבוֹד (PSA 29:3), אֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל (PSA 68:36), הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ISA 5:16), הָאֵל יְהוָה (PSA 85:9), and אֵל אֵלִים (DAN 11:36). Note that two occurrences tagged under this lemma in the corpus (GEN 19:8, DEU 7:22) are instances of the homographic plural demonstrative determiner הָאֵל ("these") modifying definite plural nouns.

core_meaning_summary: Loyal devotion, steadfast covenantal faithfulness, protective care, or personal favor shown between humans or by God toward people, with one rare proverbial occurrence denoting shameful or sinful conduct.

senses.definition: Faithful loyalty, dutiful kindness, or merciful treatment practiced between human beings—especially within kinship, friendship, diplomatic alliances, or just governance, as well as compassion toward the vulnerable.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; frequently object of עָשָׂה with עִם / אֶת / עַל (recipient) or with possessive suffix + אֶת; also in prepositional phrase בַּחֶסֶד (ISA 16:5)

senses.definition: Goodwill, gracious acceptance, or favorable standing granted to someone in the presence of a superior or royal official.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun as object of הִטָּה ("extend/incline") or נָשָׂא ("obtain/lift up") followed by לִפְנֵי ("before")

senses.definition: God's steadfast commitment, covenantal faithfulness, and protective, saving care toward his people or individuals; in the plural, concrete deeds or manifestations of such faithful care.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun (often with divine possessive suffix or in construct חֶסֶד יְהוָה, object of עָשָׂה / שָׁמַר, or in predicate לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ) and masculine plural (חֲסָדִים in PSA 25:6, ISA 63:7)

senses.definition: Disgrace, reproach, or misguided devotion—standing in syntactic antithesis to צְדָקָה ("righteousness" that exalts a nation) and predicated as חַטָּאת ("sin").
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun in construct (וְחֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים חַטָּאת) contrasting with צְדָקָה

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs as the object of עָשָׂה ("to do/show") with prepositions עִם, אֶת, or עַל to express reciprocal loyalty, covenantal obligation, or mercy toward another party (GEN 19:19, GEN 24:49, JDG 1:24, 1SA 20:8, 2SA 9:1, 1CH 19:2, PSA 109:16). Regularly paired with אֱמֶת ("truth/faithfulness", GEN 24:49, ISA 16:5), אֱמוּנָה ("faithfulness", PSA 89:25), בְּרִית ("covenant", 1KI 8:23), רַחֲמִים ("compassion/mercies", PSA 25:6, ISA 63:7, HOS 2:21), and צֶדֶק/מִשְׁפָּט ("righteousness/justice", HOS 2:21). Fixed liturgical and character formulas include כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ ("for his steadfast faithfulness endures forever", 2CH 7:6, PSA 118:2, PSA 136:1, PSA 136:8, PSA 136:14, PSA 136:20, PSA 136:26), עֹשֶׂה חֶסֶד לַאֲלָפִים (EXO 20:6, DEU 5:10, JER 32:18), and רַב־חֶסֶד (JOL 2:13). Appears in the plural (חֲסָדִים) for concrete deeds or expressions of care (PSA 25:6, ISA 63:7), and rarely with נָשָׂא or הִטָּה + לִפְנֵי for gaining favor before a ruler (EZR 7:28, EST 2:9). PRO 14:34 presents a striking contrastive usage where חֶסֶד of peoples is opposed to צְדָקָה ("righteousness") and equated with חַטָּאת ("sin").

core_meaning_summary: An action, practice, labor, undertaking, or the resulting product, handiwork, or design made by God or humans.

senses.definition: An act, course of conduct, or customary practice carried out by humans, nations, or God, often evaluated morally or religiously.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, often in construct with an agent or with יָדַיִם

senses.definition: Daily toil, occupation, enterprise, or purposeful endeavor in which a person engages.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, frequently in construct with יָדַיִם or possessive suffix

senses.definition: The tangible yield or output of labor, such as agricultural harvest from the field or manufactured wares traded in commerce.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, plural with possessive suffix in agricultural or commercial contexts

senses.definition: A crafted object, architectural feature, or created thing, or the specialized manner and skill of its construction and design.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, usually singular construct before an artisan, material, style, or creator (or with כְּ indicating likeness of design)

collocations_and_notes: Very common in construct chains: מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַיִם ('work/deeds/handiwork of hands') denotes either human endeavor and moral deeds (DEU 14:29, JER 44:8), crafted idols and artifacts (ISA 17:8, ISA 37:19), or God's creative activity (PSA 102:26, ISA 64:7). Also frequent in technical descriptions of craftsmanship as מַעֲשֵׂה + artisan or material (e.g., מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב in EXO 28:15, מַעֲשֵׂה רֹקֵחַ in EXO 30:25, מַעֲשֵׂה רֶשֶׁת in EXO 27:4). Often contrasted with or paired with דְּרָכִים ('ways', JON 3:10), עֲבֹדָה ('service/work', ISA 28:21), and מַחְשָׁבוֹת ('plans', PRO 16:3).

core_meaning_summary: To bring to mind, keep in attentive thought, or cause something or someone to be remembered, mentioned, or memorialized.

senses.definition: To call past events, deeds, people, or truths to conscious thought, or to retain them in memory so as to reflect upon them or act rightly in light of them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), transitive with direct object or clause introduced by כִּי or interrogative

senses.definition: To take attentive notice of or remain mindful of a person, covenant, devotion, or offense in a way that leads to action (such as deliverance, favor, blessing, or reckoning guilt); often takes the preposition לְ for the beneficiary or affected party.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), transitive with direct object (person, covenant, offering, or sin) and optional לְ phrase

senses.definition: To speak aloud or bring up a phrase or formula in speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), transitive with spoken expression as object

senses.definition: To be brought to mind or held in memory (such as being remembered before God for deliverance, or negatively, ceasing to be remembered among people); in one legal passage concerning firstborn livestock, the precise sense is uncertain.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (passive), intransitive with optional לִפְנֵי or locative phrase

senses.definition: To cause someone else to take notice of or remember a person, place, promise, or wrongdoing; to mention or call attention to.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), transitive with direct object and optional אֶל phrase

senses.definition: To perform a liturgical or sacrificial act of memorializing, such as offering frankincense or using a psalm heading marked for remembrance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), infinitive construct with לְ or participle with cultic substance

senses.definition: Used substantivally of a high royal official responsible for keeping records or bringing matters before the king.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative) participle functioning as a title noun

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with covenant (בְּרִית), steadfast love (חֶסֶד), and past wonders or sins. In Qal, the verb often carries pragmatic force beyond mental recall: when God remembers a person or covenant, deliverance or blessing follows (GEN 8:1, EXO 6:5, PSA 98:3), and with the preposition לְ it can mean taking account of something for someone's benefit (NEH 13:22) or holding past guilt against someone (PSA 79:8). Infinitive absolute + finite verb expresses emphatic admonition to remember (DEU 7:18). In EXO 34:19, the Niphal form תִּזָּכָר occurs in an obscure syntactic construction regarding firstborn livestock (possibly meaning 'be reckoned/claimed' or referring to male offspring). In Hiphil, the participle מַזְכִּיר functions as a royal administrative title ('recorder/remembrancer', 2SA 8:16), the infinitive לְהַזְכִּיר appears in psalm superscriptions with an unspecified liturgical role (PSA 38:1, PSA 70:1), and the participle with frankincense denotes a ritual memorial offering (ISA 66:3).

core_meaning_summary: Masculine noun denoting the dark period between evening and morning, used both for a specific nocturnal span or time-setting and adverbially for actions taking place at night or continuously around the clock.

senses.definition: The nocturnal span of darkness between evening and dawn, regarded as a distinct division of the day, a counted temporal unit, or the time frame of an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine singular, plural לֵילוֹת), used with numerals, demonstratives (בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא / הַזֶּה), prepositions, or in construct chains

senses.definition: Designates the time during which an action occurs, either generally at night or specifically during the immediate upcoming night ('tonight').
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun used adverbially without a preposition (לַיְלָה or definite הַלַּיְלָה) modifying a verb of motion, lodging, or action

senses.definition: Paired with 'day' in a fixed merism expressing continuous, unbroken duration across the entire 24-hour cycle or the ordered cosmic alternation of light and dark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinated adverbial pair יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה or לַיְלָה וְיוֹמָם

senses.definition: Darkness or obscurity used figuratively in poetry for confusion, distress, or concealment in contrast with light.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in similes (כַלַּיְלָה) or poetic parallelism with חֹשֶׁךְ ('darkness') and אוֹר ('light')

collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears with prepositions (בַּלַּיְלָה, עַד לָיְלָה, כַלַּיְלָה) and in construct expressions such as חֲלֹם הַלָּיְלָה ('dream of the night'), חֲצוֹת לָיְלָה ('midnight'), אַשְׁמוּרָה בַלָּיְלָה ('watch in the night'), and שׁוֹדְדֵי לָיְלָה ('plunderers of the night'). Plurals occur as לֵילוֹת (SNG 3:1). Frequently paired with יוֹם or יוֹמָם to express totality of time.

core_meaning_summary: Feminine noun denoting physical soil or dirt, arable farmland and its produce, a people's territory or homeland, and the inhabited surface of the earth.

senses.definition: Physical earth, dirt, clay, or ground surface as a material substance or the terrain beneath one's feet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), often governed by prepositions (מִן, בְּ) or in construct (מַעֲבֵה הָאֲדָמָה)

senses.definition: Cultivable soil, farmland, or landed property that can be sown, bought, divided, and taxed, and that brings forth crops and vegetation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), frequently with possessive pronominal suffixes or as direct object of verbs of sowing, buying, or dividing

senses.definition: A defined geographical region, territory, or homeland occupied by or promised to a nation or people, from which inhabitants may be exiled or to which they may return.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), in construct with proper national names (e.g., אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל), with possessive suffixes, or modified by relative clauses of gift/inheritance

senses.definition: The surface of the habitable world as the realm where humanity and terrestrial creatures live and move.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), characteristically in the prepositional phrase עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה ('on the face of the earth') or מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה

senses.definition: Proper name of a fortified town listed in a tribal territorial inventory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun (toponym) in a list of town names

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with the definite article or pronominal suffixes (e.g., אַדְמָתְךָ, אַדְמָתָם) and in construct chains such as פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה ('face of the ground/earth'), פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה ('produce of the soil'), and אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל / אַדְמַת יְהוּדָה ('land of Israel/Judah'). Often paired or contrasted with אֶרֶץ ('earth/land') and שָׂדֶה ('field').

core_meaning_summary: To be or become numerous, great, or extensive in number, quantity, or degree, and in the causative stem to make many, enlarge, or do something abundantly or repeatedly; also used in a fixed infinitive form for 'much/many' and once in connection with archery.

senses.definition: To become numerous, increase in number, volume, distance, or duration (used of living beings, floodwaters, a journey's distance, sorrows, and lifespan).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive with subject (people, animals, water, distance, days, sorrows)

senses.definition: To cause to increase in number, size, or degree; to multiply offspring, people, objects, actions, territory, honor, or events (sometimes with מִן for comparison, 'more than').
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem; transitive with direct object (or לְ + noun), optionally with מִן for comparison

senses.definition: To act abundantly, excessively, or repeatedly in performing the action of a companion verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem functioning adverbially before לְ + infinitive construct or a finite verb

senses.definition: Used as an indeclinable quantifier or adverbial modifier expressing a large quantity or high degree ("many," "much," "greatly," "exceedingly"), frequently intensified by מְאֹד.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative infinitive absolute (הַרְבֵּה) modifying a noun, clause, or verb

senses.definition: In a single occurrence paired with קַשָּׁת ("bowman/archer") in a wilderness setting, designating a shooter with a bow (or possibly one growing skilled as an archer); exact nuance within this lemma's range is context-dependent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active participle (רֹבֶה) in construct with קַשָּׁת

collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear stem distinction between the simple active stem (becoming numerous, increasing in number, quantity, or extent) and the causative stem (making numerous, enlarging, multiplying, or doing something abundantly). Frequently paired with פָּרָה ("to be fruitful," GEN 1:22; GEN 48:4; EZK 36:11) and contrasted with מָעַט ("to be few/diminish," NUM 33:54; JER 30:19). The causative infinitive absolute הַרְבֵּה is heavily grammaticalized as an adverb or quantifier ("much, many"), often reinforced by מְאֹד ("very," GEN 15:1; 2SA 12:2; 1KI 10:10; 1CH 20:2; 2CH 14:12; NEH 2:2). In GEN 21:20, the simple active participle רֹבֶה appears uniquely in construct with קַשָּׁת ("bowman/archer").

core_meaning_summary: To consume liquid by drinking, whether literally for sustenance, festivity, or abstinence, or figuratively as experiencing divine judgment, violence, or nourishment.

senses.definition: To take a liquid (such as water, wine, milk, strong drink, or blood) into the mouth and swallow it, expressed with a direct object, partitive מִן, or a prepositional phrase marking the vessel or source.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; transitive with direct object, or with מִן / בְּ marking liquid, source, or vessel

senses.definition: To take liquid refreshment or partake in a meal or drinking banquet, commonly paired with eating (or negated with eating to indicate fasting); includes drinking by animals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive or paired with eating, or infinitive with עִם (person)

senses.definition: Figuratively, to undergo or absorb an experience, especially to suffer divine wrath or judgment (often depicted as drinking a cup or wine), to incur violence, or (of trees) to draw up water as nourishment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; with direct object (cup, violence, water) or מִן (wrath, wine)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with אָכַל ("to eat") in the narrative idiom "eat and drink" (e.g., GEN 25:34; EXO 24:11; JDG 19:21; 1KI 19:8; 2KI 6:23; ECC 3:13) and in negative pairings to describe fasting ("bread he did not eat and water he did not drink," DEU 9:9; EZR 10:6). Common objects include מַיִם ("water"), יַיִן ("wine"), and שֵׁכָר ("strong drink"). Takes מִן before the liquid (GEN 9:21), the vessel (2SA 12:3), or the water source (1KI 17:6), and בְּ before the drinking cup (GEN 44:5). Infinitive absolute + finite verb expresses certainty or inevitability (שָׁתוֹ יִשְׁתּוּ / שָׁתֹה תִשְׁתֶּה, JER 49:12). The active participle with a suffix (שֹׁתָיו, ISA 24:9) or in construct (שֹׁתֵי מָיִם, EZK 31:16) designates "drinkers (of)." All occurrences in the evidence packet appear in the simple active stem.

core_meaning_summary: To leave, leave behind, abandon, neglect, or forsake a person, place, possession, relationship, or covenant allegiance in the simple active stem, and to be neglected or forsaken in the passive stem.

senses.definition: To depart from or leave behind a person, household, location, or possessions (including leaving objects behind when fleeing, withdrawing before an enemy, or leaving wealth at death).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with direct object (person, place, or object), sometimes with locative adverb or מִן ('from')

senses.definition: To leave behind resources for another's benefit, station someone at a post, or entrust dependents to another's care.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with direct object and לְ- ('for/to') marking the beneficiary or stationed party, or imperative entrusting dependents

senses.definition: To forsake, neglect, or withdraw care, protection, or loyalty from someone, or (in passive participial forms) to be left desolate, unprotected, or at large.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with person, life, or attribute (loyalty) as object, or Qal passive participle describing a desolate or unattended state

senses.definition: To forsake, reject, or turn away from God, his temple, covenant, or moral path, or conversely to give up and abandon idols or counsel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with deity, covenant, temple, path, counsel, or idols as direct object

senses.definition: To be neglected, unattended, or forsaken (said of the house of God when its service and support were not maintained).
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive stem (Niphal), intransitive with inanimate subject (the house of God)

collocations_and_notes: In GEN 2:24, leaving parents (עָזַב) is paired antonymically with clinging to a spouse (דָּבַק). In covenant and worship contexts, forsaking YHWH is repeatedly followed by serving or bowing down to foreign/other gods (JOS 24:16, JDG 10:6, 1KI 11:33, JER 5:19, JER 16:11) or breaking his covenant and failing to keep his instruction (DEU 31:16, 1KI 19:14, JER 16:11). In PSA 94:14, it stands in parallel with נָטַשׁ ("cast off"). Idiomatic usages include עָזַב חַסְדּוֹ אֶת ("withdraw/abandon steadfast loyalty toward," RUT 2:20) and the merism עָצוּר וְעָזוּב ("restrained and left-free/abandoned," i.e., all categories of people in Israel, 2KI 14:26) using the Qal passive participle.
