core_meaning_summary: To rescue, deliver, or snatch away from danger, oppression, or another's grasp in the active causative stem, and to be spared, escape, or free oneself in the passive/reflexive stem.

senses.definition: To rescue, deliver, or save a person, life, city, or people from enemies, violence, death, hardship, or moral/legal liability, often by intervening between contending parties or removing someone from another's control.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object (person, life, city, or people) and optional prepositional phrase with מִן ('from') or מִיַּד ('from the hand of')

senses.definition: To snatch away, reclaim, recover, or defend livestock, territory, captives, or prey from the possession or mouth of an adversary or predator.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object (livestock, territory, plot, or prey) and optional מִן / מִיַּד / מִפִּי ('from / from the hand of / from the mouth of')

senses.definition: To be delivered, spared, or snatched to safety from destruction or judgment, or reflexively to extricate and free oneself from an entanglement or obligation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), intransitive, with optional instrumental phrase introduced by בְּ- ('by')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently constructed with מִיַּד ("from the hand/power of") or מִן ("from") to mark the source of danger or control (e.g., GEN 37:22, 2KI 18:34, JER 20:13). Emphatic infinitive-absolute + finite verb combinations occur in הַצֵּל לֹא הִצַּלְתָּ (EXO 5:23), הַצֵּל תַּצִּיל (1SA 30:8), and הַצֵּל יַצִּילֵנוּ (2KI 18:30, ISA 36:15). The participial phrase אֵין מַצִּיל ("there is no one to rescue/intervene") appears in 2SA 14:6 and DAN 8:4. Frequently paired or paralleled with verbs meaning "save" (הוֹשִׁיעַ, 1CH 11:14, PSA 7:2, ISA 19:20) and "deliver" (פִּלֵּט, PSA 22:9, PSA 82:4). EZK 14:16 and AMO 3:12 directly contrast the active causative stem (rescuing others / snatching prey) with the passive/reflexive stem (being spared / escaping). No simple active (Qal) forms occur in the evidence packet.

core_meaning_summary: To lie down to rest or sleep, to lay or be laid down, to have sexual intercourse, or euphemistically to die and lie in death.

senses.definition: To recline horizontally, lie down to rest or sleep, or remain lying in a place or on a surface.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); intransitive, frequently with locative phrases (עַל, בְּ, שָׁם) or paired with verbs of sleeping

senses.definition: To force or gently place someone in a lying position, or passively to be laid down (including placing a corpse on a bed or among the dead).
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil, transitive with direct object) and causative passive stem (Hophal, passive with prepositional location)

senses.definition: To engage in sexual intercourse with someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); taking the partner with עִם or אֶת / direct object marker אֹת־

senses.definition: To die or rest in death and the grave, especially in the idiomatic expression of sleeping/lying with one's ancestors.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); intransitive, commonly with עִם־אֲבֹתָיו or locative phrases referring to dust or the underworld

collocations_and_notes: The simple active stem (Qal) covers resting/lying down (1a), sexual intercourse (1c), and dying/resting in death (1d). In contrast, the causative active stem (Hiphil, 2SA 8:2; 2KI 4:21) means "cause to lie down / lay down," and the causative passive stem (Hophal, EZK 32:32) means "be laid down" (specifically among the dead). Common collocations include שָׁכַב עִם־אֲבֹתָיו ("lie down with one's ancestors") as a standard royal death formula, often followed by burial notices (e.g., 1KI 15:24; 2CH 16:13), and שָׁכַב עִם / אֶת for sexual relations.

core_meaning_summary: To add something to an existing amount or group, increase, or do an action again, further, or no longer.

senses.definition: To add an amount, item, or quality to what already exists, or to cause something to increase in quantity or extent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) and causative active (Hiphil) stems; transitive with direct object (or object implied), often with עַל or אֶל marking the base to which addition is made

senses.definition: To be added to an existing group or portion, or to experience an increase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal); intransitive, with עַל marking the recipient entity

senses.definition: To perform an action again, continue doing something, or do something further or more intensely; when negated, to stop doing something or never do it again.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) and causative active (Hiphil) stems; auxiliary with infinitive construct (with or without לְ), coordinated finite verb, or standing elliptically, often modified by עוֹד or negated by לֹא/אַל

collocations_and_notes: Frequently functions as an auxiliary verb governing an infinitive construct (with or without לְ) or a finite verb to express repetition ("again"), continuation, or intensification ("more"), very often paired with the adverb עוֹד ("again, still") and frequently negated with לֹא or אַל ("no longer, never again"). In 2SA 3:9 it appears in the oath formula כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂה אֱלֹהִים ... וְכֹה יֹסִיף לוֹ ("May God do so ... and do even more to him"). Both the simple active stem (Qal) and causative active stem (Hiphil) occur in both additive (1a) and auxiliary/continuative (1c) constructions without a sharp semantic difference in these forms, whereas the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal, NUM 36:3; PRO 11:24) expresses being added or increasing.

core_meaning_summary: To have the ability, power, or permission to do something, or to prevail over, succeed against, or endure someone or something.

senses.definition: To possess the physical, mental, emotional, or circumstantial capacity or power to carry out an action or reach a state (most often negated to express impossibility or inability).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal; imperfect forms with u-stem vocalization) followed by an infinitive construct (usually with לְ-, occasionally bare).

senses.definition: When negated, to be prevented or forbidden from doing something by law, ritual restriction, a binding oath, or a divine command; not to be permitted or free to act.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) negated with לֹא + infinitive construct with לְ-, in legal, cultic, or vow-bound contexts.

senses.definition: To gain the upper hand, overcome an opponent, or succeed in accomplishing one's aim (or, when negated, to fail to succeed or overcome).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) used absolutely without a complementary infinitive (sometimes reinforced by an infinitive absolute), or with the preposition לְ- marking the opponent or target overcome.

senses.definition: To bear, withstand, or tolerate a person or overwhelming force (used negated to express inability to endure).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) negated with לֹא, taking a direct object (אֹתוֹ) or used absolutely with a causal מִן-phrase.

collocations_and_notes: Appears predominantly in negated clauses (with לֹא, or poetically בַּל in PSA 21:12). Simple active imperfect forms consistently exhibit u-vowel prefix vocalization (e.g., אוּכַל, תוּכַל, יוּכַל, נוּכַל). Frequently takes a complementary infinitive construct prefixed with לְ-, though bare infinitives also occur (DEU 1:9; ISA 47:11; JER 49:23). With infinitive absolute reinforcement (NUM 13:30; 1SA 26:25) or in absolute usage without an expressed infinitive (2KI 3:26; PSA 21:12; ISA 16:12; JER 20:7), it denotes prevailing or succeeding. With לְ- before a person (GEN 32:26; JER 1:19), it expresses overcoming an opponent.

core_meaning_summary: The curved or flat inner surface of the hand (palm) or foot (sole), extending to the hand itself as an agent of action, grasp, gesture, or power, as well as hollow anatomical sockets and shallow dish-like vessels.

senses.definition: The palm or open inner surface of the hand, and by extension the hand itself as used for holding, working, gesturing (in prayer, clapping, or pledging), or as representing a person's moral deeds and innocence or guilt.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular, dual, or plural), often with pronominal suffixes or in construct with יָד ('hand'); frequently governed by prepositions בְּ-, עַל, or מֵעַל, or serving as direct object of gesture verbs (e.g., spread, lift, clap, strike, shake).

senses.definition: Figuratively, the grasp, control, power, or hostile reach of an agent, or a state of exposure and vulnerability when something is held in one's own hand.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, in construct before a human agent/enemy (especially with מִן 'from the grasp of') or with prepositional בְּ- indicating vulnerability.

senses.definition: The flat underside or sole of a human, animal, or visionary foot.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular or plural) in construct before רֶגֶל ('foot') or פַּעַם ('step/foot').

senses.definition: The hollow or socket of the thigh/hip joint.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct before יֶרֶךְ ('thigh/hip').

senses.definition: A measure of capacity equivalent to what an open palm or single hand can hold; a handful.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun following מְלֹא ('fullness of').

senses.definition: A shallow, palm-shaped metal dish, pan, or ladle used in sanctuary and temple service to hold incense or offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular or plural כַּפּוֹת), modified by material (gold, silver), weight, or contents (incense).

collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired or paralleled with יָד ('hand') in expressions of power, deliverance, or craftsmanship (e.g., EXO 4:4; ISA 62:3; PSA 18:1). Frequent fixed idioms include: כַּף רֶגֶל ('sole of the foot', e.g., GEN 8:9; JOS 3:13; EZK 1:7) and מִכַּף רַגְלוֹ וְעַד קָדְקֳדוֹ ('from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head' for the whole body, 2SA 14:25); תַּחַת כַּפּוֹת רַגְלַי ('under the soles of my feet' for subjugation, 1KI 5:17); פָּרַשׂ כַּפַּיִם / נָשָׂא כַפַּיִם ('spread out / lift up the palms' in prayer, 1KI 8:54; 2CH 6:12; PSA 63:5); מָחָא כָף / הִכָּה כַף אֶל כָּף ('clap the palms / strike palm against palm', ISA 55:12; EZK 21:19); תָּקַע כַּף ('strike the palm' to make a pledge/surety, PRO 6:1); נַפְשִׁי בְכַפִּי ('my life is in my palm' for constant peril, PSA 119:109); and מְלֹא כַף ('handful/palm-full', ECC 4:6). Dual and plural forms alternate between כַּפַּיִם (paired hands) and כַּפּוֹת (soles, cut-off hands, or cultic dishes).

core_meaning_summary: A friend, close companion, neighbor, or fellow member of a community, also functioning idiomatically with 'man/each' to express reciprocity.

senses.definition: A personal friend, trusted confidant, or close companion, ranging from a royal or social associate to a cherished beloved.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural רֵעִים), often with possessive suffixes or in construct with a personal name

senses.definition: Another person within one's social, occupational, or covenant community—a neighbor, peer, or fellow citizen—in legal, ethical, and everyday interactions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with singular pronominal suffixes (רֵעֲךָ, רֵעֵהוּ) governed by verbs of action, speech, lending, or injury, or in construct (e.g., אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ, 'his neighbor's wife')

senses.definition: Each other or one another, expressing reciprocal action or relation between members of a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with 3rd-person suffix (רֵעֵהוּ) paired idiomatically with אִישׁ ('each one') and a linking preposition (אֶל, לְ-, בְּ-, אֵת, מֵאֵת)

collocations_and_notes: Very commonly occurs with a pronominal suffix (especially רֵעֵהוּ 'his neighbor/fellow' and רֵעֲךָ 'your neighbor/fellow'). Frequently paired with אָח ('brother/kinsman') in DEU 15:2, ISA 41:6, JER 34:17, with קָרֹב ('near one/neighbor') in PSA 15:3, and with שָׁכֵן ('neighbor/resident nearby') in JER 6:21. In SNG 5:16, רֵעִי ('my friend') stands in direct poetic parallelism with דוֹדִי ('my beloved') as an affectionate title for a romantic partner. In reciprocal idioms with אִישׁ ('each person'), the prepositions אֶל, לְ-, בְּ-, אֵת, and מֵאֵת specify directionality or opposition ('to/for/against/from one another').

core_meaning_summary: A four-footed land animal, encompassing domesticated livestock, riding beasts, wild or scavenging quadrupeds, and non-human animals broadly.

senses.definition: Domesticated herd or farm animals—such as cattle and sheep/goats—that are owned, pastured, kept in stalls, sacrificed, eaten, or taken as spoil in war.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun, often with possessive suffixes (e.g., בְּהֶמְתּוֹ), in construct with owners, or expanded by cattle and flocks

senses.definition: An individual pack or riding animal used as a mount by a traveler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun serving as antecedent to רֹכֵב בָּהּ ('riding upon it')

senses.definition: Land animals or quadrupeds considered broadly as a biological or legal category distinct from humankind, birds, fish, and creeping things, whether ritually clean or unclean.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun, frequently coordinated with אָדָם ('humankind') or contrasted with עוֹף ('birds'), רֶמֶשׂ ('creeping things'), and דָּגִים ('fish')

senses.definition: Wild land animals, including predators and scavenging beasts that feed on unburied corpses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun, frequently in the construct phrase בֶּהֱמַת הָאָרֶץ ('beasts of the earth') or in partitive בַּבְּהֵמָה ('among the beasts')

senses.definition: Beasts used figuratively as a standard of comparison for people regarded as unreasoning, contemptible, or mortal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular or plural (בְּהֵמוֹת) governed by the comparative preposition כְּ- ('like/as')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in merism or coordination with אָדָם ('humankind'), e.g., בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה ('both human and animal') or מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה ('from human to beast'), to encompass all earthly life or objects of judgment/blessing (EXO 9:9, EXO 11:5, NUM 18:15, PSA 135:8, JER 31:27, EZK 14:13, JON 3:7). Commonly occurs in the construct phrase בֶּהֱמַת הָאָרֶץ ('beasts of the earth') for scavenging or wild animals alongside עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם ('birds of the sky') (DEU 28:26, ISA 18:6, JER 16:4, JER 34:20). Classified ritually as טְהוֹרָה ('clean') vs. טְמֵאָה ('unclean') (GEN 7:8, LEV 20:25, LEV 27:11). In JON 3:7, הַבְּהֵמָה is immediately appositionally specified as הַבָּקָר וְהַצֹּאן ('the cattle and the flock'). The plural בְּהֵמוֹת appears in PSA 49:21 in a simile for mortal humans lacking understanding.

core_meaning_summary: To perish, vanish, be lost, or go astray in the simple active stem, and to destroy, exterminate, or wipe out in the intensive and causative stems.

senses.definition: Of people, nations, or cities: to die, be destroyed, be wiped out, or suffer total ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intransitive; subject is persons, peoples, or a city

senses.definition: Of objects, wealth, refuge, memory, counsel, hope, or prophetic visions: to disappear, fail, be lost, or come to nothing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intransitive; subject is concrete possessions or abstract states/capacities (often with מִן indicating from whom something vanishes)

senses.definition: As a participle describing straying livestock or a displaced person: to wander lost, go astray, or be in peril of perishing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) participle used substantively or attributively

senses.definition: To destroy, annihilate, or wipe out people, cultic objects and sites, memory, or loud noise.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive active stem (Piel), transitive; takes a direct object (people, idols, shrines, memory, or sound)

senses.definition: To cause to perish, eliminate, or destroy enemies, nations, or military equipment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil), transitive; takes a direct object (adversaries, nations, or chariots)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of dying, ending, or destroying such as גָּוַע (NUM 17:27), כָּלָה (JOB 4:9; PSA 37:20), שָׁמַד (NUM 33:52; EST 3:13; ISA 26:14), הָרַג (EST 3:13; EST 9:12), and כָּרַת (MIC 5:9). Often occurs with abstract subjects like מָנוֹס ("escape/refuge," JOB 11:20; JER 25:35; AMO 2:14) and תִּקְוָה ("hope," PRO 11:7). In DEU 26:5, אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי may describe an ancestor either as "wandering/homeless" or as "perishing/in mortal danger." Across stems, the simple active (Qal) is intransitive ("perish, be lost"), whereas both the intensive active (Piel) and causative active (Hiphil) are transitive ("destroy, wipe out").

core_meaning_summary: Collective noun referring to large domestic bovine livestock—cattle and oxen—used for agriculture, wealth, food, sacrifice, and also depicted in temple metalwork.

senses.definition: Large domestic bovine animals (cattle, oxen, cows) viewed collectively as herds or property, or counted individually with numerals, used for grazing, pulling carts or yokes, meat, and sacrificial offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective masculine singular noun (often paired with צֹאן; occasionally counted directly with numerals or used after צֶמֶד)

senses.definition: The cattle herd or bovine species designated as the source of an individual young animal (calf or young bull) prepared as a meal or offered in sacrifice.
glosses: cattle (in "young bull / calf of the herd")
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive noun in construct phrases בֶּן־בָּקָר / בֶּן־הַבָּקָר (often following פַּר / פָּרִים)

senses.definition: Sculpted or engraved representations of oxen or cattle forming decorative panels or supporting bronze furnishings in the temple.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective noun referring to artistic or bronze figures

collocations_and_notes: Very frequently paired with צֹאן ("flocks / sheep and goats") to designate total livestock holdings or sacrificial animals (e.g., GEN 12:16; EXO 20:24; DEU 16:2; HOS 5:6). Appears with צֶמֶד ("yoke / pair") for draft teams (1SA 11:7; JOB 42:12). Although grammatically singular and usually collective, it is occasionally counted directly with numerals (NUM 7:7; NUM 7:23). In construct after בֶּן/בְּנֵי and often following פַּר/פָּרִים, it identifies a young bovine for food or sacrifice (GEN 18:8; LEV 4:14; NUM 28:19).

core_meaning_summary: A slaughtered animal sacrifice offered to a deity (typically involving a shared meal), a meat-feast, figuratively a spiritual offering, and also a Midianite king's personal name.

senses.definition: A slaughtered animal offering presented to YHWH or another deity, distinguished from a whole burnt offering in that its blood and fat belong to the altar while its flesh is typically eaten by worshippers or priests; includes peace-offerings and thanksgiving offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, frequently in construct with šĕlāmîm or tôḏāh, and often paired with ʿōlāh or minḥāh

senses.definition: A communal or household feast of slaughtered meat, whether a covenant or family sacrificial meal or a banquet contrasted with simple food.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, absolute or in construct (e.g., zeḇaḥ mišpāḥāh "family feast", ziḇḥê rîḇ "feasts of strife")

senses.definition: Figuratively, an inner disposition of humility and contrition presented as an offering acceptable to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural construct (ziḇḥê ʾĕlōhîm) equated with "a broken spirit"

senses.definition: Zebah, one of the two kings of Midian pursued and captured alongside Zalmunna.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper personal noun, always paired with Zalmunna

collocations_and_notes: Frequently serves as the cognate object of the verb zāḇaḥ ("to sacrifice a sacrifice": GEN 31:54, LEV 17:7, LEV 22:29, JDG 16:23, 2CH 7:5, 2CH 30:22, PSA 27:6, PSA 107:22, EZK 20:28). Commonly paired with ʿōlāh ("burnt offering") and minḥāh ("grain/tribute offering"). Recurrent construct phrases include zeḇaḥ (haš)šĕlāmîm ("sacrifice of peace-offerings"), zeḇaḥ tôḏāh / ziḇḥê tôḏāh ("sacrifice(s) of thanksgiving"), and ziḇḥê tĕrûʿāh ("sacrifices of joyful shouting"). Plural is normally masculine (-îm / -ê), though a feminine-like plural ending occurs in HOS 4:19 (mizziḇḥôṯām). In JDG 8:5, 12 the identical form functions as the proper name of a Midianite king.

core_meaning_summary: To ask a question, seek information or divine counsel, request something, wish well, or borrow (and in the causative stem, lend or hand over).

senses.definition: To put a question to someone, inquire about a matter, or interrogate in order to learn information or gain counsel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb, often with direct object (person asked) and direct speech (with or without lēʾmōr), or with lĕ- / ʿal marking the topic; intensive/iterative stem paired with simple active infinitive absolute and bĕ- + place for customary inquiry (2SA 20:18)

senses.definition: To consult YHWH, God, or a divinatory object in order to obtain an oracle, decision, or guidance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + bĕ- (deity or divinatory object), sometimes with lĕ- (beneficiary) and direct speech

senses.definition: To ask for, desire, request, or demand a thing, favor, permission, or requirement from someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + direct object (thing requested), optionally with min (source) or lĕ- (beneficiary); passive/reflexive stem with min + person and lĕ- + infinitive for earnestly asking leave for oneself (1SA 20:6)

senses.definition: To inquire after or pray for the peace and well-being of a person or city.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + lĕ- (person) + lĕ-šālôm, or + construct phrase šĕlôm + noun

senses.definition: To ask for the temporary use of items from others; to borrow.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + direct object (items) + lĕ- (for oneself) + mēʾēṯ (from neighbors)

senses.definition: In the causative stem, to hand over, lend, or dedicate someone upon request; in the simple passive participle, to be lent or dedicated.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem + direct object + lĕ- (recipient); simple passive participle + lĕ-

collocations_and_notes: Frequently introduces direct questions with lēʾmōr ("saying"). Often forms the figura etymologica with the simple active infinitive absolute + finite verb (1SA 20:6 in the passive/reflexive stem; 2SA 20:18 in the intensive stem). Common collocations include šāʾal bĕ- + divine name or cult object ("inquire of a deity"), šāʾal lĕ- + šālôm / šĕlôm ("ask after/pray for the well-being of"), and šāʾal lĕ- + person ("request for oneself/another"). Stem distinctions observed: the simple active stem covers asking, consulting, requesting, and borrowing, while its passive participle (1SA 1:28) denotes one handed over upon request; the passive/reflexive stem (1SA 20:6) expresses earnestly asking permission for oneself; the intensive/iterative stem (2SA 20:18) expresses customary inquiry for counsel at a place; and the causative stem (1SA 1:28) means to grant, lend, or hand over someone to another.

core_meaning_summary: A verb denoting both the physical or figurative breaking, shattering, and bringing to ruin of objects, bodies, and powers, and, in commercial contexts, the buying or selling of grain and food provisions.

senses.definition: To fracture, smash, snap, or wreck a solid object or structure such as a door, bone, earthenware vessel, yoke-bar, or ship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with direct object (or marked with אֶת)

senses.definition: To smash completely or shatter into pieces durable, plural, or formidable objects such as stone tablets, sacred pillars, altars, idols, bronze fixtures, teeth, ships, or trees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive active stem (Piel), transitive with direct object

senses.definition: To suffer breaking, cracking, or wrecking, used of ships, bones, leaking cisterns, city gate-bars, idols, tree boughs, or a limb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/middle stem (Niphal), intransitive with affected entity as subject

senses.definition: To cut off sustenance or bring a person, ruler, or nation to ruin and defeat (basic active stem), or to be crushed and ruined beyond recovery (passive/middle stem).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with 'staff of bread' or personal object; or passive/middle stem (Niphal), intransitive with personal/collective subject

senses.definition: To purchase grain, food, or basic drink provisions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with grain, food, or drink as direct object, or absolute

senses.definition: To sell or supply grain for payment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil), transitive with grain (שֶׁבֶר) as direct object

collocations_and_notes: Two sharply distinct semantic fields appear under this lemma in the corpus: (1) physical or figurative breaking/shattering (Senses 1a–1d), and (2) commercial trading in grain and provisions (Senses 2a–2b). Within the breaking senses, the basic active stem (Qal) typically takes individual objects (a door, a bone, a pottery vessel, a yoke-bar, a ship) or marks food-supply disruption (בְּשִׁבְרִי ... מַטֵּה־לֶחֶם, LEV 26:26), while the intensive active stem (Piel) characteristically describes violent or total shattering of durable, plural, or formidable targets (stone tablets, cultic pillars, altars, images, bronze temple fixtures, teeth/fangs, ships, trees, sea-monster heads, bones). In commercial contexts, the basic active stem (Qal) collocates with בָּר ('grain', GEN 42:3) and אֹכֶל ('food', GEN 42:10; GEN 43:22) for buying, whereas the causative stem (Hiphil) takes שֶׁבֶר ('grain', AMO 8:5) in parallel with opening wheat stores for selling.

core_meaning_summary: A focusing and qualifying particle that restricts an assertion to a single item or condition, contrasts or limits a preceding statement, confirms the certainty of a declaration, or marks immediate temporal completion.

senses.definition: Marks the following word, phrase, or clause as the sole exception, condition, extent, or characteristic, excluding everything else.
senses.grammatical_frame: Restrictive particle preceding a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, number, or clause

senses.definition: Introduces a qualification, exception, or contrast against a preceding command, rule, or situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial adversative particle contrasting with a preceding clause

senses.definition: Reinforces the truth, certainty, or intensity of an assertion, exclamation, or exhortation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Asseverative particle preceding a verbal or nominal clause, imperative, or infinitive absolute construction

senses.definition: Marks an action as having taken place immediately prior to the following event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverbial particle preceding an infinitive absolute and finite verb

collocations_and_notes: Frequently stands at the beginning of a clause or immediately before the focused constituent (such as a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, or verb). Common collocations include אַךְ הַפַּעַם ('just this once', GEN 18:32), אַךְ בְּזֹאת ('only on this condition', GEN 34:22), אַךְ דָּבָר אֶחָד ('only one thing', 2SA 3:13), אַךְ שְׁתַּיִם ('only two things', JOB 13:20), and כִּי אַךְ ('for surely', 2KI 5:7). Repeated in parallel poetic lines for rhetorical emphasis in PSA 39:7, PSA 58:12, PRO 21:5, and JER 32:30. In JDG 7:19, it precedes an infinitive absolute paired with a finite verb (אַךְ הָקֵם הֵקִימוּ) to mark an action just completed.

core_meaning_summary: The cessation of physical life (dying), lethal danger or execution, and poetically the personified power or realm of the dead.

senses.definition: The end or cessation of biological life, whether referring to a specific individual's dying or death in general as the opposite of life (including plural construct מוֹתֵי in EZK 28:10).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (absolute, construct מוֹת/מוֹתֵי, with suffixes, or in temporal phrases with בְּ, עַד, אַחֲרֵי, לִפְנֵי)

senses.definition: A fatal danger, deadly plague, lethal blow, or judicial capital penalty (including idioms for a death sentence or deserving to die).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (absolute or in construct expressions such as בֶּן מָוֶת, מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת, כְּלֵי מָוֶת, הֲרֻגֵי מָוֶת)

senses.definition: Death personified as an active power or figure, or conceived as an underworld realm/abode parallel to Sheol or Abaddon.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (subject of verbs, addressee, or construct expressions such as חַדְרֵי מָוֶת, חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת, מִשְׁבְּרֵי מָוֶת)

collocations_and_notes: Common construct expressions include יוֹם מוֹתוֹ (the day of his death, GEN 27:2, 1SA 15:35, 2CH 26:21, JER 52:34), אַחֲרֵי מוֹת (after the death of, 2SA 1:1, 2KI 1:1, 2KI 14:17, 2CH 22:4), עַד מוֹת (until the death of, NUM 35:32, JOS 20:6), לִפְנֵי מוֹתוֹ (before his death, DEU 33:1), בֶּן מָוֶת (son of death = one deserving death, 2SA 12:5), מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת (death sentence, JER 26:16), כְּלֵי מָוֶת (deadly weapons, PSA 7:14), דַּרְכֵי מָוֶת (ways of death, PRO 14:12, PRO 16:25), חַדְרֵי מָוֶת (chambers of death, PRO 7:27), חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת (cords of death, PSA 18:5), and מִשְׁבְּרֵי מָוֶת (breakers of death, 2SA 22:5). Plural construct מוֹתֵי appears as a cognate accusative with מוּת in EZK 28:10, and the poetic form הַמָּוְתָה occurs in PSA 116:15. Frequently contrasted with חַיִּים (life, DEU 30:15, JER 8:3) and paired in parallelism with שְׁאוֹל (Sheol, PSA 89:49, PRO 7:27, ISA 28:18, HOS 13:14) or אֲבַדּוֹן (Abaddon, JOB 28:22).

core_meaning_summary: To move or extend around something in a circle, surround or go about a place, turn in a different direction, or cause something to turn, move, or change.

senses.definition: To move, curve, stand, or extend in a circuit around an object, region, or person (active in the basic stem and intensive stem; intransitive or with direct object in the passive/reflexive stem for borders).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal), passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), or intensive stem (Poel); intransitive or + direct object (אֶת / suffix)

senses.definition: To close in on, march around, besiege, or beset a city, dwelling, or person in hostility or threat (observed in the basic stem and once in the passive/reflexive stem in JDG 19:22).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) or passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) + direct object (אֶת / suffix)

senses.definition: To travel or circulate through a city or region, making rounds or patrolling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) + בְּ (in/throughout)

senses.definition: To change direction or orientation: turn aside, turn back, dodge, return to a place, or turn again to perform a subsequent action (passive/reflexive stem in Ezekiel describes not swerving from a straight course).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) or passive/reflexive stem (Niphal); intransitive, often + אֶל, מִן, לְאָחוֹר, or coordinated with another verb

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to turn, move to another place, roll, or be redirected (including turning one's face toward or away, diverting troops, or inclining a ruler's heart); passive-causative in ISA 28:27 of rolling a cartwheel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) + direct object (or intransitive military maneuver + מֵעַל); passive-causative stem (Hophal) in ISA 28:27

senses.definition: To pass over or transfer from one party to another (basic stem), bring about an outcome (basic stem + בְּ), or alter a name (causative and passive-causative stems).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) + מִן...לְ or + בְּ; causative stem (Hiphil) or passive-causative stem (Hophal) with שֵׁם

collocations_and_notes: Across stems: the basic active stem (Qal) expresses going around, surrounding, patrolling, turning, or transferring; the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) expresses curving or turning (e.g., borders, moving figures) as well as surrounding an object (JDG 19:22); the intensive-stem pattern (Poel) highlights continuous encompassing or ritual procession (PSA 26:6, JON 2:4) and appears in the poetic statement "a female shall encompass a man" (JER 31:22, contrasted with turning away); the causative stem (Hiphil) expresses turning/redirecting someone or something (e.g., turning one's face, moving an object, changing a name or heart), with the passive-causative (Hophal) denoting a wheel rolled over grain (ISA 28:27) or names being changed (NUM 32:38). Common collocations include + אֶת (direct object) for encircling a place/person, + אֶל/מִן for turning toward or away from, + בְּ for going about within a region (2CH 17:9, SNG 3:3), סָבַב פָּנִים (turn the face, 1KI 8:14, 2CH 29:6), סָבַב שֵׁם (change a name, NUM 32:38, 2KI 24:17), and coordination with a second finite verb to mean "do again" (PSA 71:21). Frequently paired or paralleled with הִקִּיף (surround, JOS 6:3, 2CH 4:3) and סָבִיב (around, 2CH 4:3, ECC 1:6).

core_meaning_summary: Ordinal adjective and adverb indicating second position in a sequence, the counterpart in a pair, or the repetition of an action a second time.

senses.definition: Occupying position two in a chronological, genealogical, spatial, or organizational sequence (such as days, months, years, sons, architectural stories, wall sections, or marching divisions).
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative ordinal adjective (masc. sg./pl., fem. sg.), or substantivized with the definite article

senses.definition: Designating the counterpart or remaining member of a pair, or a companion/additional person in contrast to a single individual (ECC 4:8).
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive ordinal adjective or substantive, usually paired with אֶחָד ("one") or negated with אֵין ("there is no")

senses.definition: Indicating that an action or event takes place once more after a prior occurrence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular שֵׁנִית functioning adverbially to modify a verbal clause

collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with אֶחָד ("the one ... the second/other") in paired items or measurements (EXO 26:5, EXO 29:39, EXO 37:18, NUM 11:26, 1KI 6:26, 1KI 7:15) and continued in sequences with שְׁלִישִׁי ("third": GEN 6:16, 1CH 8:39, 1CH 26:2, ISA 37:30). Common in calendrical expressions such as בַּיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי ("on the second day"), בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי ("in the second month"), and בַּשָּׁנָה הַשֵּׁנִית ("in the second year"). Shows masculine singular שֵׁנִי, feminine singular שֵׁנִית, and masculine plural שְׁנִיִּם (GEN 6:16, NUM 2:16); in NEH 3:30 מִדָּה שֵׁנִי appears alongside מִדָּה שֵׁנִית in NEH 3:20. The feminine singular שֵׁנִית regularly serves adverbially for repeated actions ("a second time").

core_meaning_summary: Verb denoting experiencing or expressing gladness, delight, or malicious gloating in the simple active stem, and causing someone or something to be glad in the causative stem.

senses.definition: To feel or express gladness, joy, or contentment over favorable events, worship, deliverance, God's character, or ordinary life blessings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active): intransitive; used absolutely or with בְּ (source/sphere), עַל (occasion), לִפְנֵי (before YHWH), כִּי/לְמַעַן (reason), or cognate accusative שִׂמְחָה

senses.definition: To take malicious delight or exult over another's downfall, ruin, or misfortune.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active): intransitive with לְ or אֶל marking the victim, or absolute in contexts of hostile mockery

senses.definition: To cause a person, community, heart, or soul to experience joy or gladness, or (with לְ of the victim in PSA 30:2) to allow enemies to gloat over someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (causative): transitive with direct object (person, city, לֵב, or נֶפֶשׁ), optionally with בְּ (instrument/place) or cognate accusative שִׂמְחָה

collocations_and_notes: In the Qal (simple active), frequently paired with other verbs of rejoicing and praise such as גִּיל ("rejoice"), שׂוּשׂ ("exult"), רָנַן ("shout for joy"), and עָלַץ/עָלַז ("exult": JOB 3:22, PSA 14:7, PSA 35:27, PSA 68:4, JER 50:11, JOL 2:21, ZEC 2:14). Often takes בְּ to mark the sphere or source of gladness (e.g., בַּיהוָה, בֵּאלֹהִים, בְּחַגֶּךָ, בְּלִבּוֹ), לִפְנֵי יְהוָה in cultic settings (DEU 12:12, PSA 68:4), כִּי for the reason of joy, and occasionally the cognate accusative שִׂמְחָה (JON 4:6). In Ecclesiastes, appears in the refrain לֶאֱכוֹל וְלִשְׁתּוֹת וְלִשְׂמוֹחַ ("to eat, drink, and enjoy oneself": ECC 8:15; cf. ECC 3:12, ECC 11:9). The Piel (causative) contrasts clearly with the Qal by taking a direct object (people, heart, soul, or city) to express causing joy, and in PSA 30:2 takes לְ to indicate allowing enemies to gloat over the speaker.

core_meaning_summary: A verb used primarily in the intensive, passive, and reflexive stems meaning to cover over physically (with water, clouds, garments, or coverings), to clothe oneself, or figuratively to overwhelm, conceal, or overlook wrongs.

senses.definition: To place or spread something over a person, body part, structure, pit, or terrain so as to enclose, shield, adorn, or submerge it; in passive stems (Pual, Niphal), to be covered over or submerged.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object (or ʿal); Passive intensive (Pual) and Passive simple (Niphal) with covered entity as subject

senses.definition: To dress or wrap another person in clothing, or (with an omitted reflexive object in the intensive stem, or in the reflexive intensive stem) to put on a garment or sackcloth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object of person or garment (or bĕ- + garment); Reflexive intensive (Hithpael) + bĕ- + sackcloth

senses.definition: To overtake or overwhelm a person completely with dread, horror, or the violent consequences of wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) with abstract emotion or violence as subject + direct object of person

senses.definition: To withhold knowledge of an action from someone, keep hostile feelings secret, or conceal one's sins rather than confessing them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object of deed, emotion, or sin (+ min- 'from' someone)

senses.definition: To cover over an offense so as to pardon sin (by God) or foster reconciliation rather than broadcasting a fault (in human relations).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object (pešaʿ 'transgression', ḥaṭṭāʾt 'sin')

collocations_and_notes: In the sampled corpus, the verb occurs predominantly in the active intensive stem (Piel), alongside passive intensive (Pual: GEN 7:19; EZK 41:16), passive simple (Niphal: JER 51:42), and reflexive intensive (Hithpael: 2KI 19:1; ISA 37:2); no simple active (Qal) occurrences appear in the sample. Frequently collocates with water, clouds, darkness, fat, or garments/sackcloth (śaq, beged, kĕsût), and in PRO 17:9; 28:13; PSA 32:5; 85:3 with pešaʿ, ʿāwōn, or ḥaṭṭāʾt (contrasted with môdeh 'confessing' in PRO 28:13 and paired with nāśāʾ 'forgive' in PSA 85:3).

core_meaning_summary: A relational preposition and spatial term denoting position directly opposite, facing, or in front of someone or something, extending to presence before witnesses or in one's sight/awareness, as well as distance away from or correspondence to.

senses.definition: Positioned directly across from, facing, or physically in front of a person, object, or architectural feature.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition neged or lĕ-neged + noun or pronominal suffix

senses.definition: In the physical presence, direct sight, or public witness of a person, assembly, or deity, including legal testimony, worship, or conduct observed by others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition neged or lĕ-neged + person, divine name, or ʿênayim ('eyes')

senses.definition: Kept continually before one's mind, attention, or regard.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition lĕ-neged + pronominal suffix (with abstract nouns or offerings as subject)

senses.definition: Positioned at a distance opposite something, or separated and removed away from someone's presence or line of sight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition min-neged (+ noun, lĕ-, or pĕnê / ʿênayim)

senses.definition: Matching or corresponding to someone as a suitable counterpart.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition kĕ-neged + pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Assigned over, attending to, or positioned in charge of a sphere of service or work.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition lĕ-neged + noun phrase denoting work or task

collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with prepositions: lĕ-neged (often interchangeable with bare neged for 'in front of, before, in the sight of', and in NEH 11:22 for oversight over work), min-neged ('at a distance opposite' or 'away from the presence/sight of'), and kĕ-neged ('corresponding to', GEN 2:18). Common collocations include lĕ-neged ʿênê / min-neged ʿênê ('before the eyes of' / 'out of the sight of', PSA 5:6; 36:2; ISA 1:16; JER 16:17; AMO 9:3) and public or legal witness formulas (neged hazzĕqēnîm, neged YHWH, RUT 4:4; 1SA 12:3). In 2CH 6:12 it appears alongside lipnê ('before').

core_meaning_summary: A verb denoting physical touching or contact (often with ritual effect), forceful striking or affliction in the simple active stem, and bringing into contact, extending to a limit, or arriving in the causative stem.

senses.definition: To make physical contact with a person, object, or surface, including contact that transmits ritual impurity or holiness, or spatial contact between adjacent structures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + preposition בְּ-, עַל, or אֶל introducing the object touched

senses.definition: To strike forcefully, harm, or afflict with suffering or calamity; in the passive participle, to be stricken or afflicted.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + preposition בְּ- or עַד; also passive participle (נָגוּעַ) without preposition

senses.definition: To cause something to touch a target, or to bring or cast a structure down into contact with the ground.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with explicit or implied direct object + preposition עַל, לְ-, or אֶל

senses.definition: To extend as far as or reach up to a spatial boundary, height, or extreme degree.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively + preposition לְ- or עַד לְ-

senses.definition: To arrive at a place or appointed turn in time, or (of events and outcomes) to come upon or befall someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively, either absolute or + preposition אֶל

collocations_and_notes: In the simple active stem (Qal), the target is most often introduced by the preposition בְּ-, and occasionally by עַל (ISA 6:7, DAN 10:16), עַד (JOB 4:5, JER 4:18), or אֶל (1KI 6:27); in ritual legislation it frequently marks contact that transmits impurity or holiness. In 2SA 5:8, the verb governs בַּצִּנּוֹר in an obscure military instruction where the sense is physical reaching or striking. In the causative stem (Hiphil), it exhibits both transitive causative usage (bringing an object into contact or casting down to the ground) and intransitive usage (reaching a limit, arriving at a place or time, or befalling someone, governed by לְ-, עַד לְ-, אֶל, or absolute).

core_meaning_summary: A grammatically plural noun denoting physical vitality and mortal existence, the temporal span of a lifetime, and flourishing or well-being.

senses.definition: Physical vitality, animating breath, or continued mortal existence as opposed to death or destruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (absolute, construct, or with pronominal suffixes); object of verbs of saving, loathing, or choosing, or in construct (e.g., נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים, דֶּרֶךְ הַחַיִּים)

senses.definition: The temporal duration or span of earthly existence; a person's age or lifetime, including the period while one remains alive.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun in temporal construct chains (יְמֵי חַיֵּי-, שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי-), or with prepositions בְּ- or לְ- plus suffix or personal name

senses.definition: Health, security, flourishing, and blessed quality of existence associated with wisdom, righteousness, or favor; also lived earthly experience.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (subject, predicate, object, or governed by preposition לְ- or בְּ-; also in wisdom constructs like עֵץ חַיִּים, אֹרַח חַיִּים, חַיֵּי בְשָׂרִים)

senses.definition: The addressee's life invoked as the surety in an oath formula.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun with second-person pronominal suffix in an oath exclamation paired with חֵי נַפְשֶׁךָ and followed by אִם

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in temporal construct chains such as כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֵּי- ("all the days of the life of..."), שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי- ("the years of the life of..."), and מִסְפַּר יְמֵי חַיֵּי- ("the number of the days of the life of..."), as well as with בְּ- + suffix ("during one's lifetime", PSA 49:19, 63:5, 146:2). Regularly paired in parallel with נֶפֶשׁ ("soul/self", e.g., PSA 26:9, LAM 3:58) and רוּחַ ("spirit/breath", JOB 7:7, ISA 38:16), and contrasted directly with מָוֶת ("death", DEU 30:19, PRO 12:28, JER 21:8) and שַׁחַת ("pit", PSA 103:4, JON 2:7). In JOB 24:22, the form ends in -în (חַיִּין). In 2SA 11:11, חַיֶּךָ functions alongside חֵי נַפְשֶׁךָ as a solemn oath formula.

core_meaning_summary: A feminine noun denoting the physical right hand, the right side or direction (usually contrasted with the left), a position of honor or support beside someone, and figuratively the instrument or emblem of power, victory, and oath-taking.

senses.definition: The physical hand on the right side of the body, used for grasping, blessing, skilled action, holding objects, or swearing oaths.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (often with pronominal suffix), or as second element in construct yad yĕmîn ('hand of right')

senses.definition: The right hand conceived metonymically as an agent or emblem of strength, deliverance, victory, support, or forceful action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subject of active verbs (e.g., 'uphold', 'acquire', 'find', 'do valiantly') or with instrumental preposition b- ('by means of')

senses.definition: The right side or right-hand direction relative to a person, object, or path (including attributive 'right' for paired body parts, and figuratively the favorable or sound course).
senses.grammatical_frame: With spatial prepositions (min, ʿal, l-), adverbially without preposition after verbs of turning (NUM 22:26, DEU 17:11, 1SA 6:12), or attributively in definite construct/apposition (LEV 7:32, LEV 9:21)

senses.definition: A station immediately beside a person's right side, denoting honored status, attendance, advocacy, or protective accompaniment.
senses.grammatical_frame: With prepositions ʿal or l- + person/suffix after verbs of standing or going

collocations_and_notes: Very frequently paired or contrasted with śĕmōʾl ('left'), forming merisms for 'any direction / any deviation' (NUM 22:26, DEU 17:11, 1SA 6:12, 2SA 2:19), 'on every side' (EXO 14:29, 1KI 7:49, 2CH 4:8, NEH 8:4, ISA 9:19, ZEC 4:11), or basic discernment (JON 4:11; cf. moral/practical inclination in ECC 10:2). Appears in the construct phrase yad yĕmîn ('right hand', JDG 3:15, JDG 7:20, 2SA 20:9) and as an attributive qualifier of anatomical parts (šôq hayyāmîn 'the right thigh', LEV 7:32, LEV 9:21). In 2KI 23:13, mîmîn l- specifies relative location ('to the right of', conventionally south when facing east). In poetic parallelism, yāmîn pairs with yād ('hand', PSA 21:9, PSA 89:14) and zĕrôaʿ ('arm', PSA 89:14).

core_meaning_summary: A verb whose stem distinctions express initiating an action (causative/active Hiphil, passive Hophal), treating something sacred or honorable as profane or open to common use (intensive/factitive Piel, passive Pual and Niphal), or being pierced/wounded internally (simple Qal).

senses.definition: To enter upon or initiate an action, state, or sequence; in the passive Hophal, for an action to be started by people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active) usually + l- + infinitive, or + imperative (DEU 2:24), or + min / b- indicating starting point (EZK 9:6); Hophal (impersonal passive) + l- + infinitive (GEN 4:26)

senses.definition: To treat what is sacred, consecrated, commanded, or honorable as ordinary, defiled, or violable; to strip of sanctity or honor (or, in passive stems, to be treated as profane).
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (transitive) + direct object (sanctuary, holy things, divine name, Sabbath, statutes, father, bed), or + min 'from' in expulsion as defiled (EZK 28:16); Pual (passive participle, EZK 36:23); Niphal (passive/reflexive, ISA 48:11, EZK 20:9, EZK 22:26, and possibly LEV 21:9)

senses.definition: To open a newly planted vineyard to ordinary, non-restricted use so its produce may be enjoyed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (transitive) with vineyard (kerem) as explicit or implied object

senses.definition: To be pierced, wounded, or stricken internally (said of the heart in distress).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive/stative) with subject lēb ('heart') + b- 'within'

collocations_and_notes: Strongly polarized by stem in the sampled corpus: (1) Hiphil (with impersonal passive Hophal in GEN 4:26) expresses initiation ('begin'), almost always governing l- + infinitive (e.g., GEN 10:8, DEU 3:24, JDG 16:19) and frequently paired contrastively with kālâ ('finish', 1CH 27:24, 2CH 29:17, 2CH 31:7), or taking min / b- for a starting point (EZK 9:6). (2) Piel (with passive Pual in EZK 36:23 and passive/reflexive Niphal in ISA 48:11, EZK 20:9, EZK 22:26) expresses profanation/desecration of sacred names, sanctuaries, offerings, Sabbaths, or honor, explicitly contrasted with qōdeš ('holy') in EZK 22:26 and paired with ṭimmēʾ ('make unclean') in LEV 20:3. In LEV 21:9, the first verb (tēḥēl l- + infinitive) reflects either passive/reflexive degradation ('she degrades/profanes herself by prostituting') or inception ('she begins to prostitute'), while the second (mĕḥallelēt) is active Piel ('she profanes her father'). (3) A specialized Piel usage with vineyards (kerem) in DEU 20:6 and JER 31:5 denotes releasing a newly planted vineyard from restriction for ordinary consumption. (4) Only one Qal form appears in the sample (PSA 109:22, with lēb 'heart'), denoting internal piercing or wounding.

core_meaning_summary: Predicative particle asserting existence, presence, possession, or availability, also used in affirmative replies, suffixed participial predications, and once substantively for wealth or substance.

senses.definition: Asserts the existence, occurrence, or spatial presence of an entity, state, or event, often in existential statements, questions, or conditional and apprehensive clauses, and with participles or relative markers to denote an indefinite member or subset ('there is one who / some who').
senses.grammatical_frame: existential particle + noun phrase / participle (often with locative prep. בְּ־ / עַל־, or interrogative הֲ־, or conditional אִם / פֶּן / אוּלַי)

senses.definition: Indicates possession, availability, entitlement, or capability belonging to a person or entity, and with an infinitive or the idiom יֶשׁ־לְאֵל יָד־ expresses having the means or power to act.
senses.grammatical_frame: particle + prep. לְ־ or אֵת (+ noun phrase or infinitive construct)

senses.definition: Functions as a predicative copula with an attached pronominal suffix before a participle in conditional clauses to express ongoing or intended action, or with אֵת + noun + adjective to predicate a state or quality.
senses.grammatical_frame: particle + pronominal suffix + participle; or particle + אֵת + noun + adjective

senses.definition: Serves as a standalone elliptical affirmation confirming existence, presence, or agreement in direct speech, including the doubled emphatic form יֵשׁ וָיֵשׁ.
senses.grammatical_frame: standalone predicate in dialogue (or doubled with conjunction וְ־)

senses.definition: Used substantively as a noun denoting tangible property, wealth, or enduring substance bequeathed as an inheritance, paralleled with treasuries.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine-like substantive object of verb (לְהַנְחִיל)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasts with the negative particle אַיִן/אֵין in alternative questions (הֲיֵשׁ ... אִם־אָיִן, EXO 17:7; NUM 13:20) and antithetical clauses (PRO 13:7; NEH 5:5). Commonly takes maqqef and shortens to יֶשׁ־ before nouns or prepositions, and accepts pronominal suffixes as יֶשְׁךָ (GEN 24:42; JDG 6:36). Notable idioms include יֶשׁ־לְאֵל יָדִי ('it is in my power', GEN 31:29), הֲיֵשׁ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ יָשָׁר ('is your heart right?', 2KI 10:15), and the emphatic doubled response יֵשׁ וָיֵשׁ (2KI 10:15). Also combines with אֲשֶׁר (NEH 5:2) or partitive מִן (NEH 5:5) to introduce indefinite subsets. In 1SA 21:9 it follows אִין in an unusual interrogative construction asking whether a weapon is on hand.

core_meaning_summary: Proclitic relative and subordinating particle introducing relative clauses, headless nominalized clauses, possessive expressions with לְ־, complement clauses, causal grounds, and compound temporal or comparative conjunctions.

senses.definition: Introduces a relative clause modifying an explicit nominal, pronominal, or temporal antecedent, including clauses with resumptive pronouns indicating possession or oblique relationships.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle prefixed to verb, participle, adjective, noun, or prepositional phrase after an antecedent

senses.definition: Introduces a headless relative clause functioning as a noun phrase (subject or object), frequently following מַה־, כֹּל, אֵת, or a preposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle without explicit nominal head, or following מַה־ / כֹּל / אֵת / preposition

senses.definition: Prefixed to the preposition לְ־ with a pronominal suffix to mark emphatic or appositional possession in relation to a preceding noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle + prep. לְ־ + pronominal suffix (שֶׁלִּי)

senses.definition: Functions as a subordinating complementizer introducing an object, explanatory, or circumstantial/concessive clause after verbs of knowing, questions, or evaluative statements.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle introducing finite verbal or nominal clause after main verb/predicate

senses.definition: Introduces a causal clause stating the reason or ground for a preceding statement or command, either alone or combined in בְּשַׁגַּם ('because indeed').
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle (or compound בְּשַׁגַּם) + nominal or verbal clause

senses.definition: Combines with prepositions or adverbs (עַד־שֶׁ־, כִּמְעַט שֶׁ־, כָּל־עֻמַּת שֶׁ־) to form compound conjunctions marking temporal limits, simultaneity, or exact comparison.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition/adverb (עַד / כִּמְעַט / כָּל־עֻמַּת) + proclitic particle + clause

collocations_and_notes: Proclitic particle regularly causing gemination (with dagesh forte) in the following consonant, vocalized שֶׁ־ (or שַׁ־ in the compound בְּשַׁגַּם in GEN 6:3). Predominates in Song of Songs, Ecclesiastes, and the later ascent psalms. Combines frequently with מַה־ ('what/that which', ECC 1:9; 3:15; 8:7), כֹּל ('all that/who', 1CH 5:20; ECC 2:7), אֵת ('the one whom', SNG 3:1, 4), לְ־ ('my own', SNG 1:6), and prepositions/adverbs such as עַד־, כִּמְעַט, בְּ־, and כָּל־עֻמַּת to form compound conjunctions. In relative clauses with oblique roles, a resumptive pronominal suffix often appears within the clause (e.g., PSA 146:5; ECC 2:21; 10:17).

core_meaning_summary: A chair or elevated seat of honor, especially the ceremonial throne of a king or of God, and by extension royal rule, dynasty, or judicial and administrative authority.

senses.definition: A physical chair or seat for sitting, such as a seat at a doorway, a priest's seat beside a sanctuary entrance, or a seat of honor placed for a guest.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; object of a preposition (`עַל`) or verb (`שׂים`, 'set/place')

senses.definition: An ornate ceremonial seat or elevated chair occupied by a monarch or envisioned as occupied by God, symbolizing royal rank, precedence, or divine majesty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine (variant `כִּסֵּה`); commonly with `יָשַׁב עַל` ('sit upon'), `קוּם מִן` ('rise from'), or `שׂים` / `נתן` ('set, place')

senses.definition: Royal office, dynastic succession, sovereign power, or a seat of judicial and administrative authority, whether human or divine.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine (also shortened variant `כֵּס` and plural `כִסְאוֹת`); often in construct before a ruler, kingdom, or quality, or as object of verbs of establishing (`הֵקִים`, `כּוֹנֵן`, `סָעַד`)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently governed by `יָשַׁב עַל` ('sit upon', indicating occupancy of a seat or accession to royal rule) and `הֵקִים` / `כּוֹנֵן` / `סָעַד` ('establish / uphold', indicating continuity of dynasty or government). Note orthographic variants: `כֵּס` in EXO 17:16 (`כֵּס יָהּ`) and `כִּסֵּה` in 1KI 10:19; the plural `כִסְאוֹת` / `כִּסְאֹת` appears in PSA 122:5. Construct expressions include `כִּסֵּא דָוִד` ('throne of David'), `כִּסֵּא יִשְׂרָאֵל` ('throne of Israel'), `כִּסֵּא הַמְּלוּכָה` / `כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּתוֹ` ('royal throne'), and `כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ` ('throne of your glory').

core_meaning_summary: The sun as a luminous celestial body, also used to mark times of day (sunrise and sunset), cardinal directions (east and west), and the earthly sphere of human life.

senses.definition: The sun, the bright celestial body in the sky that supplies daylight and heat, moves across the heavens, serves as an emblem of permanence, and is sometimes treated as an object of worship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (with both masculine and feminine verbal/pronominal agreement); definite or indefinite, functioning as subject, direct object, or object of a preposition

senses.definition: The sun as a marker of time of day, specifically sunrise (with verbs of shining forth) or sunset (with verbs of going in).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in temporal clauses or construct phrases with verbs or infinitives of rising (`זרח`) or setting (`בוא`)

senses.definition: The cardinal directions east or west, designated by the point of the sun's rising or setting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct chains governed by `מִזְרָח` ('rising') or `מָבוֹא` ('going in / setting'), frequently with directional endings or prepositions (`מִן`, `עַד`)

senses.definition: The earthly world of mortal life and human activity, expressed in the spatial idiom 'under the sun'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by the preposition `תַּחַת` ('under') in the fixed expression `תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ`

senses.definition: Figuratively, a person's vitality, well-being, or span of prosperity, whose sudden 'setting' while still day signifies premature ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with a possessive suffix as subject of `בָּא` ('has set') in poetic metaphor

collocations_and_notes: Common collocations include `בּוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` / `מְבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` ('going in / setting of the sun', i.e., sunset or west), `זָרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` / `מִזְרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` ('rising of the sun', i.e., sunrise or east), and the fixed phrase `תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ` ('under the sun', frequent in Ecclesiastes). Frequently paired with `יָרֵחַ` ('moon') and `כּוֹכָבִים` ('stars'). Grammatically, `שֶׁמֶשׁ` displays variable gender agreement, taking masculine verbs and suffixes in most occurrences (e.g., GEN 15:12; EXO 16:21; JOS 10:13; PSA 113:3; JER 15:9) and feminine verbs in others (2SA 2:24; ISA 38:8; JON 4:8). With pronominal suffixes, the stem appears as `שִׁמְשׁ־` (JER 15:9).

core_meaning_summary: To slaughter an animal (or, in condemned or figurative contexts, humans) as a ritual sacrifice to a deity or for a meal/feast.

senses.definition: To slaughter and present an animal as a ritual offering to YHWH or to another deity, often accompanied by a communal meal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb; used transitively with an animal or cognate sacrifice-noun object, with or without לְ ('to') or לִפְנֵי ('before') + deity, or intransitively/absolutely.

senses.definition: To practice sacrificing habitually or repeatedly, especially at high places, to foreign deities, or to objects of devotion, frequently paired with burning incense.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive active verb; typically intransitive with locative בְּ ('at/on') or recipient לְ ('to') or associative עִם ('with').

senses.definition: To slaughter human beings in idolatrous sacrifice, or figuratively to prepare a great slaughter-feast of victims.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb; transitive with human direct objects or cognate זֶבַח ('sacrifice/feast') and recipient לְ ('to/for').

senses.definition: To slaughter livestock for meat or for a communal feast, including non-sanctuary slaughter for food away from the chosen altar.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb; transitive with livestock direct object or partitive מִן ('from') + herd/flock, followed by eating/feasting verbs.

collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes the cognate noun זֶבַח ("sacrifice") as direct object (GEN 31:54, LEV 22:29, DEU 33:19, JDG 16:23, 1SA 1:21, 1KI 8:62, PSA 4:6, PSA 107:22) and marks the divine recipient with לְ ("to", e.g., לַיהוָה "to YHWH", לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם/לַשְּׂעִירִם "to other gods/goat-demons") or לִפְנֵי ("before", LEV 9:4, 1KI 8:62, 2CH 7:4). Often paired in cultic contexts with burning incense/offerings (קטר, 1KI 11:8, 2KI 15:4, HAB 1:16) or offering burnt offerings (הֶעֱלָה עֹלוֹת, 1SA 6:15). Stem usage shows a clear contrast: the simple active stem is used for individual or narrated acts of slaughtering/sacrificing (both cultic and domestic), while the intensive active stem appears predominantly in participles and imperfects expressing habitual or repeated cultic sacrificing, especially at high places or to foreign/idolatrous recipients (1KI 3:2, 1KI 11:8, 2KI 15:4, 2CH 28:23, HOS 4:14, HAB 1:16; note the immediate shift from simple active narrative action to intensive active resolve within 2CH 28:23).

core_meaning_summary: The feminine-agreement numeral component meaning 'ten' ('-teen') used in compound numbers from eleven through nineteen.

senses.definition: Ten, as the second element in cardinal compound numerals (eleven through nineteen) counting feminine nouns of time, measurement, objects, cities, or persons.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine compound numeral element following a unit numeral (1–9); precedes a singular/plural counted noun, follows a plural counted noun, or stands predicatively/elliptically.

senses.definition: Ten, as the second element in compound numerals functioning ordinally (eleventh through eighteenth) in regnal or calendar year dates.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine compound numeral element in chronological phrases: following construct שְׁנַת ('year of'), following the definite noun הַשָּׁנָה with definite unit numeral (1KI 6:38), or in prepositional בְּ + compound numeral + שָׁנָה ('in the Nth year').

collocations_and_notes: Always occurs as the second component of compound numerals for 11 through 19, paired with feminine-form unit numerals: אַחַת/עַשְׁתֵּי (11), שְׁתֵּים/שְׁתֵּי (12), שְׁלֹשׁ/שְׁלוֹשׁ (13), אַרְבַּע (14), חֲמֵשׁ (15), שֵׁשׁ (16), שְׁבַע (17), שְׁמֹנֶה/שְׁמוֹנֶה (18), and תְּשַׁע (19). Consistently modifies feminine nouns (e.g., שָׁנָה 'year', אַמָּה 'cubit', עִיר/עָרִים 'city/cities', יְרִיעֹת 'curtains', אֲבָנִים 'stones', מַצֵּבָה 'pillar', קַעֲרֹת 'dishes', כַּפּוֹת 'spoons', נָפֶשׁ 'person', נָשִׁים 'wives', בָּנוֹת 'daughters'), in explicit contrast to masculine-agreement עָשָׂר in the same verses (EXO 24:4, EXO 39:14, NUM 7:84, EZK 32:1). In EZK 43:16, שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה stands elliptically without an explicit unit of measurement before אֹרֶךְ ('length') and רֹחַב ('width').

verses.EXO 27:14: וַ חֲמֵ֨שׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה】 אַמָּ֛ה קְלָעִ֖ים לַ כָּתֵ֑ף עַמֻּדֵי הֶ֣ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְ אַדְנֵי הֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה
verses.EXO 36:15: אֹ֜רֶךְ הַ יְרִיעָ֣ה הָ אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁים֙ בָּֽ אַמָּ֔ה וְ אַרְבַּ֣ע אַמּ֔וֹת רֹ֖חַב הַ יְרִיעָ֣ה הָ אֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְ עַשְׁתֵּ֥י 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 יְרִיעֹֽת
verses.EXO 39:14: וְ֠ הָ אֲבָנִים עַל שְׁמֹ֨ת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל הֵ֛נָּה שְׁתֵּ֥ים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 עַל שְׁמֹתָ֑ ם פִּתּוּחֵ֤י חֹתָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל שְׁמ֔ וֹ לִ שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר שָֽׁבֶט
verses.NUM 7:84: זֹ֣את חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַ מִּזְבֵּ֗חַ בְּ יוֹם֙ הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֔ וֹ מֵ אֵ֖ת נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל קַעֲרֹ֨ת כֶּ֜סֶף שְׁתֵּ֣ים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֗ה】 מִֽזְרְקֵי כֶ֨סֶף֙ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ר כַּפּ֥וֹת זָהָ֖ב שְׁתֵּ֥ים 【עֶשְׂרֵֽה】
verses.JOS 4:8: וַ יַּעֲשׂוּ כֵ֣ן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל כַּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ וַ יִּשְׂא֡וּ שְׁתֵּֽי 【עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה】 אֲבָנִ֜ים מִ תּ֣וֹךְ הַ יַּרְדֵּ֗ן כַּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ לְ מִסְפַּ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַ יַּעֲבִר֤וּ ם עִמָּ ם֙ אֶל הַ מָּל֔וֹן וַ יַּנִּח֖וּ ם שָֽׁם
verses.JOS 15:36: וְ שַׁעֲרַ֨יִם֙ וַ עֲדִיתַ֔יִם וְ הַ גְּדֵרָ֖ה וּ גְדֵרֹתָ֑יִם עָרִ֥ים אַרְבַּֽע 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 וְ חַצְרֵי הֶֽן
verses.JOS 18:24: וּ כְפַ֧ר הָֽעַמֹּנָ֛ה וְ הָֽ עָפְנִ֖י וָ גָ֑בַע עָרִ֥ים שְׁתֵּים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 וְ חַצְרֵי הֶֽן
verses.JOS 19:22: וּ פָגַע֩ הַ גְּב֨וּל בְּ תָב֤וֹר וְ שַׁחֲצִ֨ימָ ה֙ וּ בֵ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ וְ הָי֛וּ תֹּצְא֥וֹת גְּבוּלָ֖ ם הַ יַּרְדֵּ֑ן עָרִ֥ים שֵׁשׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 וְ חַצְרֵי הֶֽן
verses.JOS 21:6: וְ לִ בְנֵ֣י גֵרְשׁ֗וֹן מִ מִּשְׁפְּח֣וֹת מַטֵּֽה יִשָּׂשכָ֣ר וּ מִ מַּטֵּֽה אָ֠שֵׁר וּ מִ מַּטֵּ֨ה נַפְתָּלִ֜י וּ֠ מֵ חֲצִי מַטֵּ֨ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בַ בָּשָׁן֙ בַּ גּוֹרָ֔ל עָרִ֖ים שְׁלֹ֥שׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵֽה】
verses.JOS 21:33: כָּל עָרֵ֥י הַ גֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י לְ מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ ם שְׁלֹשׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה】 עִ֖יר וּ מִגְרְשֵׁי הֶֽן
verses.1KI 7:15: וַ יָּ֛צַר אֶת שְׁנֵ֥י הָ עַמּוּדִ֖ים נְחֹ֑שֶׁת שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה 【עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה】 אַמָּ֗ה קוֹמַת֙ הָ עַמּ֣וּד הָ אֶחָ֔ד וְ חוּט֙ שְׁתֵּים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה】 אַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֖ב אֶת הָ עַמּ֥וּד הַ שֵּׁנִֽי
verses.1KI 16:23: בִּ שְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וְ אַחַ֜ת שָׁנָ֗ה לְ אָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֤ךְ עָמְרִי֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 שָׁנָ֑ה בְּ תִרְצָ֖ה מָלַ֥ךְ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִֽים
verses.2KI 3:1: וִ יהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּ שְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה 【עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה】 לִ יהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַ יִּמְלֹ֖ךְ שְׁתֵּים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה】 שָׁנָֽה
verses.2KI 13:1: בִּ שְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְ שָׁלֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָחָ֨ז בֶּן יֵה֤וּא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן שְׁבַ֥ע 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 שָׁנָֽה
verses.2KI 24:18: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְ אַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְ מָלְכ֔ וֹ וְ אַחַ֤ת 【עֶשְׂרֵה֙】 שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔ וֹ חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִ לִּבְנָֽה
verses.2KI 25:17: שְׁמֹנֶה֩ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה】 אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָ עַמּ֣וּד הָ אֶחָ֗ד וְ כֹתֶ֨רֶת עָלָ֥י ו נְחֹשֶׁת֮ וְ קוֹמַ֣ת הַ כֹּתֶרֶת֮ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ אַמּוֹת֒ וּ שְׂבָכָ֨ה וְ רִמֹּנִ֧ים עַֽל הַ כֹּתֶ֛רֶת סָבִ֖יב הַ כֹּ֣ל נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְ כָ אֵ֛לֶּה לַֽ עַמּ֥וּד הַ שֵּׁנִ֖י עַל הַ שְּׂבָכָֽה
verses.2CH 11:21: וַ יֶּאֱהַ֨ב רְחַבְעָ֜ם אֶת מַעֲכָ֣ה בַת אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם מִ כָּל נָשָׁי ו֙ וּ פִ֣ילַגְשָׁ֔י ו כִּ֠י נָשִׁ֤ים שְׁמוֹנֶֽה 【עֶשְׂרֵה֙】 נָשָׂ֔א וּ פִֽילַגְשִׁ֖ים שִׁשִּׁ֑ים וַ יּ֗וֹלֶד עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וּ שְׁמוֹנָ֛ה בָּנִ֖ים וְ שִׁשִּׁ֥ים בָּנֽוֹת
verses.2CH 13:21: וַ יִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק אֲבִיָּ֔הוּ וַ יִּ֨שָּׂא ל֔ וֹ נָשִׁ֖ים אַרְבַּ֣ע 【עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה】 וַ יּ֗וֹלֶד עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּ שְׁנַ֨יִם֙ בָּנִ֔ים וְ שֵׁ֥שׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 בָּנֽוֹת
verses.2CH 25:25: וַ יְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ בֶן יוֹאָשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת יוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲמֵ֥שׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 שָׁנָֽה
verses.2CH 27:8: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְ חָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְ מָלְכ֑ וֹ וְ שֵׁשׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה】 שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ ירוּשָׁלִָֽם
verses.2CH 36:5: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְ חָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים בְּ מָלְכ֔ וֹ וְ אַחַ֤ת 【עֶשְׂרֵה֙】 שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַ יַּ֣עַשׂ הָ רַ֔ע בְּ עֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי ו
verses.JER 1:3: וַ יְהִ֗י בִּ ימֵ֨י יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַד תֹּם֙ עַשְׁתֵּ֣י 【עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה】 שָׁנָ֔ה לְ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ בֶן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה עַד גְּל֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּ חֹ֥דֶשׁ הַ חֲמִישִֽׁי
verses.JER 52:21: וְ הָ עַמּוּדִ֗ים שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה 【עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה】 אַמָּה֙ קוֹמַת֙ הָ עַמֻּ֣ד הָ אֶחָ֔ד וְ ח֛וּט שְׁתֵּים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה】 אַמָּ֖ה יְסֻבֶּ֑ נּוּ וְ עָבְי֛ וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע אַצְבָּע֖וֹת נָבֽוּב
verses.EZK 40:11: וַ יָּ֛מָד אֶת רֹ֥חַב פֶּֽתַח הַ שַּׁ֖עַר עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּ֑וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַ שַּׁ֔עַר שְׁל֥וֹשׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 אַמּֽוֹת
verses.EZK 43:16: וְ הָ אֲרִיאֵ֗ל שְׁתֵּ֤ים 【עֶשְׂרֵה֙】 אֹ֔רֶךְ בִּ שְׁתֵּ֥ים 【עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה】 רֹ֑חַב רָב֕וּעַ אֶ֖ל אַרְבַּ֥עַת רְבָעָֽי ו
verses.GEN 14:5: וּ בְ אַרְבַּע֩ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה】 שָׁנָ֜ה בָּ֣א כְדָרְלָעֹ֗מֶר וְ הַ מְּלָכִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔ וֹ וַ יַּכּ֤וּ אֶת רְפָאִים֙ בְּ עַשְׁתְּרֹ֣ת קַרְנַ֔יִם וְ אֶת הַ זּוּזִ֖ים בְּ הָ֑ם וְ אֵת֙ הָֽ אֵימִ֔ים בְּ שָׁוֵ֖ה קִרְיָתָֽיִם
verses.1KI 6:38: וּ בַ שָּׁנָה֩ הָ אַחַ֨ת 【עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה】 בְּ יֶ֣רַח בּ֗וּל ה֚וּא הַ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הַ שְּׁמִינִ֔י כָּלָ֣ה הַ בַּ֔יִת לְ כָל דְּבָרָ֖י ו וּ לְ כָל מִשְׁפָּטָ֑י ו וַ יִּבְנֵ֖ הוּ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים
verses.2KI 14:23: בִּ שְׁנַת֙ חֲמֵשׁ 【עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה】 שָׁנָ֔ה לַ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יָרָבְעָ֨ם בֶּן יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְ אַחַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה
verses.2KI 16:1: בִּ שְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַֽע 【עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה】 שָׁנָ֔ה לְ פֶ֖קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ מָלַ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בֶּן יוֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

core_meaning_summary: As a verb, to complete, make restitution, fulfill a vow, or repay/requite; as an adjective, whole, complete, peaceful, or undivided; also a place name (Salem).

senses.definition: To reach completion or finish a task or structure; in causative/factitive use, to carry a decree through to completion or bring a life to an end.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple intransitive (Qal: subject is structure); factitive active (Piel: with direct object); causative active (Hiphil: with object decree or person)

senses.definition: To make restitution, compensate, or repay for loss, damage, theft, sacred offense, or a financial loan.
senses.grammatical_frame: Factitive active (Piel, frequently reinforced by infinitive absolute שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם) with object of loss/debt or recipient with לְ

senses.definition: To fulfill or pay a vow made to God; in the passive stem, for a vow to be fulfilled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Factitive active (Piel) with object נֶדֶר ('vow') and recipient לְ ('to God'); passive (Pual) with נֶדֶר as subject

senses.definition: To repay, reward, or requite someone in kind for good or evil deeds; in the passive stem, to be repaid or recompensed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Factitive active (Piel) with person (with לְ / אֶל or direct object) and deed/requital; passive (Pual) for person or good/evil being repaid

senses.definition: Whole, full, entire, or uncut (of stone left intact from the quarry, full wages, or an entire body of captives).
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying a noun (feminine singular שְׁלֵמָה)

senses.definition: Undivided, wholly devoted, or loyal (especially describing the heart toward God or a ruler), or peaceful and well-disposed toward others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying לֵב/לֵבָב ('heart') or predicate adjective with אֶת ('with' someone)

senses.definition: Salem, a place name of which Melchizedek is king.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun in construct phrase מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם ('king of Salem')

collocations_and_notes: The evidence packet spans verbal forms across four stems, adjectival forms, and one proper place name. Stem contrasts in the verb: simple active/intransitive (Qal) denotes reaching completion ('be finished', NEH 6:15); intensive/factitive active (Piel) denotes making something whole or settled—finishing a structure, paying back restitution or a loan, fulfilling a vow, or requiting deeds (often reinforced with an infinitive absolute שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם for legal certainty in EXO 21:36, 22:2, 22:5, JER 51:56); passive of Piel (Pual) denotes being fulfilled or repaid (PSA 65:2, PRO 11:31, JER 18:20); causative active (Hiphil) denotes carrying a decree to completion (JOB 23:14) or bringing someone to an end (ISA 38:13). Adjectival uses frequently collocate with לֵב / לֵבָב ('whole/undivided heart', e.g., 1KI 15:14, 1CH 12:39, 1CH 29:19, 2CH 15:17).

core_meaning_summary: To throw, hurl, discard, or cast down/out physically, ritually, or figuratively (used in causative active and passive stems).

senses.definition: To propel, throw, hurl, drop, or scatter a physical object or person onto a surface, into a container/pit/fire, or upon/at someone; in the passive stem, to be thrown.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with direct object and goal/locative (e.g., 'into', 'upon', 'to the ground'); causative passive (Hophal) for being thrown

senses.definition: To throw away, dispose of, leave behind, or abandon unwanted, defiled, or helpless items or persons; in the passive stem, to lie abandoned or exposed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with direct object (often with 'outside', 'from oneself'); causative passive (Hophal) with subject exposed/unburied

senses.definition: To cast down from height or standing, overthrow, banish to another place, or expel from someone's presence; in the passive stem, to be cast out or overthrown.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with personal/spatial object and source/goal ('from before', 'to another land', 'to the earth'); causative passive (Hophal)

senses.definition: To cast lots or a measuring cord in order to apportion land or determine an allotment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with object גּוֹרָל ('lot') or חֶבֶל ('measuring cord')

senses.definition: To put away or disregard something by figuratively throwing it behind one's back (teaching or sins), or to expose one's life to danger by casting it forward.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) in idiomatic phrases with אַחֲרֵי גַוּוֹ ('behind one's back') or נַפְשׁוֹ מִנֶּגֶד ('one's life out in front')

collocations_and_notes: Observed in the evidence packet solely in the causative active stem (Hiphil: to throw, cast, discard, banish) and its corresponding causative passive stem (Hophal: to be thrown, left exposed/abandoned, cast out). Frequent directional complements include אֶל ('into/onto'), עַל ('upon/against'), מִפְּנֵי / מִלִּפְנֵי / מֵעַל פָּנַי ('out of someone's sight/presence'), and locatives with directional ה (אַרְצָה 'to the ground', הַבֹּרָה 'into the pit'). Notable idioms: הִשְׁלִיךְ אַחֲרֵי גַוּוֹ/גֵוְךָ ('to cast behind one's back' — of willfully disregarding divine instruction in NEH 9:26 or putting away sins in ISA 38:17); הִשְׁלִיךְ נַפְשׁוֹ מִנֶּגֶד ('to cast one's life out in front', i.e., risk one's life, JDG 9:17); and הִשְׁלִיךְ גּוֹרָל / חֶבֶל בְּגוֹרָל ('to cast a lot / measuring line by lot', JOS 18:8, MIC 2:5). In AMO 4:3, the Hiphil second-person feminine plural form וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּנָה lacks an explicit direct object and functions either as an idiomatic expression of forced expulsion or with an implied object toward הַהַרְמוֹנָה.

core_meaning_summary: To think, plan, or devise mentally, extending across stems to artistic designing, reckoning or crediting value and status, calculating amounts, pondering, and being regarded in a particular way.

senses.definition: To form an intention, plot, or scheme in the mind toward a good or harmful outcome, either in the simple active stem or the intensive active stem.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in simple active stem (Qal), or intensive active stem (Piel in DAN 11:24); with direct object (רָעָה, אָוֶן, מַחֲשָׁבָה), לְ + infinitive, or עַל indicating target or beneficiary

senses.definition: To conceive and fashion intricate artistic patterns, textiles, metalwork, or mechanical contrivances; its active participle functions as a title for a skilled designer or master weaver.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in simple active stem (Qal), infinitive with cognate object מַחֲשָׁבֹת or active participle (חֹשֵׁב / חוֹשֵׁב) used substantively in construct phrases (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב, חֹשְׁבֵי מַחֲשָׁבֹת)

senses.definition: To credit or impute an action or moral quality to someone's account, or to regard and value a person or thing at a given worth or role.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in simple active stem (Qal); takes direct object with indirect recipient (לְ) and/or predicate noun (with or without לְ), or direct object alone when meaning to esteem/value

senses.definition: In the intensive active stem, to compute a proportional monetary sum, or to reflect thoughtfully upon, consider, and take careful notice of someone or something.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in intensive active stem (Piel); with direct object (כֶּסֶף, יָמִים, דְּרָכַי, or pronominal suffix) and optional לְ for the person affected
senses.semantic_domain: Cognition and Accounting / Calculation and Reflection

senses.definition: In the passive stem, to be counted, credited, settled in financial accounting, or regarded as having a certain status, classification, or worth.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in passive stem (Niphal); paired with prepositions לְ, עַל, כְּ, כְּמוֹ, or אֵת, or with a predicate noun or adjective

collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes the cognate object מַחֲשָׁבָה / מַחֲשָׁבֹת (EXO 31:4, EXO 35:35, JER 49:30, DAN 11:24) as well as moral or emotional nouns such as רָעָה (GEN 50:20, JER 18:8, NAM 1:11), אָוֶן (PSA 36:5, MIC 2:1), טֹבָה (GEN 50:20), עָוֺן (2SA 19:20, PSA 32:2), and צְדָקָה (GEN 15:6). Distinct stems express clear voice and aspectual differences: simple active (Qal) covers intending, designing, and crediting/regarding; intensive active (Piel) appears for calculating sums, pondering thoughtfully, and scheming; passive (Niphal) consistently marks being counted, accounted for, or regarded as something.
