core_meaning_summary: A large flowing watercourse or river, used especially with the definite article for the Euphrates as a geographical landmark, and extended poetically to surging floodwaters or continuous abundance.

senses.definition: A natural or channeled perennial watercourse of substantial flow, whether named in construct or spoken of generally as a geographical feature that waters land, borders settlements, or is divided or dried up.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, masculine singular or plural; frequently in construct before a proper name (e.g., נְהַר פְּרָת, נְהַר כְּבָר) or as subject/object of verbs of flowing, watering, or drying up

senses.definition: Specifically the Euphrates River, referred to absolutely with the definite article as a premier territorial boundary or in the regional expression 'beyond the River.'
senses.grammatical_frame: noun with definite article (הַנָּהָר), often in prepositional boundary phrases (מִן, עַד, בְּעֵבֶר, מֵעֵבֶר לְ) or apposition with נְהַר פְּרָת

senses.definition: Surging currents, deep oceanic waters, or an overwhelming torrent of water, often depicted in poetic parallelism with the sea or breaking waves.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, plural (נְהָרוֹת) or anarthrous singular in poetry, paired with יָם / יַמִּים or מַיִם רַבִּים

senses.definition: Used figuratively in similes to represent a steady, abundant, and unbroken flow of peace or prosperity.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular noun following comparative כְּ (כַּנָּהָר / כְּנָהָר) with abstract subject or object שָׁלוֹם

collocations_and_notes: Plural forms appear both as נְהָרוֹת (e.g., PSA 24:2, ISA 42:15, EZK 31:15) and נְהָרִים (ISA 18:7). Frequently appears in construct with geographical names: נְהַר פְּרָת (GEN 15:18, DEU 1:7, JER 46:6), נְהַר מִצְרַיִם (GEN 15:18), נְהַר גּוֹזָן (2KI 18:11), נְהַר כְּבָר (EZK 3:15, EZK 10:20). The definite phrase עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר / מֵעֵבֶר לַנָּהָר denotes the territory and later imperial province across the Euphrates (JOS 24:2, 1KI 14:15, EZR 8:36, NEH 3:7). Poetic parallels include יָם / יַמִּים (PSA 24:2, PSA 72:8, PSA 80:12, JON 2:4), מַיִם (PSA 105:41, ISA 43:20, SNG 8:7), and נַחַל (ISA 27:12, ISA 66:12).

core_meaning_summary: To grow up or become great in size, status, or severity; in causative and intensive stems, to raise children, exalt someone or something, increase, or boast arrogantly.

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with a child, animal, personified city, or horn as subject, to grow physically, mature into adulthood, or expand in size and territorial reach.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal, intransitive (or with suffixal/comitative complement)

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with persons, wealth, power, deeds, pain, reputation, or life as subject (often with מִן "than", בְּעֵינֵי "in the eyes of", or עַל "over"), to become wealthy, powerful, renowned, severe, or highly valued.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + מִן / בְּעֵינֵי / עַל / עַד

senses.definition: In the intensive (Piel) stem, with children as direct object, to nurture, rear, and bring up offspring.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel + direct object (children)

senses.definition: In the intensive (Piel) stem, with a person or name (שֵׁם) as direct object (often with בְּעֵינֵי/לְעֵינֵי), to elevate in rank, honor, or renown.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel + direct object (person or name) + בְּעֵינֵי / לְעֵינֵי

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem, with abstract or concrete objects (such as kindness, wisdom, instruction, or a weight) or with לַעֲשׂוֹת ("to do"), to increase, enlarge, glorify, or perform great deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil + direct object / לַעֲשׂוֹת + עִם

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem—frequently with עַל ("against"), בְּפִיכֶם ("with your mouth"), בִּלְבָבוֹ ("in his heart"), or absolutely—and in the reflexive (Hithpael) stem with עַל, to exalt oneself, assert dominance, or boast arrogantly over another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (with עַל / בְּ / absolute) or Hithpael + עַל

collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears in Qal with בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") for high valuation, with מִן ("than") for superiority, and with עִם/אֵת ("with") when describing growing up together. In Piel, frequently pairs with רֹמֵם ("to raise/exalt") for rearing children and with לְעֵינֵי/בְּעֵינֵי for elevating a leader. In Hiphil and Hithpael, commonly takes עַל ("against/over") to express arrogance or boasting. In AMO 8:5, Hiphil הַגְדִּיל ("make large") directly contrasts with הַקְטִין ("make small").

core_meaning_summary: To be good, pleasing, or favorable; in the causative stem, to do good, act rightly, improve, or perform an action thoroughly.

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, used impersonally with לְ ("for/to") to express that circumstances turn out favorably or beneficially for someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal, impersonal + לְ (beneficiary)

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with a matter, proposal, or person as subject and בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") or לִפְנֵי ("before"), to be pleasing, acceptable, or approved by someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + בְּעֵינֵי / לִפְנֵי (experiencer)

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with לֵב or לְבָב ("heart") as subject, to become cheerful, glad, or content, especially after eating and drinking.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + לֵב / לְבָב as subject

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem with comparative מִן ("than"), to be in a superior or more secure condition than another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + מִן (comparative)

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem, intransitively or with לְ, עִם, or a direct object (אֶת), to confer benefit, treat kindly, or act beneficially toward someone (often contrasted with doing harm); in 1SA 20:13 with אֶל, to deem good or see fit to bring something about.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil, intransitive or + לְ / עִם / אֶת / אֶל

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem, with a direct object (such as ways, deeds, or face) or an infinitival complement, to act rightly, reform or amend conduct, brighten an appearance, or perform an action accurately or stately.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil + direct object / לְ + infinitive / intransitive

senses.definition: As a causative (Hiphil) infinitive absolute modifying another verb, indicating that the action or state is carried out thoroughly, completely, carefully, or rightly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil infinitive absolute functioning adverbially with a finite verb

collocations_and_notes: Frequently collocates in Qal with בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") or לִפְנֵי ("before") to express approval, and with לֵב/לְבָב ("heart") to describe cheerfulness or contentment. In Hiphil, commonly contrasts with הָרַע ("to do harm/evil") and pairs with דְּרָכִים ("ways") and מַעַלְלִים ("deeds") for moral reform. The Hiphil infinitive absolute הֵיטֵב frequently functions adverbially to express thoroughness. In 1SA 20:13, Hiphil appears with אֶל ("to") and אֶת הָרָעָה ("the harm") to express what seems good or fitting to someone.

core_meaning_summary: A verb whose passive/reflexive stems express feeling regret, relenting from an action, or being consoled, while its intensive/factitive stem means to comfort, console, or bring relief.

senses.definition: To experience regret, remorse, or sorrowful compassion over a past deed, situation, or someone's plight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (passive/reflexive stem), used absolutely, with כִּי introducing the regretted act, with לְ for the person pitied, or with עַל specifying the state of humiliation

senses.definition: To change one's mind or intention and turn away from an announced judgment, blessing, or anger out of forbearance or compassion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (passive/reflexive stem) used absolutely or with עַל / אֶל ('concerning'); also Hithpael (reflexive stem) with עַל in DEU 32:36

senses.definition: To console, soothe, or bring relief to someone in grief, hardship, or distress; in passive and reflexive stems, to receive consolation or be reconciled to a loss or calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (intensive/factitive stem) with direct object (person or place) and optional מִן ('from toil') or עַל ('concerning'); Pual (passive of Piel) 'be comforted'; Hithpael (reflexive stem) 'let oneself be comforted'; Niphal (passive/reflexive stem) in EZK 14:22 'be consoled / reconciled'

collocations_and_notes: Shows a sharp functional division by verbal stem. In the Niphal passive/reflexive stem, it overwhelmingly expresses internal sorrow, regret (with כִּי clauses in GEN 6:7, 1SA 15:11, 1SA 15:35), or relenting/changing an announced course of action (frequently with עַל or אֶל introducing הָרָעָה 'the disaster' or הַטּוֹבָה 'the good', as in EXO 32:12, JER 18:10, JER 26:13, JER 42:10, JOL 2:13, JON 3:10); in EZK 14:22, however, the Niphal describes the exiles being consoled or reconciled regarding Jerusalem's disaster. In the Piel intensive/factitive stem (and its passive Pual counterpart in ISA 54:11, ISA 66:13), it consistently means 'comfort, console, bring relief' (parallel to דִּבֶּר עַל לֵב 'speak kindly' in GEN 50:21, and נוּד 'show sympathy' in JOB 2:11, PSA 69:21, ISA 51:19). In the Hithpael reflexive stem, it means 'allow oneself to be comforted' when paired with מֵאֵן 'refuse' (GEN 37:35, JER 31:15), while with עַל in DEU 32:36 it parallels יָדִין ('vindicate') and means 'have compassion / relent toward'.

core_meaning_summary: To care for or raise (in the simple active participle); to be firm, enduring, established, or trustworthy (in the passive/reflexive stem); and to trust, rely on, or believe (in the causative stem).

senses.definition: One who nurses, cares for, or raises a child as a caregiver, guardian, or tutor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active participle used substantivally (masculine plural or feminine singular)

senses.definition: To be physically firm, secure, enduring, or long-lasting (used of a secure place, a lasting royal house, enduring mercies, or chronic plagues).
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal participle modifying nouns of place, dynasty, covenant blessing, or affliction

senses.definition: To be confirmed, proved true, established securely, or found faithful and reliable in character or speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal finite verb or participle describing words, people, God, or a city

senses.definition: To trust, rely on, accept as true, or be convinced of something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil verb + בְּ ("in"), לְ ("to/in"), infinitive construct, כִּי clause, or absolute

senses.definition: When negated with "life" as object, to have no certainty or assurance of survival.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negated Hiphil verb + בְּ + חַיִּים ("life")

collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear contrast across stems: the Qal participle denotes a caregiver or tutor raising a child (2SA 4:4, 2KI 10:1); the Niphal expresses being firm, enduring, established, or trustworthy (often modifying בַּיִת "house/dynasty", עֵד "witness", or God's words/commands); and the Hiphil expresses placing trust or belief in someone or something (regularly taking בְּ for trusting a person/God/commandments, לְ for believing a speaker, message, or sign, and כִּי clauses for believing a proposition). Deliberate wordplay pairing the Hiphil ("trust") and Niphal ("be made secure/established") occurs in 2CH 20:20 and ISA 7:9. In JOB 39:24, לֹא יַאֲמִין כִּי קוֹל שׁוֹפָר idiomatically depicts the warhorse's eagerness at the horn blast (scarcely believing or unable to hold back at the sound).

core_meaning_summary: A preposition expressing spatial enclosure or passage through an opening, as well as acting on behalf of, on account of, or in exchange for someone or something.

senses.definition: Spatial enclosure or closing off around a person or object, whether shutting in, hedging about, shielding, or closing in upon.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition following verbs of shutting/closing (סָגַר, עָצַר), hedging (שׂוּךְ), shielding (מָגֵן), or approaching/confronting (קָדַם)

senses.definition: Spatial passage or line of sight passing through an opening, barrier, or covering (such as a window, lattice, cloud, or veil).
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition (or compound מִבַּעַד לְ) with verbs of looking, falling, or judging, or in nominal phrases describing partial visibility

senses.definition: Acting in favor of, in defense of, or as an intermediary for someone, or taking action on account of a situation such as sin or calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition with verbs of praying, inquiring of God, making atonement/offerings, fighting/strengthening, giving a bribe/ransom, or fulfilling a purpose

senses.definition: Substitution or equivalence in an exchange or change of state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition in nominal comparison or with נָתַן ('give') and הָיָה ('serve as / become')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes pronominal suffixes (e.g., בַּעֲדִי, בַּעַדְךָ, בַּעֲדוֹ, בַּעֲדָם) and commonly co-occurs in coordinated series (e.g., בַּעֲדוֹ וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ וּבְעַד כָּל קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל in LEV 16:17; compare LEV 9:7, LEV 16:6, JOB 1:10, 2KI 22:13). With verbs of closing (סָגַר, עָצַר), it marks the barrier or person/object enclosed inside (GEN 7:16, 2KI 4:5, 2KI 4:21, GEN 20:18, 1SA 1:6). In AMO 9:10, בַּעֲדֵינוּ follows הִגִּישׁ וְהִקְדִּים ('bring near and confront/overtake us' with calamity). Combined as מִבַּעַד לְ in SNG 4:1 and SNG 6:7, it indicates viewing through or from behind a veil. In intercessory and cultic contexts, it regularly pairs with הִתְפַּלֵּל ('pray'), נָשָׂא תְפִלָּה ('lift up prayer'), כִּפֶּר ('make atonement'), and דָּרַשׁ ('inquire of God'). With עָוָה/רָעָה or חַטָּאת (EXO 32:30, JER 11:14), it can specify the offense or calamity on account of which action is taken.

core_meaning_summary: To be displeasing, evil, or harmful; to act wickedly or inflict harm (causative); and in a distinct set of poetic contexts, to break, shatter, or come to ruin.

senses.definition: To be displeasing, troubling, or morally offensive to someone, regularly constructed with the prepositional phrase "in the eyes of."
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal stative verb + בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") + person

senses.definition: Of the eye, to become begrudging, stingy, or hostile toward someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal stative verb with עַיִן ("eye") as subject + בְּ + person

senses.definition: Of the face, to look sad, gloomy, or troubled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal stative verb with פָּנִים ("face") as subject

senses.definition: To behave wickedly, commit wrong, or act worse than others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil active verb, used intransitively, with infinitive לַעֲשׂוֹת ("to do"), or with מִן ("more than")

senses.definition: Those who habitually do wrong or practice evil.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil participle used substantivally (plural מְרֵעִים)

senses.definition: To inflict harm, mistreat, or bring disaster and affliction upon someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil causative verb + לְ + person, direct object, or absolute

senses.definition: To smash, shatter, or crush violently, or (intransitively) to be broken and ruined.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb, transitive with direct object and instrument בְּ ("with"), or intransitive

senses.definition: To suffer harm, be broken, or come to ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal passive/intransitive verb

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the idiom רָעַע בְּעֵינֵי X ("to be displeasing/evil in someone's eyes"), often contrasted with טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי X ("good in someone's eyes", JER 40:4). With עַיִן ("eye") + בְּ, it expresses a begrudging or stingy attitude toward a needy relative (DEU 15:9, DEU 28:54). In the Hiphil, it frequently contrasts with הֵיטִיב ("do good", JOS 24:20) and takes מִן for comparison ("act worse than", 1KI 16:25, 2KI 21:11, JER 7:26, JER 16:12). The Hiphil participle מְרֵעִים functions substantivally as a standard term for "evildoers," parallel to רְשָׁעִים ("wicked", PSA 26:5, PRO 24:19) and פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן ("workers of iniquity", ISA 31:2). A distinct physical-destruction usage ("smash, shatter, be broken") appears in PSA 2:9, ISA 8:9, PRO 13:20, and JER 11:16; in ISA 8:9 the Qal imperative רֹעוּ parallels וָחֹתּוּ ("and be dismayed/shattered").

core_meaning_summary: To put on, wear, or clothe someone (literally or figuratively) with garments, armor, attributes, or conditions.

senses.definition: In the simple active stem (Qal), to put on or wear physical garments, priestly vestments, sackcloth, or woven materials on one's body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); takes the garment or fabric as direct object (occasionally omitted when contextually understood, as in JOB 27:17), sometimes with עַל ('upon') specifying the body part

senses.definition: In the simple active stem (Qal), used figuratively or metonymically to take on, be enveloped by, or display a quality, status, or condition such as majesty, strength, righteousness, shame, a curse, royal bearing, or desolation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); takes an abstract noun or metonymic expression as direct object, sometimes accompanied by כְּ ('like') comparing the attribute to armor or a garment

senses.definition: In the causative active stem (Hiphil), to dress or clothe another person, or to place garments, armor, or animal skins onto someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil); typically takes two direct objects (the person dressed and the garment/armor), or a direct object of the garment with עַל ('upon') marking the body part, or the person alone when the garment is implied or from a source (מִן)

senses.definition: In the causative active stem (Hiphil), used figuratively or poetically to array, cover, or endow a creature, person, or the skies with a physical feature, darkness, or impoverished attire.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil); takes two direct objects (the recipient or part affected and the feature, darkness, or rags)

senses.definition: In the intensive passive stem (Pual), to be clothed or attired in a specified material.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive passive participle (Pual); followed directly by the noun naming the fabric worn

collocations_and_notes: Demonstrates a clear contrast across verbal stems: the simple active stem (Qal) denotes the subject putting on or wearing clothing or qualities; the causative active stem (Hiphil) denotes causing someone or something else to wear garments, coverings, or conditions (often taking two direct objects); and the intensive passive participle (Pual) describes the state of being attired in a specified material (2CH 5:12). Frequently contrasts with פָּשַׁט ('strip off', LEV 6:4, LEV 16:23, NUM 20:28) or הֵסִיר ('remove', GEN 38:19, ZEC 3:4). In EST 5:1 ('put on royalty'), the abstract noun מַלְכוּת serves metonymically for royal apparel and bearing.

core_meaning_summary: To turn around or over, overthrow in ruin, or change and transform from one state or condition into another.

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem to denote physically turning something upside down or flipping it over (such as a tent or a baked cake), turning around or wheeling back in movement, or directing one's hand or course.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (transitive or intransitive; also passive participle)

senses.definition: Used in the passive/middle (Niphal) stem for turning oneself back toward a pursuer or rolling over from one side to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (+ אֶל / מִן... אֶל)

senses.definition: Used in the reflexive/iterative (Hithpael) stem as a participle to describe continuous whirling, revolving, or tumbling motion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael participle

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem for overturning, devastating, or completely overthrowing cities, lands, or wicked people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal transitive (or infinitive absolute) + object

senses.definition: Used once in the passive of the causative (Hophal) stem with עַל to express calamities or terrors being turned against and overwhelming someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hophal + עַל (affected person)

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem to express changing or transforming something (or becoming changed) into a different substance, direction, character, or condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal transitive + direct object + לְ (or intransitive + predicate adjective)

senses.definition: Used in the passive/middle (Niphal) stem to express being turned into another substance or state, deteriorating or changing appearance, being transferred to others, or a situation being reversed to its opposite.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (+ לְ / predicate noun or adjective)

senses.definition: Used in the reflexive/middle (Hithpael) stem with a simile to describe the earth changing form or taking on shape like clay beneath a seal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael + כְּ (comparison)

collocations_and_notes: Spanning physical rotation, military/political overthrow, and transformation of state, the verb shows clear stem patterns: Qal expresses either transitive turning/overthrowing/transforming or intransitive turning back or changing color (LEV 13:3); Niphal expresses passive or middle change into another state (typically with לְ, as in EXO 7:15; ISA 34:9; JOL 3:4) as well as bodily turning (JOS 8:20; EZK 4:8) and reversal of circumstances (EST 9:1); Hithpael denotes continuous whirling/rolling motion (GEN 3:24; JDG 7:13) or taking shape (JOB 38:14); Hophal appears once for terrors turned against a sufferer (JOB 30:15). Notable idioms include הָפַךְ יָד ("turn one's hand," i.e., redirect a chariot in 2CH 18:33 or direct repeated blows in LAM 3:3) and turning something into its opposite (curse to blessing in DEU 23:6; justice to wormwood in AMO 5:7; festivals to mourning in AMO 8:10).

core_meaning_summary: Inner gladness and delight, or outward celebration, festivity, and audible rejoicing.

senses.definition: An inner emotional state of gladness, delight, or happy satisfaction, including heartfelt devotion, relief from enemies, or even malicious gloating over another's ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; frequently in adverbial prepositional phrase with בְּ ('with/in'), in construct with לֵב/לֵבָב ('heart') or the experiencer, or as cognate object with שָׂמַח ('rejoice')

senses.definition: Public or communal celebration, festivity, and merrymaking expressed audibly or visibly through singing, shouting, musical instruments, processions, and feasting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; often modified by גְדוֹלָה ('great'), paired with מִשְׁתֶּה ('feasting') or musical terms, or serving as subject/object of verbs of hearing, making, or ceasing

senses.definition: Sensory pleasure or earthly enjoyment derived from food, drink, wine, oil, and the fruits of one's labor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; direct object of verbs such as אָהֵב ('love') or שִׁבַּח ('commend'), or governed by מִן ('from')

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with שָׂשׂוֹן ('gladness/joy', e.g., PSA 51:10, ISA 35:10, ISA 51:3, JER 15:16, JER 25:10) and גִּיל ('exultation', e.g., PSA 43:4, ISA 16:10, JER 48:33), and contrasted with יָגוֹן ('sorrow'), אֲנָחָה ('groaning'), תוּגָה ('grief'), and בְּכִי ('weeping'). Very commonly governed by the preposition בְּ ('with/in joy') to express the manner of worship, procession, service, or departure, or used as a cognate accusative with the verb שָׂמַח ('rejoice with great joy', 1KI 1:40, NEH 12:43, JON 4:6). Construct chains include שִׂמְחַת לֵב/לְבָבוֹ ('joy of heart', ECC 5:19, JER 15:16, EZK 36:5), שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם ('everlasting joy', ISA 35:10, ISA 51:11), and תְּרוּעַת הַשִּׂמְחָה ('shout of celebration', EZR 3:13).

core_meaning_summary: To become intensely angry, indignant, or agitated, and in non-basic stems to fret, be enraged, or act with ardent zeal.

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem with אַף ("anger") as the subject to indicate that wrath or fierce anger kindles and flares up against a person, group, or land.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb + subject אַף (+ בְּ / אֶל / עַל target)

senses.definition: Used impersonally in the basic active (Qal) stem with the preposition לְ marking the experiencer to express becoming angry, deeply vexed, indignant, or distressed over an event or speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal 3ms impersonal + לְ (experiencer) (+ עַל / כִּי cause)

senses.definition: Used in the passive/reflexive (Niphal) stem as a participle with בְּ to describe opponents who are incensed or enraged against someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal participle + בְּ (target)

senses.definition: Used in the reflexive (Hithpael) stem in wisdom exhortations to warn against fretting, working oneself into agitation, or getting heated over the success of wrongdoers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael jussive (+ בְּ target, or + לְ + infinitive)

senses.definition: Used once in the causative/intensive (Hiphil) stem immediately before another verb ("repaired/strengthened"), indicating acting with earnest ardor or zeal in carrying out the paired action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil + finite verb (asyndetic pairing)

collocations_and_notes: Most commonly occurs in the Qal stem either with אַף ("nose/anger") as grammatical subject (e.g., חָרָה אַף יְהוָה בְּ...) or impersonally in the 3ms with לְ marking the experiencer (e.g., וַיִּחַר לְקַיִן). Targets are usually introduced by בְּ, occasionally אֶל (NUM 24:10) or עַל (JOB 19:11); reasons or triggers are introduced by עַל or כִּי. Frequently intensified by מְאֹד (GEN 4:5; NUM 11:10; 1SA 11:6; 1SA 18:8; 2SA 3:8; NEH 4:1), הֵיטֵב (JON 4:4, JON 4:9), or עַד־מָוֶת (JON 4:9), and paired with physical or behavioral expressions of displeasure such as a fallen face (GEN 4:5), breaking tablets (EXO 32:19), striking the palms (NUM 24:10), or judging a matter evil in one's eyes (NUM 11:10; 1SA 18:8). Polite entreaties use the negated jussive אַל־נָא יִחַר לְ / אַל־יִחַר אַפְּךָ בְּ (GEN 18:30; GEN 44:18; JDG 6:39). In NEH 3:20, the single Hiphil form הֶחֱרָה immediately precedes הֶחֱזִיק without a conjunction, functioning adverbially to convey ardent or zealous effort.

core_meaning_summary: To take delight in or favor a person or thing, or to wish, be willing, and purpose to do something.

senses.definition: To feel attraction toward, take delight in, or show favor to a person, whether in marital/romantic desire or in royal or divine favor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; with preposition בְּ + person

senses.definition: To take pleasure in, value, or approve of an action, moral quality, offering, condition, or earthly possession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (including stative/participial forms); with direct object, with בְּ + noun or relative clause, or absolute with locative בָּאָרֶץ

senses.definition: To wish, be willing, purpose, or choose to perform an action or bring about an outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; with לְ + infinitive construct, bare infinitive, relative clause as object of עָשָׂה ('do'), finite verb complement, or absolute

collocations_and_notes: Occurs exclusively in the Qal stem (including stative and participial forms such as הֶחָפֵץ and construct plural חֲפֵצֵי in PSA 35:27, and חָפֵץ in MIC 7:18). Frequently parallels אָהֵב ('love', 1SA 18:22), רָצָה ('be pleased with', PSA 51:18; cf. רָצוֹן 'will/pleasure' in PSA 40:9), בָּחַר ('choose', ISA 65:12; ISA 66:4), and חֵשֶׁק ('desire', 1KI 9:1). In prophetic and wisdom literature, it frequently contrasts divine preference for חֶסֶד ('loyalty/steadfast love'), מִשְׁפָּט ('justice'), and צְדָקָה ('righteousness') over animal sacrifices (1SA/PSA 51:18; ISA 1:11; JER 9:23; HOS 6:6; MIC 7:18). In EST 6:6, 6:9, 6:11, the fixed expression אֲשֶׁר הַמֶּלֶךְ חָפֵץ בִּיקָרוֹ ('whom the king delights to honor') denotes royal favor.

core_meaning_summary: In the active intensive stem (Piel), to render judgment or expect/suppose; in the reflexive/middle stem (Hithpael), to pray, make supplication to God, or intercede on another's behalf.

senses.definition: To arbitrate, pass judgment, or render an assessment in a case involving someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel; transitive with direct object suffix, or with preposition לְ ('for/concerning') + person

senses.definition: To anticipate, suppose, or think something would happen.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel; with infinitive construct phrase as clausal object

senses.definition: To address prayer, petition, confession, or praise to God (or, in one poetic context, to Zion/Israel as the place where God is present), often oriented toward a sacred place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael; absolute, or with אֶל / לִפְנֵי / עַל + addressee, or with directional אֶל / דֶּרֶךְ + sacred place

senses.definition: To intercede or plead with God on behalf of another person or community, especially by a prophet or mediator to avert judgment or obtain favor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael; with בְּעַד, עַל, or לְ + beneficiary (sometimes alongside אֶל + deity)

collocations_and_notes: Clear stem distinction between the active/intensive Piel (judicial assessment or expectation) and the reflexive/middle Hithpael (praying or interceding); 1SA 2:25 displays both stems in direct contrast. In Hithpael, prayers are commonly paired with הִתְחַנֵּן ('implore', 1KI 8:33), חִלָּה אֶת פְּנֵי ('entreat the favor of', 1KI 13:6), הִתְוַדָּה ('confess', DAN 9:20), בָּכָה ('weep', 1SA 1:10; NEH 1:4), and צוּם ('fast', NEH 1:4), as well as the nouns תְּפִלָּה ('prayer', 1KI 8:29; 2CH 6:19; JER 7:16) and תְּחִנָּה ('supplication', 2CH 6:19; 2CH 33:13; DAN 9:20). Divine response is frequently expressed with שָׁמַע ('hear', 1KI 8:29; 2CH 6:21; 2CH 7:14; JER 29:12) or נֶעְתַּר ('be entreated', 2CH 33:13). Note the unusual preposition עַל rather than אֶל with the divine addressee in 1SA 1:10, and directional orientation toward the temple or land with דֶּרֶךְ ('toward', 1KI 8:48; 2CH 6:38) or אֶל הַבַּיִת/הַמָּקוֹם ('toward this house/place', 1KI 8:29, 42; 2CH 6:21, 32).

core_meaning_summary: To be swift, light, or of little weight/esteem, with causative stems denoting lightening a burden or treating lightly, intensive/passive stems denoting cursing, and a reduplicated form meaning to shake swiftly.

senses.definition: To move with great speed or pass rapidly, often compared using מִן ("than") to eagles or a weaver's shuttle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive, often with comparative מִן)

senses.definition: Of floodwaters: to diminish in level, subside, or abate from the surface of the earth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with מֵעַל ("from upon")

senses.definition: To become lowered in esteem, diminished in status, or despised in someone's estimation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of")

senses.definition: To be a small, easy, or trivial matter; in the adverbial phrase עַל נְקַלָּה (JER 6:14), to act lightly, carelessly, or superficially.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (stative/impersonal with בְּעֵינֵי or מִן + infinitive; feminine participle in prepositional phrase עַל נְקַלָּה)

senses.definition: To reduce the weight or severity of a physical load, cargo, judicial burden, or oppressive labor imposed on someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative, typically with מִן or מֵעַל indicating the person or burden relieved)

senses.definition: To treat someone with disrespect or contempt, or to humble and bring those of high status into dishonor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (transitive with direct object)

senses.definition: To pronounce a curse upon, revile, blaspheme, or speak contemptuously/harmfully against someone or something (including God, parents, rulers, the ground, or neighbors).
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (transitive with direct object, occasionally used absolutely or with בְּ / לְ)

senses.definition: To be placed under a curse or spoken of as accursed (contrasted with those blessed).
senses.grammatical_frame: Pual (passive counterpart of Piel; finite verb or substantive participle)

senses.definition: To shake or rattle swiftly (used of shaking arrows during a divination ritual).
senses.grammatical_frame: Reduplicated stem (Pilpel) with בְּ + instrument ("arrows")

collocations_and_notes: Contrasts with כָּבֵד ("heavy") and הִקְשָׁה ("make harsh") in contexts of burdens and forced labor (1KI 12:4, 1KI 12:10; 2CH 10:4, 2CH 10:10), and with נִכְבַּדֵּי ("honored ones") in ISA 23:9. In Piel and Pual, it stands in direct opposition to ברך ("bless"; PSA 37:22; PSA 109:28; PRO 30:11) and parallels ארר ("curse"; EXO 22:27). Note the wide stem differentiation: Qal expresses swiftness, subsiding, or low esteem; Niphal expresses ease/triviality; Hiphil expresses lightening a burden or treating lightly; Piel/Pual express verbal cursing; and the reduplicated stem in EZK 21:26 denotes rapid shaking of divination arrows.

core_meaning_summary: A fleeting breath or vapor; by extension, futility, emptiness, or a worthless idol; also the personal name Abel.

senses.definition: A passing breath, puff of air, or vapor; figuratively, the brief and fragile transience of human life and days.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun as subject, predicate, construct modifier (יְמֵי חַיֵּי הֶבְלֶךָ), or object of preposition (בְּ, לְ), sometimes modified by נִדָּף ("driven away").

senses.definition: That which is empty, pointless, or devoid of lasting profit or reliability, applied to futile toil, empty speech, deceptive hope, or paradoxical outcomes.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, predominantly as predicate nominative (זֶה הֶבֶל, הַכֹּל הָבֶל), in superlative construct (הֲבֵל הֲבָלִים), or adverbially (הָבֶל / בַּהֶבֶל).

senses.definition: A worthless idol or false deity considered powerless and unreal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, chiefly plural in construct or with pronominal suffixes (הַבְלֵיהֶם, הַבְלֵי נֵכָר, הַבְלֵי הַגּוֹיִם, הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא), occasionally singular predicate (הֶבֶל הֵמָּה).

senses.definition: Abel, the second son of Adam and Eve, a shepherd killed by his brother Cain.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper masculine noun, appearing as clause subject, direct object (אֶת הֶבֶל), or object of preposition (אֶל הֶבֶל).

collocations_and_notes: In Ecclesiastes, הֶבֶל recurs in the superlative construct הֲבֵל הֲבָלִים and the refrain הַכֹּל הָבֶל / גַּם זֶה הֶבֶל, frequently paired with רַעְיוֹן רוּחַ ("striving after wind", ECC 4:16). In poetic contexts it parallels רוּחַ ("wind", ISA 57:13), צֵל עוֹבֵר ("passing shadow", PSA 144:4), and רִיק ("emptiness", ISA 30:7). When referring to false gods, it occurs mostly in the plural construct (הַבְלֵי נֵכָר, הַבְלֵי הַגּוֹיִם, הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא) alongside פְסִלִים ("carved images") or לֹא אֵל ("no-god"). In GEN 4:2–9 the identical form serves as the personal name Abel.

core_meaning_summary: To lose moisture, dry up, or wither (of water, vegetation, and bodily or inner vitality), with causative forms meaning to dry something up and certain Hiphil forms in this corpus meaning to be ashamed or put to shame.

senses.definition: Of water, rivers, streams, or floodwaters: to dry up, subside, or lose water completely.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with water, stream, or river as subject

senses.definition: Of plants, grass, roots, pastures, or body parts: to wither, shrivel, or lose moisture and vitality; used figuratively of inner strength, a failing limb, or communal hope.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with vegetation, limbs, bones, or heart as subject; sometimes reinforced by an infinitive absolute

senses.definition: Devoid of moisture; dried, stale, or withered, in contrast to what is fresh, moist, or green.
senses.grammatical_frame: Stative/adjectival use modifying nouns or functioning as predicate adjective

senses.definition: To cause seas, rivers, springs, pools, or living vegetation to dry up or wither.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative, taking a direct object) and Piel (causative with pronominal object suffix in NAM 1:4)

senses.definition: To become withered or fail/vanish away (used intransitively of a vine and of human joy).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (intransitive/inchoative)

senses.definition: To feel shame, be disgraced or confounded (as in defeat or idolatry), or to put someone to shame (with "face" as object in 2SA 19:6).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (intransitive, or transitive with direct object in 2SA 19:6)

collocations_and_notes: Often contrasted with לַח ("moist, fresh") in descriptions of produce and trees (NUM 6:3; EZK 17:24), and paired with חָרַב ("be parched/laid waste"; JOB 14:11; ISA 42:15; ISA 44:27; JER 50:38; JER 51:36; NAM 1:4) and נָבֵל ("fade"; ISA 40:8). Infinitive absolute + finite verb occurs for emphasis in EZK 17:10 and ZEC 11:17. Notably, this lemma's corpus grouping also includes Hiphil forms (הֹבִישׁ, הֹבַשְׁתָּ) meaning "to put to shame" or "be ashamed/confounded" (2SA 19:6; JER 6:15; JER 10:14; JER 48:1; JER 50:2; ZEC 10:5), where it pairs with בּוֹשׁ (JER 6:15) and חתת ("be shattered/dismayed"; JER 48:1; JER 50:2). In JOL 1:12, הֹבִישׁ appears twice intransitively: first of a withered vine, and second of joy failing or drying up from humanity.

core_meaning_summary: A monumental sacred temple (either as a whole complex or its main central hall) or a grand royal palace.

senses.definition: A sacred building dedicated to God as a place of worship, sacrifice, and divine presence, including both earthly sanctuaries and God's heavenly dwelling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, commonly in construct (הֵיכַל יְהוָה, הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ) or with pronominal suffixes (הֵיכָלוֹ), often governed by spatial prepositions (בְּ, אֶל, מִן, לִפְנֵי).

senses.definition: The main central chamber or nave of the temple building, distinguished from the inner sanctuary (Most Holy Place).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with definite article (הַהֵיכָל), paired or contrasted with דְּבִיר or קֹדֶשׁ, or serving as an architectural reference point (לְפֶתַח הַהֵיכָל, עַל פְּנֵי הַהֵיכָל).

senses.definition: A grand royal residence or imposing public building of a king or city.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular or plural (הֵיכָלוֹת) noun, in construct with מֶלֶךְ ("king") or in royal and urban contexts.

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the construct phrase הֵיכַל יְהוָה ("temple of YHWH") and הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ ("your holy temple"). In architectural descriptions of the Jerusalem temple (1KI 6:5, 7:50; EZK 41:4, 41:23), הֵיכָל designates the central main hall inside הַבַּיִת ("the house"), distinct from the inner sanctuary (דְּבִיר / קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים). In poetic and prophetic texts (2SA 22:7, PSA 18:7, PSA 29:9, ISA 6:1, JON 2:8), God's הֵיכָל is the royal-sacred seat from which he hears prayers and exercises rule. In HOS 8:14 (plural הֵיכָלוֹת, parallel to fortified cities and אַרְמְנוֹת "citadels") and AMO 8:3 (שִׁירֹות הֵיכָל), the context admits either royal palaces or sanctuaries.

core_meaning_summary: Deliverance, rescue, or victory from danger and enemies—typically accomplished by God—as well as the resulting state of safety and well-being, or God himself as deliverer.

senses.definition: An act or event of rescue, liberation, or military victory from enemies, peril, or distress, regularly attributed to God (and occasionally performed through a human agent acting with God).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular and plural (יְשׁוּעוֹת 'acts of deliverance/victories'); occurs as object of verbs of performing (עשׂה, פעל), seeing (ראה), or declaring (הודיע), and in construct phrases with the agent or recipient (e.g., 'the deliverance of YHWH', 'day of deliverance').

senses.definition: A condition of safety, stability, vindication, or personal welfare, contrasted with calamity, violence, and ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular and plural; appears parallel to nouns for dignity/nobility (נְדִבָה), justice (מִשְׁפָּט), and wisdom/knowledge, or as a symbolic name predicated of city fortifications (חֹמֹתַיִךְ 'your walls').

senses.definition: Metonymic designation or predicate applied directly to God as the protector, refuge, and source of rescue for his people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun with pronominal suffix or in construct after divine titles (אֵל יְשׁוּעָתִי, צוּר יְשֻׁעָתוֹ), as a direct nominal predicate ('I am your deliverance', 'he is my rock and my deliverance'), or in the idiom היה לְ... לִישׁוּעָה ('become deliverance for').

collocations_and_notes: Often governed by verbs of action or perception such as עשׂה ('work/accomplish', EXO 14:13, 1SA 14:45, ISA 26:18), פעל ('do/work', PSA 74:12), ראה ('see', EXO 14:13, 2CH 20:17, PSA 91:16, ISA 52:10), הודיע ('make known', PSA 98:2), and קוה ('wait/hope for', GEN 49:18, ISA 59:11). The plural יְשׁוּעוֹת frequently denotes repeated acts of rescue or triumphant victories (2SA 22:51, PSA 18:51, PSA 42:6, PSA 43:5, PSA 53:7, PSA 74:12, ISA 26:18, ISA 33:6). A poetic form with a final -āh suffix (יְשׁוּעָתָה) appears in PSA 80:3 and JON 2:10. Repeatedly paired with צְדָקָה ('righteousness', PSA 98:2, ISA 51:8), חֶסֶד ('steadfast love', 2SA 22:51, PSA 13:6, PSA 18:51), and עֹז ('strength', PSA 21:2, PSA 118:14, ISA 12:2).

core_meaning_summary: An object cast or drawn to make an impartial decision or selection, and by extension the procedural method of casting lots, the territorial share assigned thereby, or one's appointed destiny.

senses.definition: A marker or object cast or drawn—and by extension the procedure of casting lots itself—used to arrive at an impartial decision, settle disputes, or assign roles, turns, or divisions.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun (singular or plural), object of verbs of casting/placing, subject of verbs of emerging/falling, or adverbial בְּגוֹרָל

senses.definition: A territorial inheritance, share, or allotted portion of land, cities, or property assigned to a tribe, clan, or group.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun, often with pronominal suffix, in construct chains (e.g., עָרֵי גוֹרָלָם, גְּבוּל גּוֹרָלָם), or with הָיָה לְ

senses.definition: One's appointed fate, outcome, or allotted recompense determined by divine decree.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun with pronominal suffix

collocations_and_notes: Common verbal idioms for casting or drawing lots include: הִפִּיל גּוֹרָל / גּוֹרָלוֹת ('cause a lot/lots to fall', 1CH 25:8; 26:13, 14; NEH 11:1; EST 9:24; PSA 22:19; PRO 1:14; ISA 34:17; JON 1:7); נָתַן גּוֹרָלוֹת עַל ('place lots upon', LEV 16:8); הִשְׁלִיךְ גּוֹרָל ('throw a lot', JOS 18:8); יָדָה גוֹרָל ('cast a lot', OBA 1:11). The result of the lot is expressed with נָפַל ('fall [upon]', 1CH 26:14; JON 1:7), יָצָא ('go out [to/for]', NUM 33:54; JOS 19:1, 17, 24, 40; 21:4; 1CH 24:7; 26:14), or עָלָה ('come up [upon/for]', LEV 16:9; JOS 18:11). In EST 9:24, גּוֹרָל explicitly translates the foreign term פּוּר. In JER 13:25 it stands in direct parallelism with מְנָת מִדַּיִךְ ('your measured portion').

core_meaning_summary: A verbal or silent petition, intercession, or devotional address directed to God, as well as a composed liturgical text or psalm.

senses.definition: An earnest spoken or inner address directed to God—whether personal appeal, confession, thanksgiving, or intercession on behalf of others—seeking God's attention, mercy, or intervention.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun; serves as object of verbs of hearing or attending (שׁמע, האזין, פנה אל) or lifting up (נשׂא + בְּעַד 'on behalf of'); occurs as cognate object of התפלל in the reflexive stem ('to pray'); used in construct before place/person nouns (e.g., 'house of prayer', 'prayer of your servant').

senses.definition: A formal devotional poem, psalm, or liturgical song/address directed to God, including recorded prayers and collections of such compositions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular (in psalm superscriptions with לְ 'of/for', in liturgical leadership notices with לְ, or parallel to שִׁיר 'song') and plural (תְּפִלּוֹת) for a collected body of compositions.

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in hendiadys or poetic parallelism with terms for urgent appeal or outcry, including תְּחִנָּה / תַּחֲנוּנִים ('supplication/plea for favor', 1KI 8:28, 1KI 8:45, PSA 55:2, PSA 86:6, PSA 143:1, DAN 9:17), רִנָּה ('ringing cry', 1KI 8:28, PSA 17:1, JER 11:14), and שַׁוְעָה ('cry for help', PSA 102:2). Common verbal collocations are שׁמע ('hear/listen to'), האזין ('give ear to'), פנה אל ('turn toward'), and נשׂא תְפִלָּה בְּעַד ('lift up a prayer on behalf of', 2KI 19:4, JER 11:14). Appears as the cognate object of the verb התפלל in the reflexive/iterative stem (meaning 'to pray', 2SA 7:27, 1KI 8:28-29, 1KI 8:54, NEH 1:6). Associated physical actions include kneeling, spreading hands toward heaven (1KI 8:54, ISA 1:15), fasting in sackcloth (PSA 35:13), and weeping (ISA 38:5). In PSA 109:7, the speaker wishes that an adversary's תְּפִלָּה in the context of judgment might turn into offense/sin (לַחֲטָאָה). Construct expressions such as בֵּית תְּפִלָּה ('house of prayer', ISA 56:7) and תְּפִלַּת הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה ('the prayer of this place', 2CH 6:40, 2CH 7:15) designate the temple as the locus of prayer.

core_meaning_summary: The belly, abdomen, or womb—denoting both the physical midsection/stomach and the reproductive organ of gestation—and figuratively the innermost being as the seat of thoughts, breath, and moral intention.

senses.definition: The physical belly, abdomen, or stomach cavity of the human body, either externally as the front midsection of the torso or internally as the cavity that receives food and drink.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, commonly with pronominal suffix or preposition בְּ/מִן

senses.definition: The womb as the organ of pregnancy and gestation; also used in temporal expressions with מִן ('from the womb' = from birth) and in the construct phrase פְּרִי בֶטֶן ('fruit of the womb' = offspring, children), as well as metaphorically of natural origin.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, often in construct (with אֵם or following פְּרִי) or with preposition מִן/בְּ

senses.definition: The inner self or innermost parts of a person, conceived as the hidden interior where thoughts, words, breath/spirit, and intentions are stored or formed.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, commonly in construct חַדְרֵי בָטֶן or with pronominal suffix

collocations_and_notes: Common collocations include: פְּרִי בֶטֶן / פְּרִי הַבָּטֶן ('fruit of the womb', i.e., offspring, DEU 7:13; 28:11, 18; 30:9; PSA 127:3; MIC 6:7); מִבֶּטֶן אִמִּי / אִמּוֹ ('from my/his mother's womb', meaning from birth, JDG 16:17; JOB 1:21; 31:18; PSA 22:11; ECC 5:14) and shorter מִבֶּטֶן / מִן הַבָּטֶן ('from the womb / since birth', JDG 13:5; JOB 10:19; PSA 58:4; ISA 44:2; 46:3; 49:1, 5); דַּלְתֵי בִטְנִי ('the doors of my womb', JOB 3:10); חַדְרֵי בָטֶן ('the chambers of the inner being/belly', PRO 18:8; 20:27; 26:22); ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִי ('the spirit/breath within me', JOB 32:18). Often paired or in parallelism with רֶחֶם ('womb', PSA 22:11; 58:4; ISA 46:3; JER 1:5) and מֵעַיִם ('inward parts/womb', GEN 25:23; NUM 5:22; ISA 49:1). Note that in DEU 7:13 and 28:11, 18; 30:9, 'your בֶּטֶן' refers generally to human reproductive capacity/offspring alongside livestock and crops.

core_meaning_summary: To cry out aloud in distress, lamentation, alarm, or urgent supplication for help, and in causative and passive/reflexive forms to summon or be rallied together.

senses.definition: To cry out urgently to God, a ruler, or allies for rescue, mercy, or intervention in a time of threat, oppression, or need.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), usually with אֶל ("to"), לְ ("to"), directional accusative הַשָּׁמָיִם ("toward heaven"), or direct person object (JDG 12:2, NEH 9:28); also causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively in poetry (JOB 35:9).

senses.definition: To utter a loud cry of grief, physical pain, terror, or mourning, often in the context of disaster, bereavement, or childbirth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), intransitive, with cognate object זְעָקָה ("outcry"), or with עַל / לְ ("over/for") indicating the cause or object of lament.

senses.definition: To raise a vocal outcry in alarm, protest, or urgent proclamation of wrong or danger.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), absolute or introducing direct speech.

senses.definition: To call people, citizens, or armed forces together; to muster or summon for military action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object marker אֶת denoting troops or fighting men.

senses.definition: To be called together, mobilized, or rallied in response to a summons or alarm to pursue or confront an enemy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), intransitive, often with purpose infinitive or directional phrase אַחֲרָיו ("after him").

collocations_and_notes: Demonstrates clear stem distinctions in context: the basic active stem (Qal) denotes raising one's voice in outcry, lament, or urgent supplication; the causative stem (Hiphil) ordinarily takes a direct object of troops or citizens to mean summoning or mustering (JDG 4:13, 2SA 20:4), though in poetic parallelism with שִׁוַּע ("cry for help") it functions intransitively for crying out under oppression (JOB 35:9); the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) denotes being summoned or rallying together in response to a call (JOS 8:16, JDG 6:35, JDG 18:23). In Qal, frequently followed by אֶל ("to"), especially אֶל יְהוָה, or by לֵאמֹר introducing the plea; also takes a cognate accusative זְעָקָה גְדֹלָה וּמָרָה ("a great and bitter outcry," EST 4:1) and pairs with הֵילִיל ("wail," ISA 14:31, JER 47:2, JER 48:31, EZK 21:17).

core_meaning_summary: Hardship, affliction, or calamity that besets a person or community, as well as the acute inner anguish and distress it produces.

senses.definition: An external situation of severe hardship, danger, oppression, or calamity from which a person or nation needs rescue, protection, or endurance; often plural when referring to repeated or varied adversities.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular and plural); frequently in construct after יוֹם ("day") or עֵת ("time"), as object of prepositions בְּ ("in") or מִן ("from, out of"), or as subject of verbs of coming, approaching, or rising.

senses.definition: Acute emotional or physical anguish, torment, or panic experienced internally, often depicted as seizing a person like labor pains or paired with terms for sorrow, darkness, and constraint.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular); used in construct with נֶפֶשׁ ("soul/life"), paired with nouns of grief or constraint, or as subject of verbs of seizing (הֶחֱזִיק, אָחַז).

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in fixed temporal construct phrases: בְּיוֹם צָרָה / צָרָתִי ("in the day of [my] distress," GEN 35:3, PSA 77:3, PSA 86:7, PRO 25:19, JER 16:19, OBA 1:12) and בְּעֵת צָרָה / צָרָתָם ("in the time of [their] distress," JDG 10:14, NEH 9:27, ISA 33:2, JER 14:8, DAN 12:1). Commonly governed by מִן / מִכֹּל ("from [every] distress") with verbs of rescue, salvation, or redemption such as הִצִּיל, הוֹשִׁיעַ, פָּדָה, and הוֹצִיא (1SA 10:19, 1SA 26:24, 1KI 1:29, PSA 25:22, PSA 34:7, PSA 34:18, PSA 54:9, PSA 143:11). Frequently paired with רָעוֹת ("evils/calamities," DEU 31:17, 1SA 10:19), צוּקָה / מְצוּקָה ("anguish/constraint," PRO 1:27, ISA 8:22, ZEP 1:15), יָגוֹן ("sorrow," PSA 116:3), and חִיל / חֲבָלִים ("birth pangs/writhing," JER 6:24, JER 49:24). In NEH 9:27 it stands alongside the verb וַיָּצֵרוּ ("they oppressed/harassed them").

core_meaning_summary: To direct one's eyes or attention toward a person, object, direction, or situation, whether in physical looking, attentive consideration, or caring/judicial regard.

senses.definition: To direct one's visual gaze toward a person, object, or direction; to look or stare.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active stem), absolute or with directional adverb, אֶל, לְ, עַל, בְּ, or direct object; Niphal (once, ISA 5:30) with לְ in the same active sense; occasionally with 'eye' as subject

senses.definition: To turn one's mind or attention to something so as to examine, observe, or contemplate it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active stem), absolute, with direct object, or with אֶל + noun

senses.definition: To look upon someone or a situation with notice, concern, favor, or moral/judicial assessment (most often predicated of God in prayer or complaint).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active stem), imperative or imperfect, absolute or with direct object, אֶל, or לְ

collocations_and_notes: Occurs overwhelmingly in the Hiphil stem, with one Niphal occurrence (ISA 5:30) showing the same active sense ('look') rather than a passive meaning. Frequently paired in parallelism or sequence with רָאָה ('see') and occasionally with חָזָה ('behold') or שָׁמַע ('hear'). Common prepositional complements include אֶל ('toward, at'), לְ ('to, toward'), עַל ('upon'), and בְּ ('on, from'), as well as directional ה- (הַשָּׁמַיְמָה) and אַחֲרֶיךָ ('behind you'). In poetic and wisdom texts, עַיִן ('eye') can serve as the grammatical subject (PSA 92:12; PRO 4:25). In laments and prayers, imperative forms (הַבֵּט / הַבִּיטָה) regularly appeal to God to take notice of suffering or covenant faithfulness.

core_meaning_summary: The eastern compass direction or side, and the dry or forceful wind blowing from the east.

senses.definition: The eastern compass point, direction, side, or border.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (often with directional suffix -āh), used adverbially, as object of prepositions (לְ, מִן), or as genitive in construct phrases (דֶּרֶךְ הַקָּדִים, פְּאַת קָדִים, גְּבוּל קָדִימָה, רוּחַ הַקָּדִים)

senses.definition: A strong, dry, or scorching wind blowing from the east; also used figuratively for empty or futile things.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, either standing alone substantively as subject/object/genitive or as genitive following רוּחַ ('wind')

collocations_and_notes: In directional and boundary descriptions (especially EZK 40–48), frequently takes the directional suffix -āh (קָדִימָה, occasionally spelled קָדִמָה) and appears in fixed phrases such as דֶּרֶךְ הַקָּדִים(ָה) ('facing/toward the east'), הַפֹּנֶה קָדִים/קָדִימָה ('facing east'), פְּאַת קָדִים/קָדִימָה ('the east side'), and גְּבוּל קָדִימָה ('east border'). Notably, the construct phrase רוּחַ (הַ)קָּדִים exhibits two distinct uses: 'east wind' in meteorological and narrative contexts (EXO 10:13; EXO 14:21; JER 18:17; EZK 19:12; JON 4:8), vs. 'east side/quarter' in architectural measurement (EZK 42:16). In wisdom and prophetic poetry (JOB 15:2; HOS 12:2), 'east wind' is paired with רוּחַ ('wind') as a figure for empty or futile pursuits.

verses.EZK 40:32: וַ יְבִיאֵ֛ נִי אֶל הֶ חָצֵ֥ר הַ פְּנִימִ֖י דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַ 【קָּדִ֑ים】 וַ יָּ֣מָד אֶת הַ שַּׁ֔עַר כַּ מִּדּ֖וֹת הָ אֵֽלֶּה

verses.EZK 47:1: וַ יְשִׁבֵ נִי֮ אֶל פֶּ֣תַח הַ בַּיִת֒ וְ הִנֵּה מַ֣יִם יֹצְאִ֗ים מִ תַּ֨חַת מִפְתַּ֤ן הַ בַּ֨יִת֙ 【קָדִ֔ימָ】 ה כִּֽי פְנֵ֥י הַ בַּ֖יִת 【קָדִ֑ים】 וְ הַ מַּ֣יִם יֹרְדִ֗ים מִ תַּ֜חַת מִ כֶּ֤תֶף הַ בַּ֨יִת֙ הַ יְמָנִ֔ית מִ נֶּ֖גֶב לַ מִּזְבֵּֽחַ

verses.EZK 47:18: וּ פְאַ֣ת 【קָדִ֡ים】 מִ בֵּ֣ין חַוְרָ֣ן וּ מִ בֵּין דַּמֶּשֶׂק֩ וּ מִ בֵּ֨ין הַ גִּלְעָ֜ד וּ מִ בֵּ֨ין אֶ֤רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַ יַּרְדֵּ֔ן מִ גְּב֛וּל עַל הַ יָּ֥ם הַ קַּדְמוֹנִ֖י תָּמֹ֑דּוּ וְ אֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת 【קָדִֽימָ】 ה
verses.EZK 48:2: וְ עַ֣ל גְּב֣וּל דָּ֗ן מִ פְּאַ֥ת 【קָדִ֛ים】 עַד פְּאַת יָ֖מָּ ה אָשֵׁ֥ר אֶחָֽד

verses.EZK 48:8: וְ עַל֙ גְּב֣וּל יְהוּדָ֔ה מִ פְּאַ֥ת 【קָדִ֖ים】 עַד פְּאַת יָ֑מָּ ה תִּהְיֶ֣ה הַ תְּרוּמָ֣ה אֲֽשֶׁר תָּרִ֡ימוּ חֲמִשָּׁה֩ וְ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף רֹ֗חַב וְ אֹ֜רֶךְ כְּ אַחַ֤ד הַ חֲלָקִים֙ מִ פְּאַ֤ת 【קָדִ֨ימָ】 ה֙ עַד פְּאַת יָ֔מָּ ה וְ הָיָ֥ה הַ מִּקְדָּ֖שׁ בְּ תוֹכֽ וֹ
verses.EZK 48:16: וְ אֵלֶּה֮ מִדּוֹתֶי הָ֒ פְּאַ֣ת צָפ֗וֹן חֲמֵ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ וְ אַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּ פְאַת נֶ֕גֶב חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וְ אַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֑ים וּ מִ פְּאַ֣ת 【קָדִ֗ים】 חֲמֵ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ וְ אַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּ פְאַת יָ֕מָּ ה חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וְ אַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִֽים

core_meaning_summary: To flee or hurry away from danger, pursuit, or a location (Qal), or to put to flight and cause to pass across from end to end (Hiphil).

senses.definition: To run away, escape, or take flight from danger, pursuit, mistreatment, or authority, often secretly or toward a place of refuge.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; intransitive, frequently followed by מִפְּנֵי / מִלִּפְנֵי / מִן (source of threat) and/or אֶל, אַחֲרֵי, or locative expression (destination)

senses.definition: To hurry away, depart swiftly, or leave a post or place quickly, whether in response to urgent dismissal, abandonment of an unsupported duty, or swift movement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; imperative (often with ethical dative לְךָ + אֶל) or finite verb + לְ

senses.definition: Figuratively of time or mortal life: to pass away rapidly, slip away, or vanish without remaining.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; intransitive with non-human or abstract subject (e.g., days, mortal human compared to a shadow)

senses.definition: Causative of the Qal: to drive away, scatter, or put enemies or an adversary to flight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil; transitive with direct object (אֶת or pronominal suffix)

senses.definition: Of a structural crossbar: to run through, pass across, or extend continuously from one end to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil participle; with מִן ... אֶל marking span

collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with מִפְּנֵי ('from before / from the presence of'), מִלִּפְנֵי (JON 1:10), or מִן (2SA 19:10, JOB 27:22) to mark the threat or authority escaped from, and with אֶל, אַחֲרֵי (1SA 22:20), לְ (NEH 13:10), or directive -āh (2SA 4:3) to mark destination. Often occurs in narrative chains alongside נוּס ('flee', JDG 9:21), מָלַט Niphal ('escape', 1SA 19:12, 1SA 19:18), הָלַךְ, and יָצָא (JER 52:7). Appears with an infinitive absolute for emphasis (בָּרוֹחַ יִבְרָח, JOB 27:22) and with the reflexive ethical dative לְךָ in urgent commands to leave (בְּרַח לְךָ, NUM 24:11, AMO 7:12). Clear stem contrast between the basic intransitive Qal ('flee, hurry away, vanish') and the causative/transitive Hiphil ('put to flight, drive away' in 1CH 12:16, JOB 41:20, or 'run/extend across from end to end' of a crossbar in EXO 26:28).

core_meaning_summary: The subterranean realm of the dead beneath the earth, also personified as the insatiable, threatening power of death and the grave.

senses.definition: The subterranean realm or abode of the dead beneath the earth, conceived as a dark, deep, gated, and silent place of no return to which mortals descend at death and where remembrance and praise of God cease.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine); used as locative or goal with directive -āh, prepositions (בְּ, לְ, עַד, מִן), or in construct phrases denoting parts/depths (e.g., שַׁעֲרֵי שְׁאוֹל, פִּי שְׁאוֹל)

senses.definition: Death and the grave personified as an insatiable, devouring, or entangling adversary, or metonymically for mortal peril and the brink of death from which one seeks deliverance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine); subject of active verbs, partner in covenant/address, or nomen rectum in idioms of peril and power (e.g., חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל, יַד שְׁאוֹל, בֶּטֶן שְׁאוֹל)

collocations_and_notes: Grammatically feminine in agreement (e.g., רָגְזָה in ISA 14:9; לֹא תִשְׂבַּעְנָה with אֲבַדּוֹ in PRO 27:20). Regularly occurs with verbs of downward motion such as יָרַד ('go down') and הוֹרִיד ('bring down'), frequently marked with directive -āh (שְׁאֹלָה) or prepositions בְּ, לְ, עַד, and מִן. Commonly paired in poetic parallelism with מָוֶת ('death'), בּוֹר ('pit'), שַׁחַת ('pit/corruption'), אֲבַדּוֹן ('destruction/Abaddon'), אֶרֶץ תַּחְתִּית ('nether earth'), and רְפָאִים ('shades of the dead'). Notable construct and figurative phrases include שְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית / תַּחְתִּיָּה ('lowest Sheol'), שַׁעֲרֵי שְׁאוֹל ('gates of Sheol'), פִּי שְׁאוֹל ('mouth of Sheol'), בֶּטֶן שְׁאוֹל ('belly of Sheol'), חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל ('cords of Sheol'), מְצָרֵי שְׁאוֹל ('distresses of Sheol'), and יַד שְׁאוֹל ('hand/power of Sheol').

core_meaning_summary: A feminine noun (here in construct and suffixed forms) denoting work, labor, skilled craftsmanship, official or cultic service, a crafted item, or entrusted property.

senses.definition: Work, labor, or daily occupation, whether God's creative activity or human agricultural, household, and routine toil; frequently in the legal prohibition כָּל מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה ('any laborious/occupational work') on sacred days.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct or with pronominal suffix, commonly object of עָשָׂה or with מִן after שָׁבַת

senses.definition: Skilled craftsmanship, artisan trade, or organized construction work, especially in fabricating sanctuary furnishings or building temples, fortifications, and royal structures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun before material, artisan role, or structure (e.g., מְלֶאכֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, מְלֶאכֶת הַחוֹמָה) or with suffix

senses.definition: A manufactured article or finished piece of workmanship made from a given material.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun before material noun (מְלֶאכֶת עוֹר)

senses.definition: Official duty, administrative business, cultic temple service of priests and Levites, or a divinely mandated commission.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun before institutional/personal authority (e.g., מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית יְהוָה, מְלֶאכֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ, מְלֶאכֶת יְהוָה) or with suffix

senses.definition: Material goods, belongings, or property entrusted to or owned by another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun with בְּ after שָׁלַח יָדוֹ ('put his hand to') before possessor noun (בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ)

collocations_and_notes: In this lemma sample (the construct/suffixed form מְלֶאכֶת / מְלַאכְתּ-), the noun frequently occurs as the object of עָשָׂה ('to do/perform work'), כָּלָה ('to finish', GEN 2:2), שָׁבַת ('to cease/rest from', GEN 2:2–3; Hiphil in 2CH 16:5), and נָצַח ('to oversee/supervise', 1CH 23:4, EZR 3:8). Fixed expressions include כָּל מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה ('any laborious/occupational work') in festival Sabbath prohibitions (LEV 23, NUM 28–29), מְלֶאכֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ / מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית יְהוָה ('the work/service of the sanctuary/house of the LORD'), and מְלֶאכֶת עוֹר ('leatherwork/article of leather', LEV 13:48). Note that in EXO 35:35, 1KI 7:14, and NEH 5:16 the absolute form מְלָאכָה also co-occurs in the immediate context.

core_meaning_summary: A masculine noun denoting either the eastern direction and eastern regions/peoples in space, or antiquity, ancient times, and temporal priority in time.

senses.definition: The eastern cardinal direction, eastern side, or eastern territory; with מִן (מִקֶּדֶם) it indicates location on the east, movement from or toward the east, or with לְ- relative position east of a landmark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, commonly with מִן (מִקֶּדֶם, often + לְ-) or in construct (אֶרֶץ קֶדֶם, הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם)

senses.definition: In the construct phrase בְּנֵי קֶדֶם ('sons/people of the east'), the inhabitants or nomadic tribes of the eastern territories relative to Israel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct phrase בְּנֵי קֶדֶם

senses.definition: Ancient times, primeval antiquity, or the distant past; used in construct expressions for former eras or enduring realities, with prepositions (מִקֶּדֶם, מִנִּי קֶדֶם, כְּקֶדֶם), or adverbially to mean long ago.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct (e.g., יְמֵי קֶדֶם, אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם), with מִן or כְּ, or adverbial

senses.definition: Prior to or before in time, marking what precedes a set of events or works.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun functioning as a temporal preposition before a noun phrase (קֶדֶם מִפְעָלָיו)

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with the preposition מִן (מִקֶּדֶם, poetic מִנִּי קֶדֶם) in both spatial and temporal senses, and with כְּ (כְּקֶדֶם). Spatial collocations include מִקֶּדֶם לְ- ('east of [a place]'), contrast with מִיָּם ('on the west', GEN 12:8) or מֵאָחוֹר ('from behind/the west', ISA 9:11), אֶרֶץ קֶדֶם ('land of the east', GEN 25:6, alongside directional קֵדְמָה), הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם ('mountains of the east', NUM 23:7), and the recurring group name בְּנֵי קֶדֶם ('peoples of the east', JDG 6:33, JDG 7:12, 1KI 5:10, JOB 1:3, EZK 25:4). Temporal collocations include construct chains such as יְמֵי קֶדֶם ('days of old'), יַרְחֵי קֶדֶם ('months of old', JOB 29:2), מַלְכֵי קֶדֶם ('ancient kings', ISA 19:11), אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם ('God of ancient times', DEU 33:27), and שְׁמֵי קֶדֶם ('ancient heavens', PSA 68:34), often paired in parallelism with עוֹלָם ('everlasting/ages past'), מֵאָז ('from long ago'), and רֵאשִׁית ('beginning').

core_meaning_summary: Physical violence, destructive aggression, or grave social and legal wrongdoing inflicted unjustly upon others.

senses.definition: Physical aggression, bloodshed, or destructive force committed against people, cities, or lands, including warfare and murder; used in construct with either the perpetrator or the victim, and as an urgent cry for help against attack.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; subject, object of verbs of filling or coming, governed by min ('from') or lə ('for'), construct with victim (objective) or agent (subjective), or exclamatory cry; paired with šōḏ ('devastation') or kəlê ('weapons').

senses.definition: Unjust, oppressive, or deceitful conduct in social, economic, or judicial spheres, including extortion, ill-gotten gain, and wrongful acts contrasted with righteousness and innocence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural ḥămāsîm); object of verbs of doing, loving, concealing, or removing; governed by bəlōʾ/lōʾ ('without/no') in idioms with kap ('hand'); paired with mirmāh ('deceit'), šeqer ('falsehood'), or contrasted with mišpāṭ ('justice') and ṣəḏāqāh ('righteousness').

senses.definition: Cruel, unscrupulous, or malicious character when used as an attributive modifier in construct after nouns denoting a person, witness, or hostile attitude.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural ḥămāsîm) in construct after a head noun (e.g., ʾîš 'man', ʿēḏ 'witness', śinʾāh 'hatred', or participle yîp̄ēaḥ 'breathing out').

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs as the object of mālēʾ ('be full of', GEN 6:11, GEN 6:13, EZK 8:17, MIC 6:12) and in the paired expression ḥāmās wāšōḏ ('violence and devastation/plunder', JER 6:7, JER 20:8, EZK 45:9; cf. HAB 2:17). Idioms for innocence or guilt include lōʾ ḥāmās bəḵappay ('no wrong/violence in my hands', 1CH 12:18, JOB 16:17; cf. ISA 59:6). In construct phrases, it takes either an objective genitive naming the victim (JDG 9:24, JOL 4:19, OBA 1:10, HAB 2:17) or a subjective/attributive genitive (EZK 12:19; ʾîš ḥāmās / ḥămāsîm 'violent/unscrupulous person', PSA 140:5, PSA 140:12, PRO 16:29; ʿēḏ ḥāmās 'malicious witness', EXO 23:1). Note the plural form ḥămāsîm in PSA 140:5 and PRO 4:17 denoting repeated or intense acts of violence. Can also function as a direct exclamation/cry for rescue (HAB 1:2, JER 20:8).

core_meaning_summary: A solemn promise or conditional pledge made to a deity, and by extension the sacrificial offering or payment owed to fulfill that pledge.

senses.definition: A solemn verbal promise or conditional commitment made to God (or another deity, JER 44:25), binding the speaker to an action, dedication, or devotion once made or confirmed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; cognate object of nāḏar ('to vow'), object of verbs of hearing, performing (ʿāśāh), fulfilling (šillēm), confirming (hēqîm), or annulling (hēp̄ēr); often followed by lə ('to' a deity) and direct speech introduced by lēʾmōr.

senses.definition: The concrete sacrificial animal, gift, or sanctuary meal brought and offered in discharge of a vow, regularly distinguished from or paired with freewill offerings (nəḏāḇāh).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural); object of verbs of bringing (hēḇîʾ), eating (ʾāḵal), offering/fulfilling (pillēʾ, šillēm), or governed by lə ('for'); listed alongside burnt offerings, peace offerings, tithes, and freewill offerings (nəḏāḇāh).

collocations_and_notes: Regularly appears as the cognate object of the verb nāḏar ('to vow', e.g., GEN 28:20, NUM 6:2, NUM 21:2, DEU 23:22, 1SA 1:11, 2SA 15:8, ECC 5:3, JON 1:16). Fulfilling a vow is expressed primarily with šillēm in the intensive stem (Piel: 'pay, fulfill', e.g., DEU 23:22, 2SA 15:7, PSA 22:26, PSA 50:14, PSA 66:13, PRO 7:14, ECC 5:3, ISA 19:21) or pillēʾ in the intensive stem (Piel: 'fulfill/perform a vow', LEV 22:21, NUM 15:3; cf. hiphil hiplîʾ 'make a special vow', LEV 27:2, NUM 6:2). In NUM 30, paired with ʾissār ('binding obligation/pledge') and subject to hēqîm ('confirm/establish') or hēp̄ēr ('annul'). In cultic law, frequently paired with nəḏāḇāh ('freewill offering', LEV 7:16, LEV 22:21, LEV 22:23, NUM 15:3, NUM 29:39, DEU 12:6, DEU 12:17). While most contexts address vows to YHWH, JER 44:25 applies the term to vows directed to another deity.

core_meaning_summary: The left side, direction, or hand, as well as figurative deviation when paired with the right.

senses.definition: The left-hand side or direction relative to a person, object, or path, including geographical orientation toward the north when facing east.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (used with prepositions מִן, עַל, אֶל, or adverbially with verbs of turning and motion, often paired with יָמִין)

senses.definition: The left hand or left arm of a person (often personified).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine/masculine noun with pronominal suffix, or genitive after יַד (יַד שְׂמֹאל)

senses.definition: Moral or behavioral deviation (in the merism "right or left" with verbs of turning aside from instruction or command) or the unfavorable inclination contrasted with wisdom.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial noun paired with יָמִין after verbs of turning aside (סור, נטה), or with prepositional לְ contrasted with יָמִין

collocations_and_notes: Almost always paired or contrasted with יָמִין ("right"). Frequently occurs in the merism יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל ("right and left") to express comprehensive extent or strict adherence without deviation. Appears in construct with יַד ("hand") in יַד שְׂמֹאלוֹ / יַד שְׂמֹאולֶךָ ("his/your left hand"). In east-facing geographical descriptions (GEN 14:15, JOS 19:27, EZK 16:46), the left side corresponds to the north. Both plene (שְׂמֹאול) and defective (שְׂמֹאל) spellings occur.

core_meaning_summary: A physical shadow or shade cast by an object blocking sunlight, used figuratively both for protective shelter/refuge and for fleeting, transitory existence.

senses.definition: An area of darkness or relief from sunlight and heat cast by a tree, rock, cloud, mountain, structure, or sundial steps, including lengthening evening shadows.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular צֵל, plural צְלָלִים, construct צֵל / צִלְלֵי); used as subject, direct object, or in prepositional phrases (בְּצֵל, לְצֵל) often contrasted with חֹרֶב ('heat').

senses.definition: Protective shelter, refuge, or patronage (extended by God, a roof, a city, a ruler, wisdom, or wealth), often portrayed through imagery of wings, hands, or spreading tree branches.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase בְּצֵל + genitive/pronoun (often with verbs of dwelling, hiding, or taking refuge such as חָסָה, יָשַׁב, שָׁכַן, סָתַר, כִּסָּה) or predicate/subject noun (NUM 14:9; PSA 121:5).

senses.definition: An emblem of brevity, transience, and fleeting human existence, likened to a shadow that stretches out, passes by, or flees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate noun (צֵל יָמֵינוּ) or object of comparison introduced by כְּ־ (כַּצֵּל, כְּצֵל עוֹבֵר) with verbs of motion or duration (בָּרַח, הָלַךְ, עָבַר, הֶאֱרִיךְ).

collocations_and_notes: Exhibits geminate inflection with singular suffixed forms צִלִּי, צִלּוֹ, צִלָּהּ, צִלָּם, צִלְךָ (and צִלֲלוֹ in JOB 40:22) and plural forms צְלָלִים / צִלְלֵי. Common idioms include בְּצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ ('in the shadow of your wings', PSA 17:8; 36:8; 63:8), חָסָה בְצֵל ('take refuge in the shadow of', JDG 9:15; ISA 30:2), and יָשַׁב בְּצֵל ('dwell in the shadow of', EZK 31:6; HOS 14:8; JON 4:5). In 2KI 20:10–11 and ISA 38:8, הַצֵּל denotes the cast shadow moving across the steps of Ahaz. EZK 17:23 and 31:6, 12 blend literal tree shade with political shelter under an imperial power.

senses.definition: Untruth, deceit, or fabricated claims in testimony, rumor, speech, or prophetic/divinatory visions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used as direct object of verbs of speaking, hearing, or seeing/prophesying, or as second noun in construct chains (e.g., עֵד שָׁוְא, שֵׁמַע שָׁוְא, מַחֲזֵה שָׁוְא)
senses.semantic_domain: Truth and Falsehood / Speech and Prophecy

senses.definition: Lack of substance, reality, value, or worth, describing vain idols, insincere offerings, futile deliverance, or empty existence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used as predicate, object of verbs of trusting or looking, or as second noun in construct chains (e.g., הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא, מִנְחַת שָׁוְא)

senses.definition: Without effect, to no purpose, or for an empty and improper end, including the empty or false invocation of God's name and fruitless human or disciplinary effort.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial prepositional phrase לַשָּׁוְא or predicative/interrogative שָׁוְא / עַל מַה שָּׁוְא modifying a clause

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the prepositional phrase לַשָּׁוְא ("in vain / for falsehood / to an empty end"), especially with נָשָׂא ("lift up [the name/soul]"). Regularly paired or paralleled with כָּזָב ("lie"), שֶׁקֶר ("falsehood"), מִרְמָה ("deceit"), אָוֶן ("iniquity/emptiness"), הֶבֶל ("vapor/vanity"), and תָּפֵל ("insipid/unsubstantial"). Common construct expressions include מְתֵי שָׁוְא ("false/worthless men"), הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא ("worthless idols/vanities"), עֵד שָׁוְא ("false witness"), and מַחֲזֵה שָׁוְא ("false vision"). Orthographic variants in the sample include בַּשָּׁיו (JOB 15:31) and הַשָּׁוא (ZEC 10:2).

core_meaning_summary: A dove or pigeon (used literally, sacrificially, and figuratively as an emblem of beauty, affection, or mourning), and also the masculine proper name of the prophet Jonah.

senses.definition: A dove or pigeon, noted for flying, nesting in rock clefts or chasms, cooing or moaning, and offered (especially as young birds, בֶּן/בְּנֵי יוֹנָה) in temple sacrifices.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular יוֹנָה, plural יוֹנִים, construct plural יוֹנֵי); often in construct chain בֶּן־יוֹנָה / בְּנֵי (הַ)יּוֹנָה as object of sacrificial verbs (הֵבִיא, הִקְרִיב, לָקַח, עָשָׂה) or following comparative כְּ־.

senses.definition: A figurative or poetic designation derived from the bird: a term of endearment for a beloved woman, a comparison for beautiful eyes, or an element in a psalm superscription.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun with 1cs suffix (יוֹנָתִי) as vocative, plural predicate (עֵינַיִךְ יוֹנִים), or singular construct (יוֹנַת) after preposition עַל in a superscription.

senses.definition: Jonah, an Israelite prophet (identified in 2KI 14:25 as son of Amittai from Gath-hepher) and the protagonist of the Book of Jonah.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine proper noun used as subject, direct object (with אֶת), or object of prepositions (עַל, אֶל, לְ־).

collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in sacrificial law in the construct plural/singular phrases בְּנֵי (הַ)יּוֹנָה and בֶן יוֹנָה ('young of a dove') paired as an alternative with תֹּרִים ('turtledoves'). In poetry and prophecy, serves as a standard comparison for moaning/cooing (הגה, המה), trembling flight, or naivety (פּוֹתָה אֵין לֵב in HOS 7:11). In Song of Songs, יוֹנָתִי is paired with רַעְיָתִי and תַמָּתִי as an affectionate address. The construct יוֹנַת in PSA 56:1 appears in the superscription עַל יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחֹקִים, whose precise liturgical or musical reference cannot be determined from the text alone. As a masculine proper name (2KI 14:25; Book of Jonah), it identifies the prophet Jonah son of Amittai.

verses.GEN 8:10: וַ יָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַ יֹּ֛סֶף שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת הַ 【יּוֹנָ֖ה】 מִן הַ תֵּבָֽה
verses.GEN 8:11: וַ תָּבֹ֨א אֵלָ֤י ו הַ 【יּוֹנָה֙】 לְ עֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב וְ הִנֵּ֥ה עֲלֵה זַ֖יִת טָרָ֣ף בְּ פִ֑י הָ וַ יֵּ֣דַע נֹ֔חַ כִּי קַ֥לּוּ הַ מַּ֖יִם מֵ עַ֥ל הָ אָֽרֶץ
verses.LEV 1:14: וְ אִ֧ם מִן הָ ע֛וֹף עֹלָ֥ה קָרְבָּנ֖ וֹ לַֽ יהוָ֑ה וְ הִקְרִ֣יב מִן הַ תֹּרִ֗ים א֛וֹ מִן בְּנֵ֥י הַ 【יּוֹנָ֖ה】 אֶת קָרְבָּנֽ וֹ
verses.LEV 5:7: וְ אִם לֹ֨א תַגִּ֣יע יָד וֹ֮ דֵּ֣י שֶׂה֒ וְ הֵבִ֨יא אֶת אֲשָׁמ֜ וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֗א שְׁתֵּ֥י תֹרִ֛ים אֽוֹ שְׁנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי 【יוֹנָ֖ה】 לַֽ יהוָ֑ה אֶחָ֥ד לְ חַטָּ֖את וְ אֶחָ֥ד לְ עֹלָֽה
verses.LEV 5:11: וְ אִם לֹא֩ תַשִּׂ֨יג יָד֜ וֹ לִ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֗ים אוֹ֮ לִ שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵי 【יוֹנָה֒】 וְ הֵבִ֨יא אֶת קָרְבָּנ֜ וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֗א עֲשִׂירִ֧ת הָ אֵפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת לְ חַטָּ֑את לֹא יָשִׂ֨ים עָלֶ֜י הָ שֶׁ֗מֶן וְ לֹא יִתֵּ֤ן עָלֶ֨י הָ֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּ֥י חַטָּ֖את הִֽיא
verses.LEV 12:6: וּ בִ מְלֹ֣את יְמֵ֣י טָהֳרָ֗ הּ לְ בֵן֮ א֣וֹ לְ בַת֒ תָּבִ֞יא כֶּ֤בֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָת וֹ֙ לְ עֹלָ֔ה וּ בֶן 【יוֹנָ֥ה】 אוֹ תֹ֖ר לְ חַטָּ֑את אֶל פֶּ֥תַח אֹֽהֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶל הַ כֹּהֵֽן
verses.LEV 14:22: וּ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֗ים א֤וֹ שְׁנֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י 【יוֹנָ֔ה】 אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּשִּׂ֖יג יָד֑ וֹ וְ הָיָ֤ה אֶחָד֙ חַטָּ֔את וְ הָ אֶחָ֖ד עֹלָֽה
verses.LEV 14:30: וְ עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הָֽ אֶחָד֙ מִן הַ תֹּרִ֔ים א֖וֹ מִן בְּנֵ֣י הַ 【יּוֹנָ֑ה】 מֵ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּשִּׂ֖יג יָדֽ וֹ
