core_meaning_summary: To exert strenuous effort, labor, or toil at productive tasks, livelihood, or arduous investigation.

senses.definition: To work hard, labor, or exert strenuous effort in building, tending, earning sustenance, or pursuing human undertakings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); intransitive, with בְּ ('at/on'), לְ ('for'), or infinitive לַעֲשׂוֹת ('to accomplish'), often with cognate noun עָמָל

senses.definition: To strive strenuously or exert mental effort in attempting to investigate and discover something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); followed by purpose infinitive לְבַקֵּשׁ ('to seek')

collocations_and_notes: All 11 occurrences in this packet are in the simple active stem (Qal). Heavily concentrated in Ecclesiastes, where it characteristically appears in a cognate construction with the noun עָמָל ('toil that one toils') and the phrase תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ ('under the sun', ECC 1:3; 2:19; 2:20; 5:17). Also collocates with בְּ marking the object worked on (PSA 127:1; ECC 2:21; JON 4:10) and with לְ marking beneficiary or goal (PRO 16:26; ECC 5:15).

core_meaning_summary: As a verb, to vomit up or figuratively spew out inhabitants; as a noun, vomit or regurgitated matter.

senses.definition: To eject food, a swallowed person, or (figuratively) swallowed wealth from the stomach through the mouth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative-type verb stem (Hiphil); transitive with direct object (pronominal suffix or אֶת + noun)

senses.definition: Used figuratively of the land expelling or spewing out its inhabitants because of defilement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal, LEV 18:28) and causative-type stem (Hiphil); transitive with הָאָרֶץ ('the land') as subject and אֶת + inhabitants as object

senses.definition: Matter ejected from the stomach; vomit associated with drunkenness and defilement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; after מָלֵא ('be full of') or governed by preposition בְּ ('in') with pronominal suffix

collocations_and_notes: This packet groups both verbal and nominal forms under this lemma. Verbally, it occurs chiefly in the causative-type stem (Hiphil) as a transitive verb taking a direct object (marked by אֶת or a pronominal suffix), and once in the simple active stem (Qal, קָאָה in LEV 18:28) with the exact same transitive syntax and meaning as the adjacent causative-type form (תָקִיא). Nominally, קִיא denotes vomit, associated with drunkenness and filth (ISA 19:14; ISA 28:8; JER 48:26).

core_meaning_summary: The numeral ten thousand, or in the dual/plural an indefinitely vast multitude (myriads).

senses.definition: The exact numerical unit of ten thousand (10,000), used either alone or multiplied by a preceding numeral when counting people, coins, or metal weights.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine numeral (singular or plural), standalone or following a multiplier (2, 4, 6, 12) in apposition to counted nouns

senses.definition: An indefinitely huge number or vast multitude of troops, chariots, or people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Dual (רִבֹּתַיִם) or plural (רִבֹּאוֹת) noun without a preceding multiplier, in poetic parallelism or as a direct object

collocations_and_notes: Exhibits varied orthography across the corpus: singular `רִבּוֹ` / `רִבּוֹא`, plural `רִבּוֹת` / `רִבֹּאוֹת`, and dual `רִבֹּתַיִם`. In `1CH 29:7` it appears both for a standalone 10,000 and combined with `וּשְׁמוֹנַת אֲלָפִים` ("and eight thousand", i.e., 18,000). In `EZR 2:64` and `NEH 7:66`, `אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא` totals 40,000 within 42,360. In `NEH 7:70-71` both plural `שְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹת` and singular `שְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹא` denote 20,000.

core_meaning_summary: To dig, bore, or break through a barrier or surface, or to row vigorously through water.

senses.definition: To dig, bore, or break through a wall, house, or into the underworld so as to create an opening or gain entry or exit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb taking a direct object (houses) or prepositional phrase with בְּ- (in a wall, into Sheol), optionally with לְ- (for oneself) or בְּיָד (by hand)

senses.definition: To row vigorously with oars (literally digging into the water) in an effort to bring a vessel back to shore.
glosses: to pull hard at the oars
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb used intransitively with an infinitive of purpose (לְהָשִׁיב, to bring back) in a nautical context

collocations_and_notes: Occurs exclusively in the basic active (Qal) stem. Commonly takes `בַּקִּיר` ("in/through the wall") as a prepositional complement (`EZK 8:8`, `EZK 12:5`, `EZK 12:7`, `EZK 12:12`), sometimes with reflexive `לְ-` ("for oneself") or instrument `בְּיָד` ("by hand"). In `JOB 24:16` it takes a direct object (`בָּתִּים`, "houses"), and in `AMO 9:2` it takes `בִשְׁאוֹל` ("into Sheol") as a hyperbole for extreme subterranean hiding. In `JON 1:13` it describes sailors rowing against a raging sea.

core_meaning_summary: A violent windstorm or tempest, also used figuratively for overwhelming divine wrath or disaster.

senses.definition: A fierce storm or tempest of wind, especially a violent gale threatening ships at sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often with the adjective גָּדוֹל (great) or parallel to רוּחַ (wind)

senses.definition: A figurative storm representing overwhelming divine judgment, anger, or military devastation sweeping down upon enemies or the wicked.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often with preposition בְּ- (with/in) or modified by participles (מִתְחוֹלֵל, מִתְגּוֹרֵר) and paired with חֵמָה (wrath) or סוּפָה (whirlwind)

collocations_and_notes: Often modified by `גָּדוֹל` ("great") in narrative and prophecy (`JER 25:32`, `JON 1:4`, `JON 1:12`) or by reflexive/whirling participles `מִתְחוֹלֵל` (`JER 23:19`) and `מִתְגּוֹרֵר` (`JER 30:23`). Frequently paired in poetic parallelism with `רוּחַ` ("wind"), `סוּפָה` ("whirlwind/tempest"), `חֵמָה` ("wrath"), and `סַעֲרַת יְהוָה` ("tempest of YHWH").

core_meaning_summary: To rage or surge like a storm (of the sea or attackers), to be inwardly agitated or storm-tossed, and in intensive stems to whirl away or scatter violently as by a tempest.

senses.definition: To surge violently, rage, or grow tempestuous (said of the sea).
senses.grammatical_frame: Base stem (Qal) active participle following hōlēk ("going/increasing"), with "the sea" as subject and optional preposition ʿal ("against")

senses.definition: To rush forward furiously or charge like a storm against an adversary.
senses.grammatical_frame: Base stem (Qal) finite verb with plural subject and infinitive of purpose ("to scatter")

senses.definition: To be storm-tossed, battered, or thrown into turmoil (used substantively/attributively of an afflicted, uncomforted city).
senses.grammatical_frame: Base stem (Qal) feminine singular active participle used as a vocative descriptor

senses.definition: To become deeply agitated, disturbed, or enraged in one's mind or heart over an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) finite verb with lēb ("heart/mind") as subject and preposition ʿal ("over")

senses.definition: To be whirled or blown away like chaff from a threshing floor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive stem (Poel) finite verb used intransitively/passively with "chaff" as subject and preposition min ("from")

senses.definition: To sweep away or scatter people violently across foreign lands as by a storm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive transitive stem (Piel/Poel) finite verb with direct object suffix and preposition ʿal ("among/upon")

collocations_and_notes: Observed across three stems: the base active stem (Qal) describes the sea growing tempestuous (paired with hōlēk "going/increasing" in JON 1:11, JON 1:13), an army rushing storm-like into attack (HAB 3:14), and a personified city tossed in turmoil (ISA 54:11, parallel to "afflicted" and "uncomforted"). The passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) in 2KI 6:11 takes lēb ("heart/mind") as subject to denote inner agitation or distress. Two intensive-stem forms appear with long vowels: in HOS 13:3 yəsōʿēr describes chaff whirled from a threshing floor (parallel to smoke from an opening), and in ZEC 7:14 ʾēsāʿărēm takes a direct object suffix with ʿal ("upon/among") to denote God sweeping people away in storm-like scattering across the nations.

core_meaning_summary: To fall into or be in a state of deep sleep, unconsciousness, or overwhelming stupor (attested solely in the passive/reflexive stem).

senses.definition: To fall fast asleep or remain in heavy slumber, especially when vigilance or labor is expected.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) finite verb or participle, intransitive (with optional temporal preposition bə- "during")

senses.definition: To sink into a deep stupor, unconsciousness, or visionary swoon, whether from overwhelming awe, divine rebuke, or lethal exhaustion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) finite verb or participle (including periphrastic hāyîtî + participle), often with spatial phrase ("upon my face to the ground") or causal preposition min ("at/because of")
senses.semantic_domain: Physiology and Perception / Stupor and Trance

collocations_and_notes: All seven occurrences appear exclusively in the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal). In ordinary sleep contexts it follows šākab ("lie down", JON 1:5), stands in contrast to gathering crops in summer (PRO 10:5), or is addressed with mah ləkā ("what is with you?", JON 1:6). In extraordinary/crisis contexts it combines with ʿal pānay ("upon my face [to the ground]") during an overwhelming vision (DAN 8:18, DAN 10:9, once periphrastically with hāyîtî "I was"), follows miggaʿărātəkā ("at your rebuke") for stunned chariotry (PSA 76:7), or appears alongside yāʿap̄ ("faint/exhausted") and mût ("die") when Sisera is struck down while sleeping/unconscious (JDG 4:21).

core_meaning_summary: Fierce, surging anger or wrath of humans or God, and by extension the violent raging of a stormy sea.

senses.definition: Intense anger, fury, or indignation felt by a human ruler, warriors, or God, often manifested in harsh punishment, slaughter, or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun; governed by preposition bə- ("in/with"), or as subject/object in construct phrases (with king, YHWH, or ʾap̄ "anger")

senses.definition: Violent turbulence, storminess, or raging motion of the sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with possessive suffix referring to the sea, governed by preposition min ("from") after verb of ceasing

collocations_and_notes: Frequently governed by the preposition bə- ("in, with") to express the manner or emotional state accompanying violent or punitive action (2CH 16:10, 2CH 28:9, ISA 30:30). Construct phrases include zaʿap̄ ʾap̄ ("furious rage of anger", ISA 30:30) and zaʿap̄ YHWH ("wrath of YHWH", MIC 7:9). In PRO 19:12 it is likened to a young lion's growl and contrasted with rāṣôn ("favor, goodwill"). In JON 1:15 it governs the preposition min ("from") after ʿāmad ("stand still") to describe the subsiding of a storm at sea.

core_meaning_summary: Coercive physical force or harshness, intense vehemence in speech or outcry, and structural repair or reinforcement of a building.

senses.definition: Great intensity, sharpness, or earnestness in verbal contention or desperate outcry.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by preposition bə- ("with"), functioning adverbially with verbs of quarreling or calling out

senses.definition: Physical repair, reinforcement, or structural maintenance of a building.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by preposition lə- ("for"), expressing purpose regarding a building

collocations_and_notes: Five of the six occurrences appear in the adverbial prepositional phrase bəḥozqâ ("by force / harshly / vehemently / earnestly"), modifying verbs of oppression, quarreling, seizing, ruling, or crying out. In 2KI 12:13 it takes the preposition lə- ("for") in parallel with the verb phrase ləḥazzēq ʾet bedeq ("to repair the breach of"), denoting structural repair/upkeep of the temple.

core_meaning_summary: To surround, encompass, or close in upon someone, especially used of threatening waters or overwhelming peril.

senses.definition: In the basic active (Qal) stem, of deep waters: to engulf or close in around a person on all sides.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb with direct object suffix (person)

senses.definition: In the basic active (Qal) stem, figuratively of mortal perils, deathly breakers or cords, or innumerable calamities (רָעוֹת): to encompass, beset, or close in upon a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb with direct object suffix or with עַל + object

collocations_and_notes: All occurrences appear in the basic active (Qal) stem in 3rd-person plural suffix conjugation (qatal) forms. Commonly takes an accusative pronominal suffix on the verb (2SA 22:5; PSA 18:5; PSA 116:3; JON 2:6), or the preposition עַל (PSA 40:13). Parallel verbs in context include סבב ('to surround', JON 2:6), בעת ('to terrify', 2SA 22:5; PSA 18:5), מצא ('to come upon/find', PSA 116:3), and נשׂג ('to overtake', PSA 40:13).

core_meaning_summary: A skilled mariner, ship's pilot, or seafarer; in the compound title רַב הַחֹבֵל, the ship's captain.

senses.definition: A skilled seafarer or ship's pilot/navigator responsible for steering or managing a vessel, contrasted with rowers (EZK 27:8) and grouped with sailors and oar-handlers (EZK 27:27, 27:29).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural (with suffixal forms or construct חֹבְלֵי הַיָּם)

senses.definition: In the construct title רַב הַחֹבֵל ('chief of the seafarer[s]/crew'), collective or generic singular designating the ship's crew or pilots under a captain's authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular determined, governed in construct by רַב (רַב הַחֹבֵל, 'captain')

collocations_and_notes: In EZK 27:8, Tyre's חֲכָמִים ('wise/skilled men') are identified as her חֹבְלִים, contrasted with the inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad who serve as rowers (שָׁטִים). In EZK 27:27 and 27:29, it stands alongside מַלָּחִים ('sailors') and תֹּפְשֵׂי מָשׁוֹט ('oar-handlers'). In JON 1:6, the singular form appears in the construct phrase רַב הַחֹבֵל ('chief of the seafarers/pilots'), denoting the ship's commanding officer.
uncertainty_note: While EZK 27:8 contrasts חֹבְלִים (identified with skilled/wise men) against rowers (שָׁטִים), EZK 27:27 and 27:29 pair חֹבְלִים closely with מַלָּחִים ('sailors'), leaving it somewhat uncertain whether חֹבֵל always denotes a specialized pilot/helmsman or can also function more broadly as a term for seafarer/crewman.

senses.definition: Figuratively, overwhelming surges of mortal danger, sorrow, or divine anger that engulf or afflict a person.

collocations_and_notes: Attested only in the plural (construct `מִשְׁבְּרֵי` in 2SA 22:5 and PSA 93:4; with 2ms suffix `מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ` in PSA 42:8, PSA 88:8, and JON 2:4). Frequently paired with `גַּלֶּיךָ` ("your waves") in the identical formula `כָּל־מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ וְגַלֶּיךָ עָלַי עָבָרוּ` (PSA 42:8; JON 2:4). Paralleled with `נַחֲלֵי בְלִיַּעַל` ("torrents of ruin") in 2SA 22:5 and `מַיִם רַבִּים` ("many waters") in PSA 93:4.

core_meaning_summary: A journey, walking distance, physical walkway/passage, or freedom of movement/access among others.

senses.definition: The act, duration, or spatial distance of a journey or walk on foot, including the span of an expedition or a city's extent measured in days of walking.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun; subject of הָיָה with עַד־מָתַי ('how long will your journey be') or in construct with a time span ('a walk of X days')

senses.definition: A paved walkway, corridor, or open passage alongside building chambers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun in architectural description followed by dimensional measurement (אֶת/עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת רֹחַב)

senses.definition: Right of access, free passage, or ability to walk and move about among a group of attendants.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun as direct object of נָתַן ('give') + לְ + בֵּין ('between/among')

collocations_and_notes: In construct with time expressions (`מַהֲלַךְ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים` in JON 3:3; `מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם אֶחָד` in JON 3:4) to indicate spatial distance measured by walking duration. In EZK 42:4 juxtaposed with `דֶּרֶךְ` ("way/path"). In ZEC 3:7 appears in the plural `מַהְלְכִים` governed by `נָתַתִּי לְךָ ... בֵּין הָעֹמְדִים הָאֵלֶּה`.
uncertainty_note: The exact nuance of the plural מַהְלְכִים in ZEC 3:7 is somewhat uncertain from context alone: it most likely denotes abstract free access or goings among the standing figures, though a concrete sense of 'walking companions/attendants' cannot be entirely ruled out.

core_meaning_summary: To cover, overlay, or wrap up; and to faint, swoon, or collapse from exhaustion, heat, thirst, or affliction.

senses.definition: To be overlaid, covered, or encrusted with decorative gemstones.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive of the intensive stem (participle) + noun of material (סַפִּירִים)

senses.definition: To wrap or shroud oneself in garments or a veil so as to conceal one's appearance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reflexive-intensive stem (Hithpael), intransitive, paired with כָּסָה ('cover') + בַּצָּעִיף ('with a veil')

senses.definition: To faint, grow weak, or collapse physically from severe thirst, intense heat, or overwhelming distress.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive of the intensive stem (ISA 51:20) or reflexive-intensive stem (AMO 8:13, JON 4:8); intransitive, optionally with בְּ marking the cause (e.g., בַּצָּמָא 'from thirst')

collocations_and_notes: Occurs in the passive of the intensive stem (Pual: SNG 5:14, ISA 51:20) and in the reflexive-intensive stem (Hithpael: GEN 38:14, AMO 8:13, JON 4:8). In GEN 38:14 it immediately follows `וַתְּכַס בַּצָּעִיף` ("and she covered herself with the veil"). Causes of fainting/collapse include thirst (`בַּצָּמָא`, AMO 8:13), intense sun/heat (`וַתַּךְ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ עַל־רֹאשׁ יוֹנָה`, JON 4:8), and divine wrath (`מְלֵאִים חֲמַת יְהוָה`, ISA 51:20).

core_meaning_summary: A fast-growing, shade-producing plant that sprouts rapidly and withers quickly when attacked by a worm.

senses.definition: A rapidly growing plant tall or broad enough to cast shade over a person's head, vulnerable to being attacked by a worm and quickly withering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; object of מָנָה ('appoint'), נָכָה ('strike'), and חוּס עַל ('have pity on'), and subject of עָלָה ('grow up'), יָבֵשׁ ('wither'), and אָבַד ('perish')

collocations_and_notes: Appears only in the narrative of JON 4:6–10 (twice in JON 4:6: once indefinite, once with the definite article). Associated verbs and phrases: `וַיַּעַל מֵעַל לְיוֹנָה לִהְיוֹת צֵל עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ` ("it grew up over Jonah to be shade over his head"), `וַתַּךְ ... וַיִּיבָשׁ` ("struck ... and it withered"), `לֹא עָמַלְתָּ בּוֹ וְלֹא גִדַּלְתּוֹ` ("you did not labor over it nor make it grow"), and `שֶׁבִּן־לַיְלָה הָיָה וּבִן־לַיְלָה אָבָד` ("which came up in a night and perished in a night").
uncertainty_note: All occurrences appear within the single episode of Jonah 4:6–10. While the context clearly establishes that it is a fast-growing, shade-giving, perishable plant, the exact botanical species is not specified in the primary text.

core_meaning_summary: Proper name of a coastal port city (Joppa) on the sea, serving as a harbor for maritime travel and timber transport toward Jerusalem as well as a geographic border landmark.

senses.definition: A coastal city and maritime port used for embarking on sea voyages and receiving sea-borne cargo such as timber from Lebanon destined for Jerusalem, and cited as a landmark opposite a tribal border.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun: object of the preposition מוּל ("opposite"), nomen rectum after יָם ("sea of"), or directional complement after יָרַד ("go down to")

collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the construct chain יָם יָפוֹ / יָם יָפוֹא ("the sea of Joppa") as the coastal landing point for cedar timber floated from Lebanon on the way up to Jerusalem (2CH 2:15; EZR 3:7). Spelled with a final aleph (יָפוֹא) in EZR 3:7 and without it (יָפוֹ) in the other three passages.

core_meaning_summary: A sailor or mariner who crews and works aboard a seagoing ship.

senses.definition: A person who works aboard a ship on the sea; a sailor or seafarer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural (attested in absolute, determined, and suffixal forms)

collocations_and_notes: Attested exclusively in the masculine plural (absolute, definite, and with pronominal suffixes referring to ships or Tyre). core_meaning_summary: A noun denoting either the uniform form, shape, or cut of crafted objects alongside their dimensions, or (in the plural) the lowest extremities or bases of mountains.

senses.definition: The uniform shape, form, or standardized proportion shared by matching crafted items, paired directly with measurement (מִדָּה).
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun modified by אֶחָד ("one") in apposition/coordination with מִדָּה אַחַת ("one measure") and followed by לְ ("for")

senses.definition: The lowest parts, bases, or extreme limits of mountains reached when descending into the subterranean depths.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct plural noun (קִצְבֵי) governed by the directional preposition לְ ("to") before הָרִים ("mountains") with a verb of downward motion (יָרַדְתִּי)

collocations_and_notes: In both 1KI 6:25 and 1KI 7:37, קֶצֶב occurs in the fixed phrase מִדָּה אַחַת (וְ)קֶצֶב אֶחָד לְ... ("one measure [and] one shape/form for..."), describing paired or serial crafted temple furnishings. In JON 2:7, it appears in the construct plural לְקִצְבֵי הָרִים ("to the bases/extremities of mountains") as the goal of יָרַדְתִּי ("I went down").
uncertainty_note: While the craftsmanship sense alongside מִדָּה is well supported by 1KI 6:25 and 1KI 7:37, the exact distinction between קֶצֶב and מִדָּה ("measure") is not fully specified by those formulas. The poetic plural קִצְבֵי הָרִים appears only in JON 2:7, so whether it refers specifically to mountain bases/roots or more generally to subterranean boundaries/extremities rests on a single context.

core_meaning_summary: A verb attested in two distinct stems with separate contextual meanings: in the Qal, growing sleek or plump alongside becoming fat; in the Hithpael, giving thought or showing favorable regard toward someone in danger.

senses.definition: To become sleek, smooth, or plump in physical condition, paired directly with growing fat in a description of prosperous wrongdoers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal suffix-conjugation (perfect), 3rd person plural, intransitive, paired asyndetically with שָׁמְנוּ

senses.definition: To give thought to, turn attention toward, or take account of someone so as to spare or help them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael prefix-conjugation (imperfect), 3rd person masculine singular, with divine subject and prepositional complement לָנוּ ("to/for us")

collocations_and_notes: In JER 5:28, the Qal plural עָשְׁתוּ is placed asyndetically right after שָׁמְנוּ ("they grew fat"), forming a pair describing physical thriving among those who neglect justice. In JON 1:6, the Hithpael יִתְעַשֵּׁת takes הָאֱלֹהִים as subject and is followed by the prepositional phrase לָנוּ ("for/to us") and a result clause ("so that we do not perish"). No shared collocations link the two stems in these verses.
uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice in the corpus, once in the Qal (JER 5:28) and once in the Hithpael (JON 1:6), with no overlapping context. In JER 5:28, whether the Qal verb specifically denotes physical sleekness/glossiness, stoutness, or general prosperity cannot be narrowed further from its sole pairing with שָׁמְנוּ. In JON 1:6, whether the Hithpael denotes mental reflection, compassionate regard, or active intervention remains slightly open, as does any semantic relationship between the two stems.
